title: Baseline retest for cores/bench
Multi-cycle stalling MDU: move 32-bit DIV/REM and MUL out of the single-cycle EX path
motivation:
The baseline closes timing at only 5.44 MHz (worst path 199.8 ns, 156 logic cells, 150 logic
levels: MEM/WB rd -> forward_unit -> ex_stage operand mux -> alu -> EX/MEM / dmem address).
That path runs through the combinational `/` and `%` operators in alu.sv, which synthesize to
a fully unrolled 32-step restoring divider (x4 variants: signed/unsigned DIV and REM). The
three separate 33x33 `*` products in the same ALU are the next-longest cone. Fitness is
iter/cycle x Fmax, and CoreMark executes very few divides and only ~1-3K multiplies per
~449K-cycle iteration (CoreMark/MHz = 2.23), so spending 2-35 stall cycles per M-op costs
at most ~1-2% of iterations/cycle, while removing the divider from the critical path should
raise Fmax several-fold (the remaining critical path becomes forward mux -> 32-bit add /
branch compare, on the order of 15-25 ns).

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a small multi-cycle M-extension unit (new rtl/mdu.sv) that the EX stage stalls on, and
remove the combinational multiply/divide cones from the single-cycle ALU in synthesized
(non-ALTOPS) builds.

mdu.sv (clock, reset, start, op[4:0], a, b -> done, result):
  * IDLE: when `start` (EX holds a valid M-op, !stall_ex_mem) capture raw forwarded operands
    a_r/b_r and op_r (this is essential: the forward muxes are dynamic and the producer
    leaves EX/MEM and MEM/WB while the M-op sits in EX, so the MDU must not re-read rs1/rs2
    after the first cycle).
  * MUL/MULH/MULHSU/MULHU: ONE shared 33x33 signed multiplier on sign-extended operands
    (a_ext = {a_signed & a[31], a}, b_ext = {b_signed & b[31], b}; a_signed for MULH/MULHSU,
    b_signed for MULH). One RUN cycle registers the selected half (prod[31:0] for MUL, else
    prod[63:32]) into res_r; then DONE. EX occupancy 3 cycles. This also collapses the three
    baseline multipliers into one (less area, less fanout from alu_a/alu_b).
  * DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU: radix-2 restoring divider on |a|/|b| (one load cycle computing abs
    values and sign bits, 32 iterate cycles with a 33-bit subtract/compare, one fix-up cycle
    applying result negation) -> res_r, then DONE. ~36 cycles. Special cases per RV32M:
    b==0 -> DIV/DIVU = 0xFFFFFFFF, REM/REMU = a (original, not |a|); INT_MIN / -1 falls out
    naturally (quotient 0x80000000, remainder 0, same-sign -> no negate). Quotient negated
    iff signs differ and b != 0; remainder negated iff a is negative (and b != 0).
  * DONE: `done`=1 for exactly one cycle with result = res_r, then back to IDLE
    unconditionally (EX/MEM holds a bubble in RUN/DONE so no dmem stall can overlap).

ex_stage.sv:
  * is_mdu_op = in.valid && in.ctrl.alu_op >= ALU_MUL (ops 11..18). Under
    `ifdef RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS is_mdu_op is tied to 0 and the MDU is not instantiated: the
    ALU's existing ALTOPS algebraic stand-ins keep the formal contract unchanged.
  * mdu_start = is_mdu_op && mdu_idle && !stall (stall = dmem_stall); output
    mdu_stall = is_mdu_op && !mdu_done.
  * EX/MEM next-state priority: reset > stall (dmem hold, unchanged) > mdu_stall (capture a
    bubble: `reg_q <= '0`, so valid=0, reg_write=0, mem_read/write=0) > normal capture.
    On the DONE cycle alu_result <= mdu_result (the existing is_jump?pc+4 mux stays, add
    is_mdu_op ? mdu_result : alu_result). RVFI-only fields rs1_val/rs2_val of the M-op use
    the MDU's captured a_r/b_r (so rs1_rdata/rs2_rdata stay correct even though the forward
    sources have moved on; these fields only feed RVFI so synthesis prunes them from the
    timed netlist).
  * Instantiate alu with a new parameter HAS_MULDIV (default 1, so test_alu.py and the
    ALTOPS build are unchanged); in the non-ALTOPS build ex_stage passes HAS_MULDIV=0 and the
    ALU's MUL*/DIV*/REM* arms become 32'b0 (constant-folded), eliminating the three
    multipliers and four dividers from the ALU cone.

hazard_unit.sv / core.sv: new input mdu_stall; stall_if |= mdu_stall; stall_id |= mdu_stall
(flush_id's existing `&& !dmem_stall` stays; load_use/redirect are 0 while an M-op sits in EX
so the ID/EX register simply holds). MEM/WB is NOT held: the instruction ahead of the M-op
advances normally on the start cycle, later cycles retire bubbles (valid=0), so the existing
forward_unit/MEM-WB bypass behaviour is untouched. A redirect can never squash an M-op in EX
(only EX itself resolves branches), so no abort path is needed. The start condition is
gated by !dmem_stall so a dmem-stalled older op holds everything (including MDU start) first.

Test updates (cores/bench/test): test_pipeline.py cycle-count expectations for M-ops (if any)
must be loosened to the new latency; add a test that issues back-to-back MUL/DIV/REM with
dependent consumers (forward from the instruction before the M-op and from the M-op result),
with imem/dmem ready toggling, and checks the retired order/values. test_alu.py continues to
pass because alu.sv keeps HAS_MULDIV=1 as default.

Optional fallback if the new worst path is the mdu a_r -> 33x33 multiplier -> res_r cone:
split it into two registered stages (partial products, then sum), costing one more stall
cycle per multiply.

title: Extract combinational MUL/DIV/REM from EX into a multi-cycle stalling MDU
motivation:
Baseline Fmax is 5.44 MHz: the worst path is 199.8 ns / 150 logic levels
through forward_unit -> ex_stage -> alu -> (EX/MEM alu_result / dmem address).
The ALU is a single combinational block that contains a 32x32 multiplier
(three separate 64-bit products: ss/uu/su), a 32-bit signed divider and a
32-bit signed remainder (`/` and `%` on 32-bit operands synthesize to a
~32-stage ripple subtract array, which is the 150-level path and ~half of the
12.3K LUT4). Every other path in the 5-stage pipe (fwd compare -> 3:1 mux ->
adder/shifter -> branch compare -> PC mux) is a small fraction of that, i.e.
roughly 15-25 ns on this part. CoreMark executes a few thousand MULs per
iteration (matrix kernels) and essentially no DIV/REM inside the timed region,
out of ~450K cycles/iteration, so spending 3-4 cycles on a MUL and 33+ cycles
on a DIV costs <2% iter/cycle while removing the dominant critical path. Fmax
is the only term in fitness (iter/cycle x Fmax) that has a >4.6% lever here,
and this removes the structure that sets it.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Remove all of the M-extension arithmetic from alu.sv (alu keeps only
ADD/SUB/AND/OR/XOR/SLT/SLTU/SLL/SRL/SRA/LUI) and put it in a new sequential
module rtl/mdu.sv that EX talks to with a start/busy/done handshake. EX holds
the M-op in ID/EX (stalls IF/ID and PC, injects bubbles into EX/MEM) until the
MDU result register is valid, then the result enters EX/MEM.alu_result through
one extra 2:1 mux whose input is a flop (no deep logic added to the critical
cone).

MDU design (all paths register-to-register, shallow):
 * Operand capture: on the first EX cycle of an M-op (state IDLE, valid,
   !stall_ex_mem) latch the *forwarded* rs1/rs2 into mdu_a/mdu_b. Forwarding
   sources (EX/MEM, MEM/WB) vanish on later cycles so capture must happen in
   cycle 0 and everything afterwards uses only the latched copies.
 * MUL/MULH/MULHU/MULHSU: extend to 33-bit signed operands (sign-bit per op:
   MUL/MULH both signed, MULHU both unsigned, MULHSU a signed / b unsigned),
   split each into a 16-bit unsigned low half and a 17-bit signed high half,
   and compute four 17x17 signed partial products (maps onto Gowin 18x18
   DSPs; ll, lh, hl, hh), registered. Next cycle: mid = lh + hl and
   lo = ll registered. Final cycle: 64-bit result = ll + (mid<<16) + (hh<<32),
   registered; select low or high word per op. Fixed 3-4 cycle latency; no
   long adder chain is wider than ~35 bits in any single cycle.
 * DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU: radix-2 restoring divider, one quotient bit per cycle
   (33-bit trial subtract + mux; ~5 ns), 32 iterations. Signed ops: take
   |a|, |b| in the capture/first cycle, negate quotient and/or remainder in
   the last cycle per RISC-V rules (q sign = sa^sb, r sign = sa). Special
   cases resolved in the final result mux from latched flags: divisor==0
   (DIV/DIVU -> 0xFFFFFFFF, REM/REMU -> dividend), INT_MIN/-1 (DIV ->
   INT_MIN, REM -> 0).
 * done: `res_valid` flop set when the result register is loaded, cleared on
   the edge where EX/MEM accepts the instruction (i.e. !stall_ex_mem).

Pipeline integration:
 * ex_stage computes ex_busy = id_ex.valid && is_mdu && !mdu_res_valid,
   where is_mdu = (alu_op >= ALU_MUL && alu_op <= ALU_REMU). ex_busy depends
   only on flops (ID/EX ctrl + MDU state) so it adds no forwarding depth.
 * hazard_unit takes ex_busy: stall_if |= ex_busy, stall_id |= ex_busy (hold
   ID/EX, do NOT flush), flush_id gated off while ex_busy (like dmem_stall).
   MDU advances only when !stall_ex_mem (dmem_stall freezes it; EX/MEM and
   ID/EX are already frozen then).
 * While ex_busy (and !stall_ex_mem) ex_stage writes a bubble into EX/MEM
   (valid=0, ctrl='0 so reg_write/mem_read/mem_write=0). Older instructions
   drain into MEM/WB normally. When res_valid is set the M-op proceeds:
   alu_result <= mdu_result, and the cycle also clears res_valid. A back-to-
   back M-op in ID moves into ID/EX on that same edge and starts next cycle.
 * RVFI correctness (checked by cosim and riscv-formal even though RVFI is
   untimed): EX/MEM.rs1_val / rs2_val for an M-op must be the *captured*
   operands (mdu_a/mdu_b raw copies), not the live forwarded values, because
   the producer may have left MEM/WB by the time the MDU finishes.
 * Under `RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS` the MDU still goes through the same
   start/busy/done handshake (so stall/hold/forward/liveness behaviour is what
   formal checks), but the result is the existing algebraic stand-in
   ((a+b)^K / (a-b)^K with the same constants as today's alu.sv) computed from
   the latched operands in the final cycle (>= 1 busy cycle, bounded latency,
   so the liveness check holds). The non-ALTOPS branch contains the real
   multiplier/divider. Keep both branches consistent.
 * Decoder is unchanged (ALU_MUL..ALU_REMU encodings stay); core.sv wires the
   new ex_busy output into hazard_unit. rvfi_order only advances on
   mem_wb.valid so bubbles do not disturb it.

Tests: test_alu.py keeps the base-op vectors and drops the M-op cases against
`alu`; all of those vectors (30+ per M op, exact bit results, div-by-zero and
INT_MIN/-1 corners) move to a new test_mdu.py that drives the mdu start/done
handshake, so invariant 5b coverage is not weakened. test_pipeline.py should
gain a back-to-back MUL/DIV with load-use + dmem-stall case if its harness
allows.

Expected: critical path drops from ~200 ns to the next-longest EX cone
(fwd-select -> mux -> adder/shifter/branch-compare -> PC or dmem address),
I expect ~20-30 ns => 33-50 MHz (6-9x Fmax). iter/cycle loses ~1-2%
(3 extra cycles per MUL x a few thousand per iteration, DIV negligible).
LUT4 should fall by roughly half, which also helps placement/routing.

lesson: - 2026-10-02 hyp-20261002-002-r1s1 (improvement, +770.79%): Inferred `*`, `/` and `%` inside the combinational ALU set the whole core's critical path (~200 ns, 150 logic levels, 5.44 MHz baseline), so moving M-ops into a multi-cycle MDU that stalls EX (busy derived only from ID/EX and MDU flops, result entering EX/MEM through a registered 2:1 mux) multiplied fitness ~8.7x because CoreMark's timed region has few MUL and almost no DIV/REM, making iter/cycle nearly insensitive while Fmax is the dominant lever; look for other deep arithmetic cones before touching IPC.

title: IF-stage early-redirect predictor: bimodal BHT + JAL + 4-entry return stack
motivation:
The baseline has no branch prediction: every taken branch, JAL and JALR is
resolved in EX and costs a 1-cycle redirect bubble (the wrong-path
instruction sitting in the combinational IF/ID slot is flushed). On CoreMark
roughly 14 of every ~100 instructions are taken branches or jumps, and each
bubble is also exposed to the ~22% imem stall rate when the target is
refetched, so redirect bubbles are on the order of 8-11% of all cycles.
The Fmax is set by the 200 ns combinational mul/div path through
forward_unit -> ex_stage -> alu (5.4 MHz), so any logic added in the IF stage
(a handful of LUT levels from the pc / imem_data registers) is far below the
critical path and is timing-free. The only lever a predictor has on fitness
is iterations/cycle, and the IF-stage structure here lets us convert most of
the redirect cycles into zero-bubble fetches without touching the critical
EX/ALU logic.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Predict in IF, directly from the fetched instruction word (imem_data is
available combinationally in the same cycle as imem_addr = pc, so no BTB is
needed - the target is computed from the instruction's own immediate).

1. IF-stage mini-decode of imem_data (opcode / funct3 / rd / rs1 / sign of
   imm), qualified by `!flush && !stall` so only instructions that are
   actually consumed this cycle can redirect or touch predictor state:
     - JAL: always predicted taken, target = pc + J-imm.
     - Conditional branch (funct3 != 2,3): predicted taken iff the 2-bit
       saturating counter bht[pc[8:2]] is >= 2 (128 entries, synchronous
       reset to 2'b01 so the result is deterministic), target = pc + B-imm.
     - JALR with rd==x0 and rs1 in {x1,x5} ("ret"): predicted taken with
       target = top of a 4-entry return-address stack.
     - JAL/JALR with rd in {x1,x5} push pc+4 onto the RAS (circular
       4-entry, no valid bits; a wrong guess is only a mispredict, never a
       correctness problem).
   Suppress prediction when the predicted target has bit 1 set (misaligned
   JAL/branch target), so a predicted fetch address is always 4-byte aligned
   and the existing misalign-trap handling in EX is unchanged.
   next_pc = redirect ? redirect_target
           : !stall && pred_taken ? pred_target : pc + 4.
   (Priority of the EX redirect over the predicted redirect is the same
   rule as the existing "redirect overrides stall".)

2. Carry `pred_taken` (1 bit) and `pred_target` (32 bits, needed only for
   JALR/RAS verification) in if_id_t and id_ex_t (core_pkg.sv, if_stage.sv,
   id_stage.sv - bubbles/reset are '0 so pred_taken=0 for non-branches).

3. EX-stage verification (ex_stage.sv). With
     actual_taken = (branch_taken || is_jump) && !misalign_fault
     target_ok    = !is_jalr || (pred_target == jump_target)
   redirect        = actual_taken ? !(pred_taken && target_ok) : pred_taken
   redirect_target = actual_taken ? (is_jump ? jump_target : branch_target)
                                  : in.pc + 4
   So a correctly predicted taken branch/JAL/ret redirects nothing (zero
   bubble instead of 1), a predicted-taken branch that falls through
   redirects to pc+4 (1 bubble - same cost as today's taken-branch bubble),
   and an unpredicted taken branch costs the same 1 bubble as today.
   EX/MEM pc_next, rd_wdata (PC+4 for jumps) and RVFI outputs are computed
   from the architectural outcome exactly as before, so the retirement
   stream seen by riscv-formal (pc_fwd, unique, liveness, trap) is
   unchanged.

4. BHT update in EX (ex_stage.sv or a small new rtl/bpred.sv): when a
   conditional branch is in EX with in.valid and !stall (so a branch held
   in EX by a dmem stall only updates once), increment/decrement
   bht[in.pc[8:2]] saturating on branch_taken.

Because wrong-path instructions only ever appear in IF during the same
cycle that EX asserts redirect (which already gates everything via
flush_if), no speculative RAS/BHT state is corrupted by squashed
instructions: predictor state is only touched by consumed instructions.
hazard_unit.sv, forward_unit.sv, alu.sv, decoder.sv, mem_stage.sv and the
Fmax-critical EX/ALU logic are not modified. Expected effect: taken
branches/jumps on CoreMark mostly become zero-penalty.

Measured offline (Python ISS retirement trace of the real -O3 2K CoreMark
ELF, 2.94M instructions, replaying the exact predictor described above):
conditional branches are 18.1% of instructions (55.6% taken), JAL 1.7%,
JALR 0.5%. Baseline redirect bubbles = 359k = 12.2% of instructions (each
costs exactly 1 cycle). With bimodal-128 + JAL + 4-entry RAS the residual
redirects are 54.9k (10.3% branch mispredict; 12 ret mispredicts and 22
non-ret JALR out of 13.8k JALR) = 1.9% of instructions, so 10.4% of
instructions' worth of bubbles are removed. Variants: 64-entry BHT 10.45%,
256-entry 10.7%, no RAS 9.9%, static BTFN only 8.4%, not-taken 2.2%. With
baseline CPI ~1.53 (CoreMark 2.23/MHz) that is ~6.8% fewer cycles, i.e.
~+7% iterations/cycle at unchanged Fmax. The 64-entry BHT is nearly as good
as 128 (and cheaper); either is acceptable. A RAS is worth ~0.5% on top of
JAL+BHT; keep it only if it does not complicate the implementation, the
BHT+JAL part alone gives ~9.9%. Area cost is ~256 BHT
flops + ~120 RAS flops + a 32-bit pc adder and a 32-bit compare, a few
hundred LUTs, none on the critical path. Cocotb/cosim must also be run to
verify CoreMark CRCs; if flop-array BHT area or P&R noise is a concern the
BHT can be shrunk to 64 entries.

changes.description: Add pred_taken (1b) and pred_target (32b) fields to if_id_t and id_ex_t.

Add IF mini-decode of imem_data (JAL / cond branch / ret / call), 128x2-bit bimodal BHT read, 4-entry return-address stack, predicted next_pc mux (below EX redirect priority, gated by !stall && !flush), and drive pred_taken/pred_target into the if_id bundle. title: Remove EX redirect from the IF/ID instr NOP-gate so load-use/stall_id leave the redirect cone
motivation:
`make timing` on the current champion (place option 0: 48.3 MHz, 19 levels,
25.98 ns arrival incl. 5.33 ns clock insertion) shows the worst path is not
the branch compare itself but what hangs off `redirect` afterwards:
  regfile BSRAM DO -> bypass LUT -> EX fwd mux (3 LUTs) -> 32-bit compare
  carry chain -> branch_cond/redirect (4 LUTs, fanout 105)
  -> if_stage `instr = (flush||redirect) ? NOP : imem_data`
     (-> rs1_addr/rs2_addr, fanout 10)
  -> hazard_unit load-use compare (id_ex_rd == if_id_rs1/rs2, mapped onto
     ALU carry cells) -> stall_id / stall_if (2 more LUTs, fanout ~100)
  -> D/enable of the ID/EX data flops and PC flops.
The last ~6.4 ns of the path (redirect -> NOP mask -> load-use compare ->
stall_id -> ID/EX enables) exist only because the NOP mask on the fetched
instruction depends on `redirect`. All of that work is dead on a redirect
cycle: flush_id already zeroes ID/EX ctrl/valid, and the ID/EX data fields
are deliberately not flushed.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make the IF/ID payload independent of `redirect`: in if_stage use
`out.instr = flush ? NOP : imem_data; out.valid = !flush;` and in
hazard_unit `flush_if = imem_stall;` (drop the `redirect ||` term). The
`redirect` input of if_stage stays (PC register keeps redirect priority
over stall) and hazard_unit's `redirect` input stays (flush_id =
(load_use || redirect) && !(dmem_stall || ex_busy), a narrow cone into
ID/EX ctrl/valid only). No other file needs to change.

Why behaviour is unchanged (cycle-exact, so IPC and CoreMark CRCs are
identical):
  1. On a redirect cycle the ID/EX slot either captures a flushed bubble
     (flush_id=1 -> ctrl='0, valid=0) or is held by a dmem stall and
     captures nothing. Either way the raw wrong-path instruction's
     rd/rs/imm/pc/instr bits are dead: ctrl=0 means no reg_write / mem /
     branch / MDU, so forward_unit (keys on ctrl.reg_write) and
     hazard_unit (keys on ctrl.mem_read) ignore them; valid=0 keeps them
     out of RVFI.
  2. A load-use stall needs a LOAD in EX, a redirect needs a branch/jump in
     EX, so they are mutually exclusive; a spurious load-use on a redirect
     cycle cannot occur (and the PC register gives redirect priority over
     stall_if anyway).
  3. imem_stall still forces the NOP + valid=0 bubble exactly as today, so
     fetch-stall bubbles keep rd=0/NOP semantics.
Redirect now terminates at the PC mux (1 LUT level, fanout 32) and at
flush_id -> ID/EX ctrl/valid reset (~20 flops).

re-apply it): `make timing TARGET=bench` place option 0 went from
48.337 MHz (19 levels, 25.98 ns) to 58.853 MHz (14 levels, 22.29 ns), i.e.

(selftest + CoreMark) passes. LUT4 2408 -> 2400. New worst path is
regfile BSRAM -> bypass/fwd mux -> ALU adder/result mux -> EX/MEM
alu_result / dmem BSRAM address (ADB), so the redirect cone is no longer
limiting; the next micro_opt target after this one is the 5-LUT ALU result
select in front of reg_q.alu_result (is_mdu / is_jump / shifter muxing).

argument above is why `unique`/`liveness`/`reg`/`pc_fwd` should be
unaffected: retirement validity and ctrl bubbles are identical.

title: Retime hazard/forward control across ID/EX and take EX redirect off the IF/ID and stall nets
motivation:
After the MDU extraction the worst path (25.98 ns, 19 levels, 51.4 MHz) is the EX
redirect loop, reported as u_id -> u_ex -> u_if -> u_hazard -> u_id and ending on an
ID/EX data flop (id_ex.rs2_val). That is: ID/EX flops -> forward_unit 5-bit compare +
priority -> 3:1 forward mux -> 32-bit branch compare -> redirect -> if_stage NOP mask
(out.instr = (flush||redirect) ? NOP : imem_data) -> hazard_unit load-use compare ->
stall_id -> clock-enable of ~190 ID/EX data flops. The late redirect reaches the
high-fanout stall net only because (a) the hazard compare reads the redirect-masked
instruction, and (b) the same mask also feeds the decoder/imm_gen -> ID/EX ctrl D
pins, even though flush_id already clears ctrl/valid on redirect. The forward-select
compare also sits serially in front of the operand mux in EX. IPC is already good
(taken-branch penalty is a single bubble), so the lever is levels on this loop.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Move control computation across the ID/EX register boundary so the late redirect
has only two sinks (pc flops, and the ~16 ctrl/valid flush flops):
(1) In ID, compute the 5-bit equality matches of raw IF/ID rs1/rs2 against ID/EX.rd
    (producer that will be in EX/MEM when the consumer is in EX) and against
    EX/MEM.rd (producer that will be in MEM/WB), each qualified by rd != 0, and
    register the four match bits in ID/EX. In EX, forward_unit shrinks to
    sel1 = match_exmem && ex_mem.ctrl.reg_write; sel2 = match_memwb &&
    mem_wb.ctrl.reg_write && !sel1. The reg_write qualification stays in EX using the
    already trap-corrected EX/MEM and MEM/WB ctrl flops, so misaligned jump/load
    traps (which clear reg_write) still suppress forwarding exactly as today. The
    match bits are valid whenever ID/EX holds, because EX/MEM and MEM/WB hold in
    the same stall cases (dmem stall, MDU busy), and ID/EX only captures when the
    pipeline actually advances.
(2) hazard_unit's load-use compare reads raw imem_data[19:15]/[24:20] instead of the
    masked instruction. A spurious load-use on a wrong-path or not-delivered
    instruction is harmless: flush_id still clears ctrl/valid, pc takes the redirect
    target with priority over stall, and imem_stall already forces valid=0.
(3) if_stage drops `redirect` from out.instr / out.valid (keep only the imem_stall
    flush from the registered bus-ready signal); flush_id already kills the
    wrong-path ID/EX ctrl and valid, and a held ID/EX (dmem stall / MDU busy)
    never captures IF/ID that cycle. This removes redirect -> mux -> decoder ->
    ctrl D-pin and redirect -> hazard -> stall_id -> CE fanout.
Net: ~4-6 fewer LUT levels on the critical loop with identical cycle behaviour
(no IPC change, cosim traces must remain bit-identical in retirement order).
The next-worst paths (regfile read mux -> ID/EX, EX/MEM -> fwd mux -> adder -> EX/MEM,
dmem address -> memory) are expected around 14-16 levels, so the realistic Fmax
gain is ~15-25% before place-and-route noise.

title: Timing-neutral IF-stage JAL + BHT early redirect (direction-only verify, no RAS/target compare)
motivation:
After the MDU change the core runs 4.87M cycles per 10 CoreMark iterations at 51.4 MHz (26 ns, 19 levels).
Every taken branch / JAL / JALR is still resolved in EX and costs a one-cycle redirect bubble: the
wrong-path word sitting in the combinational IF/ID slot is flushed. The earlier IF-stage predictor
(hyp-20261002-003-r1s2: 128-entry 2-bit BHT + JAL + 4-entry RAS) cut the baseline's cycles by 7.2%
(4.49M -> 4.19M), and the offline ISS replay matched that, so the IPC estimate is trustworthy. It was
scored a regression only because it ran at 5.5 MHz against a 200 ns mul/div path. On the MDU core the
same IPC gain is worth roughly +7% fitness. The critical path is no longer hidden behind a 200 ns cone,
though. It is the EX loop: ID/EX flops -> forward mux -> branch compare -> `redirect` -> IF NOP mux
(u_if) -> load-use compare (u_hazard) -> ID/EX CE/flush (u_id). The r1s2 design added a 32-bit
`pred_target == jump_target` compare and a RAS-pop target into that loop, which is what would cost
Fmax now. So keep only the predictor parts that need no wide compare in EX, and shorten the redirect
loop by the same amount the verify XOR adds.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Predict in IF straight from the fetched word, which is combinational from imem_addr = pc, so no BTB is
needed. Verify in EX by DIRECTION only, so there is no target compare and no RAS.

1. IF predecode of imem_data (opcode only plus imm sign). pred_taken_raw =
     JAL                                   (always taken), or
     conditional BRANCH (opcode 1100011)   && bht[idx][1].
   pred_target = pc + J-imm or pc + B-imm (one 32-bit carry-chain add straight off the flops/imem word).
   Suppress the prediction when pred_target[1] is set (misaligned target), so a predicted fetch address is
   always 4-aligned. JALR is NOT predicted (no RAS); it keeps today's EX redirect.
   next_pc = redirect ? redirect_target : (pred_taken_IF ? pred_target : pc + 4). The existing
   `if (redirect) pc <= redirect_target; else if (!stall) pc <= next_pc` priority is kept, so a predicted
   redirect only acts when the fetched word is actually consumed (!stall_if, which already includes
   imem_stall / load-use / dmem_stall / ex_busy). Redirect still overrides stall.
2. BHT: 128 entries x 2-bit saturating counters, index = pc[8:2], synchronous reset to 2'b01 so cycle
   counts are deterministic. It is trained ONLY in EX: update when in.valid && ctrl.is_branch &&
   !stall_ex_mem (a branch held in EX during a dmem stall is counted once), writing actual `branch_taken`
   to counter[in.pc[8:2]]. No bypass from update to read is needed (a stale read is only a mispredict).
3. Carry one extra bit, pred_taken, IF -> ID/EX. It is gated with !(flush || redirect) in IF so bubbles
   never carry a prediction, and it is cleared in id_stage's existing `reset || flush` ctrl/valid flop
   block together with ctrl.
4. EX verification: let `actual_taken` be the current `(branch_taken || is_jump) && !misalign_fault`.
   redirect = actual_taken ^ pred_taken (the carried bit). That is a single extra XOR with a flop input.
   redirect_target = pred_taken ? (in.pc + 4)                        // predicted taken, wasn't: go to fall-through
                                 : (is_jump ? jump_target : branch_target);
   in.pc + 4 already exists for the JAL link value. A correctly predicted branch/JAL now produces
   redirect = 0 and no bubble. A mispredicted one costs the same single flush cycle as today. Illegal
   opcodes, misaligned JAL (actual_taken = 0 while pred was suppressed), and JALR (pred = 0, actual = 1)
   all fall out of the generic XOR rule. ex_mem.pc_next stays correct: pc_next must equal the
   architectural next pc, so it keeps its existing misalign / jump / branch / pc+4 priority and is NOT
   derived from the prediction.
5. Timing mitigation so the redirect loop does not get longer: drive the regfile read addresses and the
   hazard unit's load-use compare from the raw imem_data[19:15] / [24:20] bits rather than from the
   NOP-substituted `if_id_w.instr`. This is cycle-equivalent. When the slot is flushed (redirect) or
   invalid (imem_stall), a spurious load-use hazard only produces a bubble in ID/EX (flush_id wins over
   stall_id for ctrl/valid) and holds the PC, which redirect/imem_stall already do. The decoder and
   imm_gen keep the NOP-substituted word, so an imem-stalled slot still decodes as ADDI x0,x0,0. This
   takes the redirect -> NOP-mux -> compare -> stall_id/flush_id leg (u_if + part of u_hazard) out of
   the loop and pays for the new XOR.

Expected: ~75-80% of the one-cycle redirect bubbles removed (JAL + biased/loop branches), losing only the
return JALR share relative to r1s2 (about 1% of cycles), for ~6-7% fewer cycles. Area: ~256 BHT flops plus
one adder, small against 2.4K LUT4. If Fmax regresses more than ~3% the first thing to try is a 64-entry
BHT or 1-bit-hysteresis counters (shorter read mux), not adding target compares.

title: Stack cycle-exact EX-loop retimings on the predictor champion: registered forward matches, one-hot operand AND-OR, redirect off the IF NOP mask
motivation:
The champion (r2s2, 137.72, 63.05 MHz, 22.07 ns / 14 cells) is limited by the EX loop:
ID/EX flops -> forward_unit 5-bit rs-vs-rd compare + EX/MEM-over-MEM/WB priority -> 3:1
forward mux -> alu_src / is_auipc operand mux -> ALU (adder/shifter/op mux) -> EX/MEM
alu_result mux, with the sibling leg forward mux -> branch compare -> redirect -> IF/ID
NOP mask -> decoder/imm_gen -> ID/EX ctrl D pins. LESSONS.md records two proven, IPC-neutral
retimings of exactly this loop that lost their rounds only to the (different-logic)
predictor and were never stacked: r2s0 (drop `redirect` from the IF NOP mask; 19 -> 14 levels

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make three cycle-exact changes (cosim retirement traces must stay bit-identical; iter/cycle
unchanged), all aimed at shortening the EX operand-select front end and the redirect fan-out.

(1) Registered forward matches (the r2s1 idea, on the champion). In ID compare the raw fetched
rs1/rs2 fields (imem_data[19:15] / [24:20]) against ID/EX.rd (producer that will sit in EX/MEM
when the consumer is in EX) and against EX/MEM.rd (producer that will sit in MEM/WB), each
qualified by rd != 0, and latch four bits (m1_rs1, m2_rs1, m1_rs2, m2_rs2) in the ID/EX
data-flop group (held on stall_id, reset to 0, NOT flushed). Correctness: ID/EX only captures
when !stall_id, which implies no dmem stall and no MDU busy, so EX/MEM and MEM/WB advance
exactly one position at that edge and the compared producers are the ones the consumer will see.
While the consumer is held (dmem stall) EX/MEM and MEM/WB data are frozen too; MDU-busy cycles
after the first do not use the forwarded operands (a_q/b_q are latched in the first EX cycle);
a load-use bubble / redirect bubble carries stale or wrong-path rd but ctrl=0, and reg_write
is qualified in EX, so nothing changes. The reg_write qualification stays in EX on the
already trap-corrected EX/MEM and MEM/WB ctrl flops (misaligned jump / load traps that clear
reg_write still suppress forwarding exactly as today). EX-side selects become one LUT level off
flops: sel1 = m1 & ex_mem.reg_write; sel2 = m2 & mem_wb.reg_write & ~sel1; sel0 = ~sel1 & ~sel2.

(2) One-hot AND-OR operand muxes. Replace the serial "forward 3:1 mux -> alu_src mux" and
"forward mux -> is_auipc mux" with explicit one-hot AND-OR terms so the whole operand select is
select-gen (1 level) + 4-term AND-OR (2 LUT4 levels) instead of ~5 levels:
alu_b = (!alu_src & sel0_b & rs2_val) | (!alu_src & sel1_b & ex_mem.alu_result) |
(!alu_src & sel2_b & wb_data) | (alu_src & imm). The pure forwarded rs1 / rs2 (3:1 AND-OR)
are kept as separate nets for the branch compare, store write_data, MDU capture and RVFI
rs1_val/rs2_val. Take AUIPC out of the ALU A operand entirely (alu_a = forwarded rs1 only):
its result pc + imm already exists as branch_target, so the EX/MEM alu_result mux becomes
is_mdu ? mdu_result : is_jump ? pc + 4 : is_auipc ? branch_target : alu_result, where pc + 4
and pc + imm come straight from ID/EX flops (early arrival, off the critical cone). Optionally
register `is_mdu` as a ctrl bit decoded in ID instead of the alu_op range compare in EX.

if_stage: out.instr = flush ? NOP : imem_data; out.valid = !flush; out.pred_taken =
pred_hit && !flush, where flush is now only the imem_stall term (hazard_unit flush_if =
imem_stall). `redirect` stays in the pc mux (priority over stall) and in flush_id, which
already clears ID/EX ctrl, valid and pred_taken on a redirect, and when ID/EX is held

and valid = 0 has no side effect (no reg_write / mem op / branch / MDU start / BHT update /

critical path should shift to the ALU adder/shifter + EX/MEM mux; if the AND-OR form does not

title: Flop-based regfile + registered forward selects + registered BHT update: clean-flop operand supply for EX
motivation:
`make timing` on the champion (63 MHz, 14 logic levels, ~16.7 ns of data delay) shows three
path groups all within 0.3 ns of each other, and all of them start in the operand-supply
structure rather than in the ALU itself:
  (a) cpu/u_rf/regs BSRAM DO -> 2 LUTs of regfile bypass/x0 mux (named u_id/id_ex_w.rs1_val_*)
      -> 2 LUTs of EX forward mux -> alu_a (is_auipc) mux -> ALU -> result mux -> dmem BSRAM
      address / EX/MEM.alu_result.  Gowin inferred the 32x32 regfile as BSRAM (sync read) and
      slid the ID/EX rs1_val/rs2_val flops into it, so the BSRAM clock-to-out (2.26 ns, vs ~0.3 ns
      for a flop) AND the write-first-bypass + x0-zero muxes ended up *inside the EX cycle*.
  (b) ID/EX.rs1_addr flop -> forward_unit 5-bit compare (carry-chain, 1.3 ns route + 0.7 ns)
      -> priority/decode with fanout 60 -> 3:1 forward mux -> 32-bit branch comparator
      -> bht_upd_new read-modify-write -> BHT RAM write (endpoint cpu/u_if/bht_*).
  (c) the same forward-compare front end -> comparator -> redirect -> pc mux (cpu/u_if/pc_*).
Prior retiming r2s1 (registered forward matches) showed +8% Fmax over the mask-only variant
at identical cycles and passed formal/cosim, but it was never stacked on the champion. It
fixes only (b)/(c) front end; (a) still limits, so no single fix gives the gain. All three
groups must be shortened together.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Restructure operand supply so EX starts from plain flops and nothing but a 3:1 AND-OR forward
mux sits between ID/EX and the ALU / comparator. All steps are cycle-exact (IPC-neutral) except
step 3, which changes BHT training latency by one cycle (negligible).

1. Flop-based regfile (rtl/reg_file.sv). Replace `logic [31:0] regs[0:31]` (inferred as BSRAM
   with absorbed ID/EX register) with 31 explicit 32-bit registers built in a `generate` loop
   (one `always_ff` per register with `if (reset) q<=0; else if (w_en && w_addr==i) q<=w_data`),
   x0 hardwired 0, collected into a packed/wire vector and read through a plain 32:1 mux
   (`flat[rs_addr]`), followed by the existing write-first bypass and x0 zeroing. Do NOT use an
   unpacked `regs[]` array (Gowin would re-infer RAM). Optionally also add
   `(* syn_ramstyle = "registers" *)`. The bypass/x0 mux now ends at the ID/EX D pins (ID cycle,
   driven by the raw imem_data address flops/LFSR, ~6-8 LUT levels, far from critical), so
   ID/EX.rs1_val/rs2_val are real flops and EX loses the BSRAM tC2Q plus 2 mux levels.
   Cost ~ +1000 FF and ~+800 LUT4, which is well within the 10000 LUT budget.

2. Registered forward selects (rtl/forward_unit.sv, rtl/id_stage.sv, rtl/ex_stage.sv,
   rtl/core_pkg.sv, rtl/core.sv). In ID, for the instruction being captured into ID/EX, compute
   (from raw imem_data rs1/rs2 fields, as the load-use compare already does)
     m1_rs1 = (rs1 != 0) && (rs1 == id_ex.rd)        // the instruction in EX now = in EX/MEM next cycle
     m2_rs1 = (rs1 != 0) && (rs1 == ex_mem.rd)       // the instruction in MEM now = in MEM/WB next cycle
   and likewise m1_rs2 / m2_rs2, and store these 4 bits as new ID/EX flops (captured on the same
   `!stall` enable as the other ID/EX payload; cleared to 0 on reset/flush with ctrl). In EX the
   selects become  fwd1 = m1_q & ex_mem.ctrl.reg_write ;  fwd2 = ~fwd1 & m2_q & mem_wb.ctrl.reg_write
   (priority EX/MEM > MEM/WB kept). Gating by the *registered* reg_write bits of EX/MEM and MEM/WB
   keeps trap-suppressed writes (misaligned jump/branch cleared in EX, misaligned mem op cleared in
   MEM), bubbles and dmem-stall retained-MEM/WB cases identical to the current combinational
   unit; do NOT gate on mem_wb.valid (valid is cleared during hold while data is retained for
   forwarding). Pipeline advance is lock-step whenever ID/EX captures a real instruction
   (stall_id covers dmem_stall / load-use / ex_busy), so the stage relationships assumed at ID
   time hold at EX time; the load-use bubble case re-evaluates the match on the replayed ID cycle
   (ID/EX holds a bubble so m1=0, m2 matches the load in EX/MEM). The 5-bit compare + fanout-60
   decode (~3 ns) leaves the EX cycle.

3. Registered BHT update (rtl/if_stage.sv, rtl/ex_stage.sv). Register {upd_en, upd_idx,
   upd_taken} (9 flops) inside if_stage and do the read-modify-write one cycle later, so
   branch_taken (32-bit comparator through the forward mux) no longer feeds bht_upd_new -> BHT
   RAM write. No update->read bypass exists already; the only effect is predictions seeing an
   update one cycle later.

4. (optional, if time permits) Predecode one-hot ALU result-select flops in ID/EX
   (add/sub/logic/slt/shift/lui/link/mdu classes, with is_jump/is_mdu folded in) so the EX result
   mux feeding EX/MEM.alu_result (and therefore the dmem BSRAM address) is an AND-OR from flops
   instead of a 5-bit op decode + deep case mux; keeps the ALTOPS/real MDU branches in mdu.sv
   untouched.

Invariants: RVFI contents, rvfi_order, traps and all cycle counts unchanged (iter/cycle stays
~2.18e-6 within ~0.1%); decoder defaults untouched. Expected effect: the three near-critical
groups each lose ~3 ns (BSRAM tC2Q + bypass LUTs for (a); compare + fanout-60 decode for
(b)/(c)), taking the data path from ~16.7 ns toward ~13.5-14 ns, i.e. Fmax ~63 -> ~72-76 MHz,
with the redirect -> pc loop and the ALU result mux then setting the limit.

title: Predictor-directed decoupled fetch: 4-entry instruction queue with IF bypass behind the JAL+BHT early redirect
motivation:
The IF-stage JAL+BHT early redirect (r2s2) already removed ~85% of the redirect bubbles. Offline ISS
numbers from r1s2 give 54.9k residual branch mispredicts plus 13.8k JALR redirects, about 69k cycles out
of ~4.58M (1.5%), so any further direction/target accuracy work (gshare, RAS, bigger BHT) is capped at
well under the 4.6% acceptance bar. The big remaining front-end loss is the 22% imem stall rate: the
PC register is frozen on every !imem_ready cycle and also on every load-use / dmem / MDU backend stall,
so fetch and decode are in lock-step and every imem stall becomes a full lost issue slot
(~0.28 lost cycles per instruction, ~0.8M cycles, ~18% of runtime). Backend-side stall cycles
(dmem stalls, load-use, MDU busy, ~0.6M cycles) are cycles in which the fetch port is idle even though
imem could deliver. Because the predictor already computes the next fetch PC from the fetched word
alone (no BTB, no extra EX logic), the fetch stream can be allowed to run ahead of decode into a small
queue, converting backend stall cycles into prefetched instructions that later cover imem stalls.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Decouple IF from ID with a small predictor-directed instruction queue; keep everything downstream of ID
(hazard/forward/EX/MEM/WB, direction-only EX verify, BHT training) unchanged.

1. if_stage.sv: the fetch PC keeps its current JAL+BHT next_pc logic (predecode of the fetched word,
   pc + J/B-imm, bht[pc[8:2]][1], misaligned-target suppression). The fetch PC now advances whenever
   the word is delivered and there is queue room: fetch_fire = io_imemReady && (q_count != DEPTH);
   it NO LONGER freezes on load-use / dmem_stall / ex_busy. EX redirect still overrides everything
   (pc <= redirect_target) and flushes the queue.
2. A DEPTH=4 circular queue of {pc, instr, pred_taken} entries (about 65 flops/entry). The entry at
   the tail pointer is written every fetch_fire cycle regardless of redirect / decode state; only the
   small tail/head/count flops depend on the late signals (redirect clears count, push/pop adjust it),
   so the late EX `redirect` does not fan out to ~260 data flops.
3. Decode input mux (the IF "bypass"): dec = q_nonempty ? entry[head] : {pc, imem_data, pred}, with
   dec_valid = q_nonempty || (io_imemReady && !redirect). q_nonempty is a registered bit, so the mux
   select is not timing-critical and a redirect penalty stays at 1 cycle: the redirect target is
   fetched in the next cycle and goes straight to decode through the bypass when the queue is empty.
   The regfile read addresses and the load-use compare take rs1/rs2 from the muxed decode word (same
   "raw word, not NOP-substituted" scheme as today: a spurious compare on an invalid slot only
   produces a bubble because flush_id already wins over stall_id for ctrl/valid).
4. Queue bookkeeping: pop = q_nonempty && !stall_id (decode consumed the head). A bypassed word that
   decode does not consume this cycle (stall_id) is pushed instead (the tail slot was already written),
   so push = fetch_fire && !(!q_nonempty && !stall_id). count_next = redirect ? 0 : count + push - pop.
   pred_taken is carried in the entry and in if_id_t exactly as now; EX keeps the direction-only
   verify (redirect = actual_taken ^ pred_taken, redirect_target = pred ? pc+4 : target) so no
   pred_target compare enters the redirect loop.
5. hazard_unit.sv: stall_if (PC hold) is replaced by "fetch cannot fire"; stall_id =
   dmem_stall || load_use || ex_busy stays as the decode-hold signal and is also the queue "no pop"
   signal. flush_if/NOP-substitution is replaced by dec_valid gating (a flushed slot is simply not
   valid), keeping `redirect` out of the instruction words.

Retirement stream, rvfi_order, pc_rdata/pc_wdata continuity and the trap rules are unchanged: only the
cycle at which an instruction reaches decode changes, and wrong-path words never leave the queue (it is
cleared on every EX redirect, and the queue only holds words along the predicted path). The formal
wrapper drives symbolic imem data, which is compatible because each retirement carries its own insn/pc.

Estimate (stochastic cycle model I ran: Bernoulli 78% imem ready, 27% memory ops with 22% dmem stall
per cycle, 8% load-use, 1.9% redirect with a 1-cycle bubble, 0.4% MDU ops; the lock-step baseline
gives CPI 1.49, close to the real ~1.56): CPI by queue depth D = 0: 1.494, 1: 1.459, 2: 1.369,
4: 1.337, 8: 1.329. So depth 4 is about -10.5% cycles (+11.7% iter/cycle) and depth 2 already gets
most of it (-8.4%); depth 8 adds almost nothing. If depth 4 costs Fmax, drop to depth 2. Fetch-ahead
beyond an unpredicted JALR only touches sequential in-range text words (the baseline already fetches
the word after a JALR). Area: ~270 extra flops plus a 4:1 mux on ~66 bits, far under the LUT budget.
Fmax risk: the new decode mux (queue head vs imem_data) and queue control sit before the decoder /
load-use compare, not in the EX forward->ALU->compare loop (the worst path is
ID/EX -> u_ex -> alu -> u_ex), and the PC loop actually gets shorter because the load-use compare no
longer feeds stall_if. An output-registered head entry (dedicated head flops, queue behind it) is the
fallback if the 4:1 head mux shows up in the timing report.

title: Late MEM-result bypass into ID/EX operand flops: drop the MEM/WB->EX forward leg so EX forwards through a single 2:1 mux
motivation:
`make timing` on the r3s1 champion (76.8 MHz, 18.7 ns arrival) shows five near-tied
worst paths, and every one of them runs through the EX 3:1 forward mux that is fed
by the MEM/WB flops:
  1. mem_wb.wb_data_4  -> fwd mux -> alu operand mux -> ALU adder -> alu_result mux -> dmem BSRAM addr (19 cells, 18.704 ns)
  2. mem_wb.wb_data_4  -> fwd mux -> branch compare -> redirect -> pc_10                (38 cells, 18.703 ns)
  3. mem_wb.ctrl.reg_write -> fwd select (fanout ~64) -> mux -> ALU -> BSRAM addr      (12 cells, 18.684 ns)
  4. mem_wb.wb_data_4  -> fwd mux -> compare -> redirect -> NOP mask -> u_id rd flop    (38 cells, 18.638 ns)
  5. ex_mem.alu_result_20 -> fwd mux -> ALU -> BSRAM addr                               (11 cells, 18.599 ns)
Because they are tied, only a change that shortens the *common* prefix (the forward
mux and its two high-fanout selects) can move Fmax; fixing the ALU/BSRAM tail or the
redirect tail alone leaves the others at 18.6-18.7 ns (this is the lesson of r3s1).
The 3:1 AND-OR needs 3 selects + 3 data inputs per bit = 2 LUT4 levels, plus the
mem_wb.reg_write / ex_mem.reg_write select decode with fanout ~64. A 2:1 mux whose
select is `m1 & ex_mem.reg_write` is exactly 4 inputs per bit: one LUT4, no select decode.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Move the MEM/WB -> EX forward leg one stage earlier, into ID. When a consumer is in ID
and the producer B is in MEM (so B will be in MEM/WB when the consumer is in EX), B's
write-back value is already available at the end of this cycle as the D input of the
MEM/WB wb_data flop (`mem_to_reg ? load_data : alu_result`, premuxed in mem_stage), and
its reg_write (after the misaligned-access trap clear) is available as
`ctrl_with_trap.reg_write`. Export both from mem_stage (`wb_fwd_data`, `wb_fwd_en`) to
id_stage and capture
   rs1_val <= (m2_rs1_d && wb_fwd_en) ? wb_fwd_data : regfile_rs1_data   (same for rs2)
where m2_rs1_d = (raw_rs1 != 0 && raw_rs1 == ex_mem.rd) already exists in id_stage
(it just stops being registered). The bypass has priority over the regfile write-first
bypass (B is younger than the WB-stage producer). The ID/EX capture only happens when
stall_id = 0, which implies no dmem stall and no MDU busy, so EX/MEM -> MEM/WB advances
exactly one slot at that edge and B's value is final; a consumer held in ID during a
dmem stall or load-use bubble simply re-evaluates the bypass in its capture cycle (for a
load-use the load is in MEM on the replay cycle and its load_data is the bypass source).
In EX, only the EX/MEM leg remains:
   fwd_rsX = m1_rsX && ex_mem.ctrl.reg_write
   rsX     = fwd_rsX ? ex_mem.alu_result : id_ex.rsX_val
(A is younger than B, so EX/MEM priority is preserved; if A is a store/branch whose rd bits
alias rs, reg_write=0 falls through to rs_val, which already holds B's value, exactly as
the old priority chain fell through to MEM/WB.) Remove the m2_rs1/m2_rs2 flops from
id_ex_t, collapse forward_unit to two AND gates, shrink fwd_*_sel to one bit, and drop
the fwd_mem_wb input of ex_stage. hold_wb data retention in mem_stage can stay (harmless).
The new late path is dmem BSRAM tC2Q (~2.3 ns) -> load extract/sign-extend -> mem_to_reg
mux -> bypass mux -> ID/EX rs?_val D, about 10 ns against the ~13 ns period, well below
the current worst. Cycle behaviour, retirement trace, hazards, trap discipline and CoreMark
CRCs are bit-identical (pure retiming across the ID/EX boundary, same family as the
proven r2s1 / r3s1 retimings), so the gain is Fmax only. Expected: one LUT level fewer
plus removal of the fanout-64 mem_wb.reg_write select on all five tied path groups,
~1 ns of 13 ns, so +6..9% fitness. Cost: ~64 LUT4 for the extra bypass mux, -2 flops.

title: Resolve redirect from EX/MEM flops (MEM-stage redirect) plus a dedicated load/store AGU off the ALU result mux
motivation:
`make timing` on the r3s1 champion (74.6 MHz, 13.37 ns data delay, 63% of it
ROUTE) shows two path families tied within 0.1 ns, so fixing either alone
buys nothing:
(a) wb_data/EX-MEM flop -> forward AND-OR (2 LUT) -> alu_b select (1 LUT,
    fanout 49) -> 32-bit adder -> FIVE LUT levels of ALU-op result mux
    (u_ex/n950_*) -> dmem_addr LUT -> dmem BSRAM ADB pin (paths 1,3,5,7...).
    Gowin absorbed the EX/MEM alu_result register into the BSRAM address
    register, so every ALU-op / MDU / jump mux level sits in front of a
    BSRAM setup pin, although a load/store only ever needs rs1+imm.
(b) forward mux -> 32-bit compare carry chain -> branch_cond op mux (2 LUT)
    -> redirect XOR (1 LUT, arrival ~8.8 ns of data delay) -> the redirect
    fan-out into pc CE, flush_if/flush_id, ID/EX ctrl/valid D pins and the
    pc_next mux: ~4.6 ns of pure fan-out/route after the redirect bit
    exists (paths 2,4,6,13,14,15,19-25: pc_*/CE and u_id reg_q.*/D).
Both tails are structural: the first is address generation sharing the
generic ALU result mux, the second is a same-cycle resolve->squash loop.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
1. Late redirect (MEM-stage redirect). EX still computes
   `redirect = actual_taken ^ pred_taken` but only registers it: add
   `redirect` (1 flop) to EX/MEM (killed on a bubble). The redirect target
   is already EX/MEM.pc_next in every redirect case (pred=0/actual=1 ->
   branch/jump target, pred=1/actual=0 -> pc+4, misalign -> no redirect),
   so no new 32-bit register is needed. The IF PC mux, `flush_if`,
   `flush_id` and the squash of the instruction currently in EX are driven
   by `redirect_m = ex_mem.valid & ex_mem.redirect` -- a flop output -- not
   by the compare cone. While redirect_m is high: EX/MEM captures a bubble
   (valid=0, ctrl=0, redirect=0) for the wrong-path op in EX, its bht_upd_en
   and MDU `start`/ex_busy are gated off, ID/EX captures a bubble, IF emits a
   NOP and PC <= ex_mem.pc_next. Cost: one extra bubble per mispredicted
   branch / JALR (about 8K redirects per CoreMark iteration of ~458K cycles,
   so ~1.5-2% more cycles). Benefit: the compare -> redirect -> fan-out tail
   (~4.6 ns, path family b) ends at one EX/MEM flop D pin; the PC CE /
   flush nets start at a flop.
2. Dedicated AGU. Add `agu_sum = rs1_fwd + in.imm` (already needed as
   `jalr_sum`; share it) registered into a NEW EX/MEM field `mem_addr` that
   only feeds mem_stage (dmem address, byte mask, misalign, load align).
   `alu_result` keeps ALU/MDU/PC+4 and the forward/write-back users. The
   synthesizer absorbs only `mem_addr` into the BSRAM address register, so
   the BSRAM-bound cone loses the operand-select LUT, the 5-level ALU-op mux
   and the mdu/jump mux (family a: ~6 LUT levels + their routes, ~5 ns).
3. Flatten the remaining ALU-result cone so it does not become the new
   limiter (~11.4 ns data delay at the mux output today): pre-decode in ID
   one-hot select flops (sel_add/sub, sel_logic, sel_slt, sel_shift, sel_lui,
   sel_mdu, sel_pc4) and register them in ID/EX (ctrl_t grows ~8 bits); the
   ALU result becomes a 2-level AND-OR of already-computed candidates
   (adder/subtractor output shared with SLT/SLTU, shifter, logic) instead of
   the 5-bit `case`. Fold `alu_src`/`is_auipc` into ID: ID/EX gets an
   `op_b` register (imm for alu_src, else rs2) and an `op_a` register (pc for
   AUIPC/JAL link, else rs1) with the m1/m2 forward-match bits masked off
   for operands that are not register reads, so the EX operand path is one
   forward AND-OR level (rs2 for stores/branches keeps its own forward mux
   for write_data / compare).
Expected: BSRAM-address and ALU->EX/MEM cones drop to ~9-10 ns, compare ->
EX/MEM flop ~9 ns; Fmax 74.6 -> ~90-100 MHz (+20-30%) against ~-2% iter/cycle,
net ~+10-20%. Correctness: architectural results and RVFI fields identical
(wrong-path ops are killed before EX/MEM so none reaches MEM/WB); formal's
pc_fwd / liveness / unique checks see the same retirement stream; dmem
stalls cannot coincide with a redirecting branch in EX/MEM (a branch is not a
memory op), so stall_ex_mem never holds a redirect.

title: Predictor-directed 8-entry fetch queue re-stacked on the flop-regfile / registered-forward core
motivation:
Offline ISS replay of the timed CoreMark region (2.92M retired instructions, 4.578M cycles
on the champion) shows where cycles go: 54k BHT mispredicts + 13.7k JALR (all returns) cost
only ~68k cycles (1.5%), so RAS / gshare / bigger BHT are capped far below the 4.6% accept
bar and are NOT worth building. The big front-end loss is the 22% imem stall rate (~0.82M
cycles, 18%) which is NOT overlapped with the ~0.8M backend stall cycles (MUL busy 94k x 4 =
376k, load-use 204k, dmem 0.28 x 685k = 193k): while the backend is stalled the PC is frozen,
so fetch idles even though imem could deliver. The previous queue attempt (r3s2, depth 4) cut
cycles 4,578,311 -> 4,220,761 (-7.8%) at a 1.5% Fmax cost, but was built on the 63 MHz core;
the champion (76.8 MHz, r3s1) has never had it. A decoupled queue lets fetch run ahead during
those ~0.8M backend stall cycles and later cover imem-not-ready bubbles. Backend stalls are
bursty (MUL = 4-cycle busy bursts, dmem stall runs), so depth 8 should hide materially more
than depth 4; rough estimate (not simulated) is ~-10..-12% cycles vs the champion.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Decouple fetch from decode with an 8-entry circular queue of {instr, pc, pred_taken} on top
of the champion (keep the flop regfile, registered m1/m2 forward matches, direction-only EX
verify, JAL+BHT predecode and the registered BHT update unchanged).
1. if_stage: fetch PC advances on fetch_fire = imem_ready && (q_count != 8) and no longer
   freezes on load-use / dmem_stall / ex_busy. EX redirect still overrides everything and
   clears q_count/head/tail (control flops only; data entries are not reset, so the late
   redirect does not fan out to ~500 data flops). The tail slot is written every fetch_fire
   cycle; pop = q_nonempty && !stall_id.
2. Decode input mux: dec = q_nonempty ? entry[head] : {pc, imem_data, pred_taken} (bypass when
   the queue is empty, so a redirect target still reaches decode in the cycle it is fetched
   and the mispredict penalty stays 1 bubble). q_nonempty is a registered bit. A bypassed word
   that decode does not consume (stall_id) is pushed instead. To keep the head mux off the
   ID critical path store the entries as one-hot-pointer AND-OR (head pointer one-hot flops)
   rather than a binary 8:1 mux, and register rs1/rs2 fields of the head entry alongside it
   if the regfile-read path shows up in `make timing`.
3. hazard_unit / core: stall_if (PC hold) becomes "queue full or imem not ready";
   load-use compare, regfile read addresses and m1/m2 match logic take rs1/rs2 from the muxed
   decode word. flush_id / stall_id / stall_ex_mem / hold_mem_wb semantics are unchanged.
4. Log cycles and Fmax separately; if the head mux shows in the critical path drop to depth 4.

title: Take EX redirect off the IF->ID NOP mask: ID/EX data fields ignore redirect
motivation:
The logged r4s0 worst path (17.739 ns arrival, 38 cells, 13 levels) is
cpu/u_ex/reg_q.alu_result_2 -> cpu/u_id/reg_q.ctrl.mem_width_1 through
clock_ibuf > u_ex > u_if > u_id:
EX/MEM alu_result -> forward mux -> branch compare -> redirect -> if_stage NOP
mask on out.instr / out.valid / out.pred_taken -> decoder / imm_gen -> ID/EX
flops. The IF/ID NOP substitution still includes the late EX `redirect`
(flush = flush_if = redirect | imem_stall, plus a second `|| redirect` in
if_stage), so the redirect net fans out through a mask LUT into ~110 ID/EX
data flops and through the decoder into ctrl. That mask is redundant: on a
redirect cycle flush_id already synchronously clears ID/EX ctrl / valid /
pred_taken, and the ID/EX data fields (imm, rd, instr, rs addrs, operands)
of a bubble (valid=0, ctrl=0) have no architectural effect.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make the IF->ID NOP substitution depend only on imem_stall (a primary-input
handshake that arrives early), not on EX `redirect`:
  - hazard_unit: flush_if = imem_stall (drop `redirect`).
  - if_stage: out.instr / out.valid / out.pred_taken masked by `flush` only
    (drop the explicit `|| redirect`).
`redirect` is then used only by (a) the pc register mux and (b) flush_id,
which resets ID/EX ctrl, valid and pred_taken. The ID/EX data flops capture
the wrong-path word on a redirect cycle, but valid=0 and ctrl='0 (from
flush_id) make it a pure bubble: no reg_write, mem op, branch, jump, MDU op,
BHT update (bht_upd_en needs in.valid) or RVFI retirement. A stale reg_q.rd
is harmless because every consumer of it is gated by a registered reg_write /
mem_read bit that the flush cleared (forward AND ex_mem_w_en, load-use
id_ex_mem_read, m2 bypass wb_fwd_en). The imem_stall term is kept so a
non-delivered word never decodes into live ctrl (flush_id does not cover
imem_stall). Cycle behaviour is identical (no IPC change, same cycles and
same retirement stream); only the redirect fan-out and the decoder/imm cone
behind it are shortened (redirect no longer reaches mask LUTs -> decoder ->
ctrl D, imm_gen -> imm D, rd/instr/rs-addr D). Earlier history: r2s0's
mask removal gave ~+22% Fmax at identical iter/cycle when redirect was a
19-level cone; the redirect loop is still the Fmax-setting group.

title: Registered MEM-stage redirect (target in EX/MEM flops) stacked on the late-bypass champion
motivation:
The r4s0 champion (196.95, 90.2 MHz) has its worst path ending in a u_id
ctrl flop: ex_mem.alu_result -> forward mux -> 32-bit compare -> branch_cond
mux -> redirect XOR -> if_stage NOP mask / flush_id / pc CE fan-out -> decoder
-> ID/EX ctrl D (38 cells). That same-cycle resolve->squash loop is a
structural property of resolving the redirect in EX and consuming it combinationally
in IF/ID. r4s1 (MEM-stage redirect + AGU + one-hot ALU) cost only +1.5% cycles
(4578311 -> 4647246, i.e. one extra bubble per mispredict/JALR) and
still beat r3s1 by +7.15% on the old core, but it never got stacked on the
r4s0 bypass retiming, which removed the m2 forward leg that was r4s1's new worst
path. Because the timed netlist drops RVFI-only logic (pc_next, branch_taken,
branch_target regs), the redirect can be carried as one flop plus a target
register that exists only for the PC mux.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Resolve branches/JALR in EX exactly as now, but only REGISTER the result:
EX/MEM gains `redirect` (= actual_taken ^ pred_taken, already gated by
misalign suppression; killed on bubbles / ex_busy) and `redirect_target`
(= pred_taken ? pc+4 : is_jump ? jump_target : branch_target; no dependence on
the compare result, only on flops and the jalr adder). IF's PC mux, flush_if,
flush_id and the squash of the one wrong-path instruction now sitting in EX
are driven by `redirect_m = ex_mem.valid & ex_mem.redirect`, a flop output.
While redirect_m is high: EX/MEM captures a bubble (valid=0, ctrl=0,
redirect=0), bht_upd_en and the MDU start are gated off for the op in EX, ID/EX
captures a bubble, IF emits NOP, and PC <= ex_mem.redirect_target. A redirecting
op is never a memory op or an M-op, so stall_ex_mem / ex_busy cannot coincide
with redirect_m (same argument as r4s1). The BHT training bundle is still
taken from EX (branch_taken ends at the 9 training flops, unchanged).

r4s1. The new tail of the compare / jalr-adder cones is one flop D pin instead of a
fan-out of ~100 loads (PC CE, flush nets, ID/EX ctrl/valid, NOP mask), taking the
~4.6 ns of redirect fan-out/route off the 11 ns cycle. To keep the next limiter
from simply being the ALU cone (the BSRAM-address path was tied with the
redirect path before r4s0), also (a) add a dedicated EX/MEM `mem_addr` register
(rs1_fwd + imm, shared with jalr_sum) that alone feeds dmem_addr/byte mask/
misalign/load align so Gowin absorbs only that register into the BSRAM address
port and the ALU-op result mux / MDU mux / PC+4 mux leave the BSRAM setup cone,
and (b) turn the 5-bit alu_op case into one-hot select flops decoded in ID
(sel_add/sub, sel_logic, sel_slt, sel_shift, sel_lui, sel_mdu, sel_pc4) so the
ALU result is a 2-level AND-OR. Retirement stream, RVFI fields, traps and CoreMark
CRCs are unchanged (wrong-path ops are killed before EX/MEM). Expected:
Fmax 90 -> ~105 MHz (+16%) against ~-1.5% iter/cycle.

title: Depth-2 predictor-steered fetch skid FIFO that also takes EX redirect off the decoder cone
motivation:
The IF-stage JAL+BHT predictor already makes the mispredict penalty 1 cycle,
so a better direction predictor or a RAS is worth only ~1-3% of cycles (CoreMark
branches ~18% of instrs, mispredicts ~10%, JALR ~2%), below the 4.6% acceptance
bar. The only large IPC term left in the front end is the ~22% imem backpressure:
when decode stalls (load-use, dmem stall, MDU busy) the PC holds and the word the
bus did deliver that cycle is thrown away and re-fetched, so a stall on the back
side becomes a second bubble on the fetch side. Prior fetch queues (r3s2 depth 4,
r4s2 depth 8) cut cycles 4,578,311 -> 4,220,761 (-7.8%, identical for depth 4 and 8,
so the benefit saturates at a very small depth) but lost Fmax: r3s2 -1.5%, r4s2
-6%, because they replaced the raw imem rs1/rs2 feed and kept `redirect` in the
IF/ID NOP mask. The current worst path (r4s0) is exactly that redirect cone:
ex_mem.alu_result -> fwd mux -> 32-bit compare -> redirect -> if_stage instr NOP
mask (u_if) -> decoder -> ID/EX ctrl flops (u_id), 38 cells / 17.7 ns. A fetch
FIFO is the natural place to cut that loop because validity is carried by flops.

-6%, because they replaced the raw imem rs1/rs2 feed and kept `redirect` in the
IF/ID NOP mask. The current worst path (r4s0) is exactly that redirect cone:

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a 2-entry flat-flop fetch skid FIFO (NOT a RAM array, no reset on data
entries, only the 2-bit count / 1-bit head valid flops are reset) between the
BHT/JAL-predicted PC and the ID stage. Entry = {pc, instr, pred_taken}. Rules:
(1) Decode input = q_nonempty ? head : imem_data, where q_nonempty is a flop
(one 2:1 LUT level, select straight from a flop); bypass keeps the zero-bubble
fetch->decode path and the 1-cycle mispredict penalty. (2) The PC advances whenever
the FIFO has room after this cycle's pop (count < 2 || take), where `take` =
!stall_id; the fetched word is enqueued when decode did not take it (stall) or
when the head is occupied; a delivered word on an empty FIFO with decode taking is
pure bypass and is not enqueued. This is the only IPC gain mechanism: a 1-3 cycle
decode stall no longer discards the word fetched during it, and a later imem stall
is covered by the buffered word. (3) `redirect` only clears the FIFO count / valid
flops and loads pc (so the stale head and the in-flight fetched word die) and still
forces ID/EX ctrl/valid/pred_taken to 0 through flush_id. (4) Cut `redirect` out of
the instruction NOP substitution entirely: ID decodes the unmasked head/imem word,
and ID/EX ctrl, valid and pred_taken are cleared by (flush_id || !deliver) where
deliver = q_nonempty || imem_ready; the decoder/imm_gen/rd/instr data flops are
don't-care on a bubble (ctrl=0, valid=0 means no side effects, same argument the
design already uses for the ID/EX data flops). This removes redirect -> mask ->
decoder (3-4 LUT levels) from the worst path group. (5) Regfile read addresses,
load-use compare and the alu operand pre-select must still use the 5-bit fields
of the *selected* word through a single 2:1 mux (head rs1/rs2 kept as dedicated
registered copies hd_rs1/hd_rs2 so the mux inputs are flops), not the multi-way
queue-head mux; the late MEM-result bypass into ID/EX rs?_val from r4s0 stays
untouched. BHT/JAL prediction is unchanged and runs on the freshly fetched word
(not on the head), so predicted-taken fetch stays zero-bubble; pred_taken is
stored with the entry and carried to ID/EX; the EX direction-only verify and the
registered BHT training are unchanged. Depth 2 is chosen because depth 4 and 8
gave identical cycle counts in r3s2/r4s2 (the FIFO rarely holds more than 2 words
at a 0.78 fetch / 1.0 drain rate) and because it keeps the head mux off the
critical cone. Expected: cycles -6..-8% (about 4.22-4.30M vs 4.578M) and Fmax
flat-to-up (+0..+8%) from removing the redirect->decoder cone, minus ~1-2% for
the head mux; net about +7% on the 196.95 champion.

title: Flat 2-level AND-OR load writeback: EX-precomputed lane/sign one-hot flops for the dmem->ID bypass
motivation:
The r5s1 champion (214.50, 99.685 MHz) logs its worst path as the dmem
BSRAM output (dmem_3_dmem_3_0_0_s, unregistered tCOO, the EX/MEM mem_addr
flop is absorbed as the BSRAM address register) -> cpu/u_mem -> cpu/u_id
rs1_val_28: 7 logic cells, arrival 15.553 ns with slack -5.259 against the
5 ns constraint (1/(5+5.259) = 97.47 MHz = seed 0; the median seed is 99.685).
Those 7 cells are, in order: the addr[1:0]*8 byte-lane mux of `shifted`,
the byte/half sign pick, the width/sext case, the mem_to_reg mux, the ID m2
bypass mux (m2 & wb_fwd_en), the alu_a / alu_b pre-select mux (is_auipc,
alu_src), then the ID/EX flop. The BSRAM output is by far the latest
arriving signal in that cone (~5 ns of the ~10 ns data path), but every
select in it (mem_addr[1:0], mem_width, mem_sext, mem_to_reg, misalign,
m2 match, raw_is_auipc/alu_src) is early, flop-derived and known a whole
cycle ahead. The synthesizer builds the cone as a serial case/mux chain in
source order instead of putting the late data input last. wb_fwd_data[i]
additionally has ~37 loads (31 regfile D pins, rs1/rs2/alu_a/alu_b ID/EX
muxes, MEM/WB wb_data), so every extra level on it also pays high-fanout
routing.

Make the late dmem read data enter a flat AND-OR whose selects are all
precomputed flops, so BSRAM out -> ID/EX operand flop is 2 LUT levels
instead of 7. Cycle behaviour is bit-identical (cycle-exact retiming), so
iter/cycle is unchanged and the whole gain is Fmax.

     - wb_alu_sel      : result = alu_result (not a load, or load with
                         misalign trap -> irrelevant)
     - ld0[3:0]        : one-hot lane feeding result bits [7:0]
                         (lane = addr[1:0] for LB/LH, 0 for LW)
     - ld1_l1, ld1_l3  : result bits [15:8] from lane 1 (LW, LH addr[1]=0)
                         or lane 3 (LH addr[1]=1)
     - ldw2, ldw3      : LW only: result bits [23:16] <- lane 2,
                         [31:24] <- lane 3
     - fill1[3:0]      : one-hot sign-bit position (rdata bit 7/15/23/31)
                         for result bits [15:8], set for LB with sext only
     - fill2[3:0]      : same one-hot, for result bits [31:16], set for
                         sext LB / LH
     - wb_en           : reg_write && !misalign (replaces the MEM-stage
                         ctrl_with_trap-derived wb_fwd_en on the bypass /
                         regfile-write enable path; the RVFI ctrl/trap copy
                         in MEM stays as is)
2. MEM (mem_stage.sv): wb_fwd_data is written as a balanced AND-OR with
   those flops as the AND terms, e.g. bits [7:0]:
     P0 = (ld0[0] & r[7:0])   | (ld0[1] & r[15:8])
     P1 = (ld0[2] & r[23:16]) | (ld0[3] & r[31:24])
     wb_fwd_data[7:0] = P0 | P1 | (wb_alu_sel & alu_result[7:0])
   and similarly for [15:8] (two lane terms + fill1-gated 4-way sign term
   + alu term), [23:16] and [31:24] (word lane term + fill2-gated sign
   term + alu term). The load-alignment `shifted` barrel shifter and the
   width/sext case are gone from the timed path (still computed for the
   RVFI-only mem_rdata/read_data copies, which synthesis prunes).
3. ID (id_stage.sv): fold the m2 bypass and the alu_a/alu_b pre-select into
   the same AND-OR so the late term sees one LUT4 level. With
   sel = m2_rsX_d & wb_en (early) and early term
   E = sel ? (wb_alu_sel & alu_result) : <non-bypass operand>, the flop D
   is (sel & P0) | (sel & P1) | E, i.e. 4 inputs (sel, P0, P1, E): one
   LUT4. Do this for rs1_val_d, rs2_val_d, alu_a_val_d (non-bypass operand
   = is_auipc ? pc : rf data, sel also & !is_auipc) and alu_b_val_d
   (non-bypass operand = alu_src ? imm : rf data, sel also & !alu_src).
   P0/P1 are produced once in mem_stage and exported so all four
   destinations share them; the regfile write data (fanout 31) uses its own
   OR of P0|P1|alu term.
The path becomes BSRAM tCOO -> LUT4 (P) -> LUT4 (D) -> flop. Expected
removal of about 4-5 logic cells (about 4-5 ns of routed delay) from the
current worst cone. The risk is that the next near-tied cone (EX forward
mux -> adder/compare -> result mux, redirect target/flops) then limits Fmax,
so the realised gain may be smaller than the cone shortening; ~+6% is the
expected net, just above the 4.6% acceptance bar. Correctness: purely a
re-encoding of the existing load extract; for misaligned loads reg_write is
cleared in both formulations so the don't-care lane choice is never used
(ld0 for word loads is lane 0 only when addr[1:0]==0). Formal ALTOPS /
cosim exercise LB/LBU/LH/LHU/LW at every offset in CoreMark and selftest.

title: Late-arrival load lane: dmem BSRAM data enters ID operand capture via a 3-level one-hot AND-OR, regfile written from WB flops
motivation:
The r5s1 champion (214.50, 99.685 MHz, 4,647,246 cycles) logs its worst path
as dmem_3 BSRAM (dmem_3_dmem_3_0_0_s) -> cpu/u_mem -> cpu/u_id
reg_q.rs1_val_28: 15.553 ns arrival, only 7 logic cells. Every other group the
earlier retimings chased (EX redirect cone, forward mux, regfile read) now ends
in flops with 5-6 early levels; this one is different because its START point
is the BSRAM data output (tCO ~5+ ns, the latest-arriving signal in the core)
and the RTL puts that signal at the BOTTOM of a serial cone:
  dmem_rdata -> byte shift by mem_addr[1:0] -> width/sext case ->
  mem_to_reg mux (wb_fwd_data) -> `m2 && wb_fwd_en` bypass mux (rs?_val_d) ->
  is_auipc / alu_src operand pre-select (alu_a/b_val_d) -> ID/EX D.
All of the select inputs of those muxes (ex_mem.mem_addr[1:0], mem_width,
mem_sext, mem_to_reg, reg_write, raw imem fields, m2 compare) come from flops
and are ready ~3 ns after the clock edge, i.e. ~2-3 ns BEFORE the BSRAM data,
but the LUT mapper does not know arrival times and keeps the serial mux chain
with the late signal entering at the first level. wb_fwd_data additionally
fans out to the 31 regfile write ports (rf_w_data), the MEM/WB wb_data flop and
four ID bypass muxes, which adds routing delay to the same late net.
So this is a structural problem (where in the cone the late signal enters and
how far it fans out), not an operator-level one, and it is worth ~4-5 ns
of a 15.5 ns path while leaving cycles unchanged.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Restructure the load-data -> ID capture path so the BSRAM output passes through
at most 3 LUT levels (shift/sext one-hot AND-OR, then one final merge) and its
fan-out is cut to a few loads. Cycle behaviour stays bit-for-bit identical
(same bypass coverage, same load-use stall, same retirement stream), so
iter/cycle is unchanged and the whole gain is Fmax.

1. mem_stage.sv: build the aligned/extended load value as a flat one-hot
   AND-OR, not nested case/shift. From flops only (in.mem_addr[1:0],
   in.ctrl.mem_width, in.ctrl.mem_sext) precompute one-hot select terms:
   for result bits [7:0]: lane0..lane3 selects (word and half@0 use lane0,
   half@2 uses lane2 for its low byte, byte@k uses lane k); for bits [15:8]:
   sel_b1 (word / half@0 -> dmem_rdata[15:8]) and sel_b3 (half@2 ->
   dmem_rdata[31:24]) plus the sign-fill selects; for bits [31:16]: word select
   on dmem_rdata[31:16] and sign-fill selects folded per source sign bit
   (dmem_rdata[7], [15], [23], [31], with byte@1 and half@0 merged on bit 15,
   byte@3 and half@2 merged on bit 31 as one precomputed select each). The
   result is `ld_data` = OR of (select & dmem_rdata bit) terms; the sign-fill
   is expanded per bit rather than computed once and fanned out, so no bit sits
   behind a 2-level sign mux. Export new outputs `ld_data` (32b, unconditioned
   aligned load), `ld_hit` (= mem_to_reg && reg_write-after-misalign-clear,
   flop-derived) and `alu_fwd_hit` (= !mem_to_reg && reg_write-after-clear);
   keep the existing wb_fwd_data / wb_fwd_en ports (wb_fwd_data = ld_hit ?
   ld_data : in.alu_result) so MEM/WB.wb_data and any unit test are unchanged.

2. id_stage.sv: split every captured bypass operand into an early term and a
   late term. With hit_ld_x = m2_rsX_d && ld_hit and hit_alu_x = m2_rsX_d &&
   alu_fwd_hit (both flop/imem-field derived, early):
     early_rsX = hit_alu_x ? ex_mem.alu_result : (hit_ld_x ? 0 : rf_rsX_data)
     rsX_val_d = early_rsX | ({32{hit_ld_x}} & ld_data)
   and for the pre-selected ALU operands fold the auipc / alu_src select into
   both halves so the late term sees one AND and one OR only:
     alu_a_val_d = (raw_is_auipc ? in.pc : early_rs1)
                   | ({32{hit_ld_1 && !raw_is_auipc}} & ld_data)
     alu_b_val_d = (raw_alu_src ? raw_imm : early_rs2)
                   | ({32{hit_ld_2 && !raw_alu_src}} & ld_data)
   So the BSRAM data crosses: lane AND-OR (2 levels) + final AND-OR (1 level)
   = ~3 cells, down from 7. ex_mem.alu_result is passed in as a new id_stage
   input (it is a flop, early) so the MEM-stage alu bypass no longer goes
   through wb_fwd_data.

3. core.sv / reg_file: stop writing the regfile from the MEM stage. Write it
   from the WB stage using the existing wb_w_en / wb_w_addr / wb_w_data
   (MEM/WB flops: reg_write && valid, rd, wb_data), and instantiate
   reg_file with BYPASS(1) so the same-cycle WB write is bypassed to the ID
   read ports (write-first). That bypass is an early term (flop -> 2 levels)
   merged into rf_rsX_data before the late-term OR above. This removes the
   BSRAM->load-align->31-way regfile write-enable/data fan-out, which the
   serial rf_w_data net currently adds on top of the ID path, and replaces it
   with a flop-sourced write bus. Coverage is unchanged: producer in MEM ->
   m2 bypass; producer in WB -> regfile bypass; older -> regfile contents.
   hold_mem_wb already clears MEM/WB.valid, so a dmem-stalled cycle cannot
   double-write.

Everything else (hazard unit, forward_unit, EX/MEM redirect registers,
BHT, MDU, one-hot ALU selects) is untouched, so the only timing change is on
paths that start at the BSRAM output or at the regfile write bus.
Expected: worst BSRAM->ID path from ~15.5 ns to ~11-12 ns; the next group
(EX forward mux -> adder/compare -> ALU result mux, ~12-13 ns by the r5s1
lesson) becomes the limiter, so I project ~+8% Fmax, no IPC change. Logs should
record Fmax, cycles and the new worst path separately.

title: BHT-steered 2-entry fetch-ahead FIFO on the registered-redirect core (conservative cnt-only accept, no late signals in PC enable)
motivation:
Offline ISS replay of the CoreMark timed window (10 iterations, 2.92M retired
instructions, ~4.65M cycles at the 214.5 champion) shows how little is left for
a pure direction/target predictor: 529,588 conditional branches, 294k taken,
~50.5k mispredicts with the current 128x2-bit bimodal BHT (update delayed 3
branches), 13,735 JALR that are ALL returns (a 4-entry RAS would hit 13,723 of
them), 49,367 JAL (already zero-bubble). At 3 cycles per redirect that is
(50.5k + 13.7k) x 3 = ~193k cycles = 4.1% of all cycles even for a PERFECT
predictor; a 512-entry BHT only removes 10.6k mispredicts (0.7%) and a RAS only
0.9%, so neither can clear the +4.6% acceptance bar. gshare is no better than
bimodal here (41.4k at 1K entries, hist 4; worse for longer history), the
CoreMark branches are data dependent.
The big, predictor-addressable loss is elsewhere: bench_stall_gen drives imem_ready
from a per-cycle xorshift (78.1% accept), independent of the address, so fetch
alone bounds the run at 2.92M / 0.78 = 3.74M cycles, yet the core takes 4.65M.
The ~0.9M extra cycles are cycles where the back end stalls (dmem stall, load-use,
MDU busy: stall_if freezes PC) while a delivered imem word is simply discarded and
must be re-fetched with another 22% chance of a stall. A fetch-ahead FIFO that the
BHT/JAL predictor keeps steering (so it holds the predicted path) converts those
discarded deliveries into banked instructions. Earlier queue attempts (r3s2 depth 4
+6.8%, r4s2 depth 8 +1.7%, r5s2 depth 2 +2.5%) all lost Fmax because the EX
`redirect` was still a combinational fan-out into the queue/ID cone, and r5s2's
LESSON says to stop retrying until the redirect is registered. It is now a flop
(EX/MEM.redirect, r5s1), so the queue flush is a flop -> clear-enable and that
objection is gone. This retry is designed around the remaining Fmax risks.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a 2-entry fetch-ahead FIFO between the imem word and ID, steered by the existing
IF predictor (JAL always taken, branch via bht[pc[8:2]][1], pred_taken carried with the
word). Keep everything the lessons say is Fmax-critical untouched: the raw
io_imemData[19:15]/[24:20] feed of the regfile read and load-use compare is only
replaced by a 2:1 mux whose select is a flop (q non-empty), the registered redirect
loop stays, and no wide compare or late signal is added to the PC enable.

1. if_stage.sv: keep the fetch PC `pc`, the BHT, the predecode of the live imem word
   and next_pc = pred_hit ? pred_target : pc + 4 exactly as today. New state: two
   queue entries {pc[31:2], instr[31:0], pred_taken} plus a 2-bit count / head
   pointer, all flops. Fetch ACCEPT is conservative and timing-safe:
       accept = imem_ready && !redirect && (cnt != 2)
   (cnt is a flop; it deliberately ignores a same-cycle pop so the late
   load-use / dmem_stall / ex_busy signals never reach the PC enable). pc <= next_pc
   iff accept; redirect still overrides: pc <= redirect_target, cnt <= 0, entries
   invalidated (flop clear-enable from the EX/MEM redirect flop).
2. Decode source: if cnt != 0, ID decodes the head entry (instr/pc/pred_taken from
   flops); otherwise it decodes the live word (valid = imem_ready && !redirect, pred
   bits as today). The same source's rs1/rs2 fields feed the regfile read addresses,
   the hazard load-use compare and the m1/m2 forward matches (mux select = cnt != 0, a
   flop, so +1 LUT level only on the imem_data -> regfile-address cone, and the
   imem word in the timed netlist comes from LFSR flops so it has no extra arrival
   skew). raw_imm / raw_is_auipc / raw_alu_src in id_stage must be taken from the same
   muxed word (they are already derived from `raw_instr`).
3. Consume/produce: ID consumes (pops the head, or takes the live word) iff
   !stall_id, where stall_id = dmem_stall || load_use || ex_busy as today (imem_stall is
   removed from it: a missing word is simply a bubble with valid=0 into ID/EX). If ID
   does NOT consume and a word is delivered (live word accepted by `accept`), that
   word is pushed onto the tail (this is the banked "skid" that today is thrown away
   and re-fetched). If cnt==0 and ID consumes the live word, nothing is pushed. A word
   is pushed only when accept=1, so the FIFO never overflows and the predicted pc
   advance and the push are always paired.
4. hazard_unit.sv: stall_if (PC hold) is replaced by the cnt-based accept above;
   stall_id loses imem_stall; flush_id = redirect || (load_use && !(dmem_stall ||
   ex_busy)) || !word_valid-style bubble is handled through `valid`, not ctrl flush
   (keep the existing "flush only clears valid/ctrl/pred_taken, not the wide data
