title: Pre-merged EX forward-select flops (m1 & reg_write registered as one bit) to drop the AND level and flop->LUT->fanout-32 head off the EX critical loop
motivation:
The r6s2 champion (228.10, 99.52 MHz, 4,362,927 cycles) logs its worst path as
cpu/u_id/reg_q.m1_alu_a -> cpu/u_ex/u_alu -> cpu/u_ex/reg_q.alu_result_15:
10 logic cells, 15.909 ns. The START point is the registered forward-match
flop m1_alu_a. forward_unit ANDs it with the EX/MEM.ctrl.reg_write flop
(fwd_alu_a = m1_alu_a && ex_mem_w_en) and the result then fans out to 32
2:1 operand muxes (and the same happens for fwd_alu_b, fwd_rs1, fwd_rs2).
So every EX path that starts at a select goes flop -> 1 LUT (AND) -> fan-out
~32 net -> operand mux -> adder / shifter / compare -> result mux, while the
paths that start at the data input of the same mux (EX/MEM.alu_result flop)
skip the AND LUT. Earlier retimings (r2s1 registered m1 matches, r4s0 folded
the auipc/alu_src select into m1_alu_*) each moved Fmax by moving compare
logic across the ID/EX boundary, and this last AND is the only logic left
between the select flop and the mux. It is a pure retiming: IPC identical,
cycles must stay exactly 4,362,927.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Register the forward SELECT itself instead of its two factors. Add four flops
(sel_alu_a_q, sel_alu_b_q, sel_rs1_q, sel_rs2_q) in ex_stage whose value is,
at every cycle, exactly (id_ex.m1_X && ex_mem.ctrl.reg_write); the muxes in
EX then use the flop output directly (flop -> fan-out -> mux, no AND LUT).
Next-state, derived from the same terms that already feed the two source flops:
  - dmem_stall (stall_ex_mem): hold (ID/EX m1 and EX/MEM.reg_write both hold).
  - ex_busy || redirect_m: 0 (EX/MEM captures a bubble, reg_write = 0).
  - otherwise: m1_X_d && ctrl_with_trap.reg_write, where m1_X_d is the
    already-existing ID-stage next-state of the m1 flop (exported from
    id_stage as an output) and ctrl_with_trap.reg_write is the same D value
    EX/MEM.ctrl.reg_write takes (includes the misalign-jump clear, so a
    trapped JAL/JALR still does not forward its link value; branches have
    reg_write = 0 so need no special case). The one stale case (load-use:
    ID/EX m1 holds while ctrl is flushed) leaves a bubble in EX whose result
    is discarded, so the select value there is a don't-care (new flop uses
    m1_X_d; behaviour of valid ops is unchanged).
The old m1_* flops are kept only where still needed (m1_rs1/m1_rs2 are no
longer needed in EX; alu_a/alu_b selects are subsumed). forward_unit.sv
becomes a pass-through (or is deleted and the four flops live in ex_stage).

lesson: - 2026-10-02 hyp-20261002-001-r7s0 (regression, -3.80%): Folding the EX/MEM `reg_write` AND into four registered forward-select flops (`sel_*_q` = m1_*_d && reg_write, so the operand muxes start at a flop with no AND LUT) scored 219.43 vs 228.10, well outside the ~2% seed spread, so deleting the one LUT between the select flop and its fan-out-32 net did not pay and most likely cost more than it saved because the AND just moved to the flop D side, where each select now merges the ID compare cone (`m1_*_d`) with late EX terms (dmem `stall_ex_mem` hold, `ex_busy`/`redirect_m` clear, and `ctrl_with_trap.reg_write` through the misalign check on late `jalr_sum[1:0]`) in a hold/clear mux deeper than the reg_write flop's own D path (inferred; the post-change worst path and cycles/Fmax were not logged); a retiming that merges two flop factors into one must be checked against the D-side fan-in of every term it absorbs, not just the Q-side path it shortens, and the next try at the select fan-out should keep the factors as separate flops and duplicate the select (`syn_preserve`) instead.

title: Two-cycle MUL fast path: DSP products straight from ID/EX operand flops, low-word sum released into EX/MEM without a result register
motivation:
Cycle accounting from experiments/log.jsonl: moving M-ops into the multi-cycle MDU (r1s1)
took the core from 4,491,485 to 4,868,540 CoreMark cycles (+377k per 10 iterations, +8.4%).
Fmax was the right trade then, but the MDU is still the largest single IPC leak left. A MUL
currently occupies EX for 5 cycles (E0 operand capture, E1 DSP partial products, E2 mid add,
E3 final sum into `result`, E4 release via res_valid), i.e. +4 stall cycles. CoreMark's matrix
kernels issue ~8k MULs per iteration, which matches ~4 cycles x 8.4k = ~34k cycles per
iteration = ~7.7% of the 436k cycles/iteration (4,362,927 / 10). DIV/REM is only ~10% of the
MDU overhead. Every other cycle sink (22% imem stalls, load-use, mispredict, dmem stalls) has
already been attacked by structural work or is a predictor/memory change; the MUL latency is
untouched and independent of the near-tied EX / MEM->ID Fmax cones, which is why the last
four Fmax-retiming attempts (r6s0, r6s1 and the r5/r6 bundles) stopped paying.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Cut the common MUL (low word) from +4 to +1 stall cycles, and the forward-dependent case from
+4 to +2, without putting anything new on the EX forward loop or the MEM->ID bypass cone.

1. DSP stage fed from flops. In the op's first EX cycle (mdu state IDLE) the four 17x17
   products are computed from the ID/EX operand flops (`in.rs1_val` / `in.rs2_val`, which
   already contain the MEM->ID late bypass) instead of the captured a_q/b_q, via a 2:1 mux
   controlled by `state == S_IDLE` (flop). The pp_* flops become free-running (gated only by
   !stall). The DSP input cone stays flop -> LUT -> DSP, no forward mux in front of it.
   The existing a_q/b_q/op_q capture stays in that same first cycle (RVFI rs1/rs2 rdata and
   the sign-select for the sum use it).
2. Forward-dependent M-ops (fwd_rs1_sel | fwd_rs2_sel high in E0: operand is the result of
   the instruction immediately ahead, only present on the EX/MEM forward leg for one cycle)
   take a slow path: E0 captures a_q/b_q, state -> S_MUL1, DSP runs off a_q/b_q in E1, then
   release (+2 stall cycles instead of +4). ex_stage passes a new `fwd_hit` and the ID/EX
   operand flops to the MDU.
3. Direct release for MUL (low word). In the release cycle E1, `mdu_result` for op MUL is the
   32-bit three-term sum `pp_ll[31:0] + ((pp_lh[15:0] + pp_hl[15:0]) << 16)` computed
   combinationally from the pp flops and fed through the existing sel_mdu AND-OR into
   EX/MEM.alu_result; res_valid is raised at the end of E0 so there is no `result`-register
   cycle. This cone is flop -> 32-bit carry chain -> mux -> AND-OR -> flop (~6-7 ns), well
   under the current ~10 ns period. `mdu_result` becomes
   `is_mul_low_q ? mul_low_sum : result_q` (one registered select).
4. MULH / MULHSU / MULHU and DIV/REM keep today's registered `result` path after the DSP
   stage (MULH: E0 DSP, E1 mid, E2 64-bit sum into `result`, E3 release = one cycle faster
   than today because E0 now does the DSP stage and there is no separate capture cycle for
   the fast case). Neither is common in CoreMark; keeping the 64-bit sum off the release
   cycle keeps the worst new cone short. DIV/REM sequencer untouched.
5. RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS branch keeps the 2-cycle handshake it has now (one capture/compute
   cycle then res_valid); only the real branch is restructured. The cocotb MDU/ALU tests that
   assume fixed latencies must be updated to wait on busy/res_valid instead.

Expected effect: ~7.7% of cycles are MUL stalls today; the fast path removes 3 of 4 of them
for non-forward-dependent MULs (most matrix MULs read freshly loaded operands that reach
ID/EX through the m2 bypass, i.e. no m1 forward) and 2 of 4 for forward-dependent ones,
so ~5-6% fewer CoreMark cycles at unchanged Fmax. DSP count stays 3-4, LUT/FF change is
small (pp flops already exist). If `make timing` shows the new `pp -> sum -> alu_result`
cone or the DSP input mux as the worst path, fall back to registering the low-word sum
(3-cycle MUL: +2 stalls, ~3% gain) rather than adding logic to the EX forward cone.

lesson: - 2026-10-02 hyp-20261002-002-r7s1 (improvement, +4.78%): Cutting the common MUL from +4 to +1 stall cycles (DSP 17x17 products read from the ID/EX `rs1_val`/`rs2_val` flops in E0 via a flop-selected `state == S_IDLE` mux, free-running `pp_*` flops, low-word sum `pp_ll + ((pp_lh + pp_hl) << 16)` released combinationally into EX/MEM with no `result` register, forward-dependent M-ops sent down a +2 slow path via `fwd_hit`) scored 239.01 vs 228.10, in line with the ~5% predicted from the per-op cycle accounting in experiments/log.jsonl (~8k MULs x 4 stalls ~ 7.7% of cycles), so Fmax most likely held flat (inferred, cycles and Fmax were not logged separately); the cycle-exact IPC lever worked because every new cone stayed flop -> short logic -> flop (the DSP inputs and the 32-bit carry chain stay under the period) and nothing was added to the near-tied EX forward / MEM->ID bypass cones, so when retimings stop paying, size remaining multi-cycle-op stall leaks from per-op cycle counts and fix them in the unit's own flops rather than in the forward network.

title: XOR-folded BHT index (free 25% fewer mispredicts) plus flop-only 4-entry return stack
motivation:
An offline ISS replay of the timed CoreMark region (2.922M retired instrs, 4.363M
cycles, 529,588 conditional branches, 13,735 JAL calls, 13,735 `ret`s, 0 other JALRs)
quantifies what is left for a predictor. The current 128x2 bimodal BHT indexed by
pc[8:2] mispredicts 54,452 of 529,588 branches (10.3%), mostly from aliasing: the same
trace gives 44.3K at 256 entries, 39.8K at 512 and 39.6K at 1024, so conflicts, not
capacity of the history, are the problem. XOR-folding higher pc bits into the same 7
index bits (idx[k] = pc[k+2] ^ pc[k+7]) takes the SAME 128 entries to 40.7K (-25%) with
no storage. History-based schemes do not help this workload: gshare 8-10 bits is
worse than bimodal (50-61K), concat-history 39.8K, a 9-bit tournament 38.9K, so
direction accuracy saturates near 39-40K (data-dependent branches) and no bigger
predictor is worth its area. Separately every `ret` (13,735 = 100% of JALRs) is never
predicted and always costs a registered-redirect bubble; a 4-entry return stack matches
13,723 of them (99.9%) in the replay.
Honest ceiling: ~14K fewer branch redirects + ~13.7K fewer return redirects at about
2-3 cycles each = ~55-80K of 4.36M cycles, i.e. +1.3-1.9% iter/cycle. That is the whole
remaining predictor budget on this core, so Fmax must be held flat.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Part 1 (primary, zero logic cost): in if_stage replace the BHT read index pc[8:2] with
the folded index h(p) = p[6:0] ^ p[11:5] where p = pc[13:2] (idx[k] = pc[k+2] ^ pc[k+7],
k=0..6), and apply the SAME fold to the training index in ex_stage (bht_upd_idx =
fold(in.pc)), which is registered into upd_idx_q anyway. Storage, counter policy, reset
value (2'b01) and the update path are unchanged. The replay says 54.4K -> 40.7K
mispredicts for this exact fold (xor>>5 on the word index); xor>>6 gives 40.7K too,
xor>>8 41.5K, so the choice is robust. Only a 2-input XOR is added between the pc flops
and the 128:1 read mux, and between in.pc flops and upd_idx_q.
Part 2 (secondary): add a 4-entry circular return-address stack of flops in if_stage.
The canonical `ret` word (imem_data == 32'h00008067) is predicted taken with target =
RAS top (flop); a `jal` with rd=x1 pushes pc+4 when its word is accepted; an accepted
predicted ret pops. Wrong-path pollution is tolerated (accuracy only). Verification
keeps to equality logic: because the predicted ret has imm==0, its target is rs1, so EX
checks `rs1_fwd == pending_target` with one 32-bit equality compare parallel to the
existing cmp_eq. The predicted target travels in a 2-entry in-order pending-target

enable.

new path near the worst path in `make timing`, drop it, since its ~0.7-0.9% gain is
smaller than the place-and-route seed spread.

title: Fetch the redirect target in the redirect cycle (imem_addr muxed from the EX/MEM redirect flop)
motivation:
Offline ISS replay of the CoreMark ELF (2.94M instrs) shows the core is
already within ~9% of its imem-bandwidth bound (2.92M words / 0.78 ready =
3.74M cycles vs 4.13M measured). The remaining leaks are small: 55k BHT
mispredicts + 13.8k JALR returns = ~69k redirects, each costing 2 lost fetch
cycles because the registered redirect is only visible in MEM and PC loads the
target at the END of that cycle, so the target word is fetched one cycle later
than it has to be. Bigger BHT (512 entries: -15k mispredicts, ~0.7%), gshare
(worse than bimodal here), RAS (13.8k returns, ~0.7%) and deeper FIFOs are each
only ~1% and cost IF-cone logic. The redirect flop is already available at the
start of the redirect cycle, so the target can be driven onto imem_addr in
that same cycle with a single LUT mux on an output path, saving 1 of the 2
penalty cycles on all ~69k redirects (~1.7% of 4.13M cycles, deterministic).

hypothesis.hypothesis:
In if_stage drive `imem_addr = redirect ? redirect_target : pc` (both flops).
In the redirect cycle the live imem word is the correct-path target word T and
is handed to ID directly (the old FIFO contents are wrong path and are dropped
as now):
  - raw_instr = (q_v0 && !redirect) ? q_in0 : imem_data; word_avail =
    (q_v0 && !redirect) || imem_ready; out.pc = redirect ? redirect_target :
    (q_v0 ? q_pc0 : pc); out.valid/out.instr are masked only by !word_avail
    (no longer by `redirect`).
  - pc update: if redirect && imem_ready -> pc <= redirect_target + 4 (T goes
    straight to ID, FIFO stays empty: q_v0/q_v1 cleared as now); if redirect &&
    !imem_ready -> pc <= redirect_target (unchanged behaviour); else as today.
    A 30-bit incrementer off the redirect_target flops is the only new logic.
  - Prediction of T is suppressed in the redirect cycle (pred_hit forced 0 /
    out.pred_taken = 0): EX still verifies direction, so a JAL / taken-biased
    branch sitting exactly on a redirect target just costs a normal mispredict
    (~10% of redirect targets, ~0.2 cycle each) and the BHT index / pred_target
    adder cones are untouched (no mux in front of them).
  - hazard_unit: flush_id no longer includes `redirect` (T must be captured by
    ID/EX); load_use_hazard is masked with !redirect (the op in EX is wrong
    path, its rd must not stall / bubble T; stall_id is then 0 in redirect
    cycles, so T is always consumed and never banked). ex_busy/dmem_stall
    already cannot coincide with redirect. flush_if = !word_avail only.
  - ex_stage is unchanged: the wrong-path op in EX is still squashed by
    redirect_m (EX/MEM bubble, no BHT training, MDU not started); T's stale m1
    match against that op is masked in EX by the bubble's registered
    reg_write=0, and its m2 bypass of the redirecting op's link value (JAL/JALR
    rd) already works through wb_fwd_data.

4.13M (~1.7%), minus ~0.2%/redirect for the suppressed prediction (~0.3%),

select as (q_v0 && !redirect) computed in parallel with the data inputs, or
drop q_v0 on redirect by also forcing q_v0 low one cycle earlier if timing
shows it.

title: Registered fetch stage + 64-word direct-mapped I-cache so fetch hits ignore the 22% imem stall
motivation:
Cycle accounting from the r7s1 / r6s2 log entries: 2.92M retired instructions in 4.128M cycles
(CPI 1.41). imem_ready is high 78.1% of cycles (bench_stall_gen: state[6:0] < 100), so the
ready-cycle budget is 0.781 * 4.128M = 3.22M. Words actually accepted by IF are the 2.92M
retired plus ~0.15M squashed wrong-path words, about 3.07M, i.e. ~95% of all ready cycles.
The core is therefore fetch-bandwidth-bound: one 32-bit word per ready cycle, and no queue
depth can beat that (depth 2/4/8 FIFOs only banked words during pipeline stalls and gave +6.3% /
+6.8% / +1.7%). The only way past the 0.78 words/cycle ceiling is to reuse words, i.e. not
need imem_ready for a fetch at all. CoreMark's hot code (crc, matrix, list find/sort, state
machine) is a few hundred instructions executed in tight loops, so a tiny word-granular
cache catches most fetches. Without the imem ceiling the remaining CPI is ~1.2 (dmem stalls,
load-use, redirects, MUL), a potential ~10-15% cycle cut, well above the 4.6% acceptance bar.
Cycle-exact retimings are exhausted (r6s0/r6s1/r7s0 all flat or negative), and this attacks
the one leak that is still ~15% of cycles.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add an instruction cache and make decode read only flops. Keep the IF/ID interface to ID
(if_id_t, dec_word, word_avail) and all ID/EX/MEM logic unchanged. Do not touch nret, the
RVFI path, or the decoder.

1. I-cache (new module rtl/icache.sv, instantiated in if_stage): 64 entries, direct-mapped,
   WORD granular (no line fill, no refill FSM). Index = pc[7:2], tag = pc[31:8] (full tag, so
   no aliasing even for symbolic PCs in riscv-formal), 1 valid flop per entry. Each entry
   stores the 32-bit word plus the two predecode bits is_jal / is_br (so the read data feeds
   the existing pred_target adder through at most the 64:1 read mux). Build it from explicit
   flops with (* syn_ramstyle = "registers" *) and a flat packed vector read through a plain
   mux, exactly like reg_file.sv, so Gowin cannot infer a BSRAM that absorbs the q_in flops
   (the r3s1 lesson). Reset clears only the valid flops. Write-through fill: whenever the
   live imem word is accepted (imem_ready && !redirect && !full && !hit) write
   {word, is_jal, is_br, tag, valid=1} at index pc[7:2]. Optional: clear all valid flops when
   a FENCE.I (opcode 0001111, funct3 001) is seen in ID, via one registered clear flop (not
   needed for CoreMark; keeps the cache architecturally correct).
2. Fetch word / fetch-ok: hit = valid[idx] && tag[idx] == pc[31:8] (pc flop -> small LUT
   compare, no late EX/MEM signal); f_word = hit ? c_word : imem_data; f_ok = hit ||
   imem_ready. accept = f_ok && !redirect && !q_v1 (still only flops + the imem handshake
   + the pc-only hit, so the PC-enable cone stays free of load-use / dmem_stall / ex_busy,
   as r6s2 required). Predecode (is_jal / is_br, imm, pc + imm, BHT[pc[8:2]][1]) runs on f_word
   (is_jal / is_br come straight from the stored bits on a hit), next_pc / pred_hit unchanged.
3. Registered IF/ID: remove the live-word bypass. ID always decodes the FIFO head, so
   raw_instr = q_in0, out.pc = {q_pc0, 2'b00}, out.pred_taken = q_pt0, word_avail = q_v0,
   flush_if = redirect || !q_v0. Words accepted with the queue empty or popping go into
   entry 0 (pop+push), a held head banks into entry 1, exactly the current 2-entry FIFO
   with the live-word mux deleted. This removes the `q_v0 ? q_in0 : imem_data` mux level from
   the worst path (cpu/u_if/q_in0 -> u_id/reg_q.alu_a_val, 9 cells in r7s1), so Fmax should
   hold or slightly improve, while the cache-read -> predecode -> pc loop is the only new
   cone. The price is one extra bubble per redirect (registered redirect now costs 3 instead
   of 2): ~50k mispredicts + 13.7k JALR + untaken-predicted ~ 70-80k extra cycles (~1.8%).
4. Hazard / ID interface: hazard_unit.sv and id_stage.sv ports are unchanged (dec_word is now
   q_in0; the load-use compare and regfile read address still come from flops, which is the
   property r2s0 / r4s2 / r5s2 showed must be preserved). core.sv wiring is unchanged except
   for the cache instance living inside if_stage.

Expected cycles: hits remove the imem-ready dependence for the loop bodies; at a ~85-90%
word hit rate the fetch ceiling disappears and cycles drop ~12-15%, minus ~2% for the extra
redirect bubble, net ~+10% iter/cycle. Area: ~64 x 59 flops = ~3.8k FF and ~1.3k LUT of read
mux/compare, well within the 20k-LUT budget; no DSP/BSRAM change. Risks and fallbacks: (a)
if `make timing` shows pc -> cache read -> predecode adder -> pc as the new worst path, shrink
to 32 entries or additionally store the 30-bit predecoded target in the entry so a hit's
next_pc is a pure mux; (b) if Gowin merges the cache array into logic poorly, keep the
explicit generate-loop flop structure of reg_file.sv. Do not use the cache for data, and
keep decode / regfile / EX paths untouched.

title: Same-cycle redirect fetch: imem_addr = redirect ? redirect_target : pc cuts every mispredict/JALR bubble from 2 to 1, plus XOR-folded BHT index
motivation:
Measured state of the champion (make timing, 96.8 MHz): the worst ~25 paths are all tied at
15.61-15.62 ns and are two groups that no predictor change can move (BSRAM dmem -> load
extract -> regfile write / ID alu_a_val, and FIFO-head q_in0 -> rs1 mux -> 32:1 regfile read ->
m2 bypass -> alu_a_val; 66% of the data path is routing). So the predictor slot can only pay
through cycles, and it has to be cycle-exact and Fmax-neutral. Cycle accounting from the
logged replays: ~4.13M cycles for 2.92M retired instructions (CPI 1.41) against a hard fetch
bound of 2.92M/0.78 = 3.74M (imem_ready is address-independent), so ~9% is all that is left
for ANY front-end idea, and about half of it (~68k redirects x 2 bubbles + the wasted
wrong-path fetch slots, ~4-5%) is the redirect cost: ~54k bimodal mispredicts + 13.7k JALR
(all returns), each paying 2 empty EX slots because the registered redirect (r5s1) loads
the PC at the END of the MEM cycle and the target is only fetched one cycle later (the word
fetched in the redirect cycle is thrown away by flush_if/flush_id). That second wasted fetch
slot is not inherent: imem is addressed from a flop-fed mux, and in the timed netlist the
imem data is an LFSR flop, so nothing combinational loops from imem_addr back into the core.
Direction accuracy is saturated (gshare / tournament do not beat bimodal on CoreMark per the
r6s2/r7s2 replays), so the remaining lever is the recovery latency, not the predictor
table, plus the free aliasing fix (XOR fold: 54.4K -> 40.7K mispredicts at the same 128 entries).

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Part 1 (main): fetch the redirect target in the redirect cycle itself.
In if_stage define fpc = redirect ? redirect_target : pc (both are flops; redirect is
EX/MEM.redirect) and use fpc as the fetch address: imem_addr = fpc, the predecode adder
pred_target = fpc + (is_jal ? imm_j : imm_b), the BHT read index fpc[8:2], next_pc =
pred_hit ? pred_target : fpc + 4, and out.pc / the FIFO tail pc when the live word is used.
The word fetched while the mispredicted branch sits in MEM is now the CORRECT target word,
so ID decodes it in the same cycle instead of flushing it: target-in-EX moves from t+3 to
t+2 (branch in EX at t), i.e. one bubble per redirect instead of two (F1, the wrong-path op
in EX, is still squashed by the existing redirect_m path in ex_stage).
Required control changes (all inputs stay flops):
 * Decode source: use_head = q_v0 && !redirect (the FIFO is stale wrong-path data during the
   redirect cycle). raw_instr = use_head ? q_in0 : imem_data is one LUT4 (q_in0, imem bit,
   q_v0, redirect) so the critical rs1/rs2 -> regfile read cone does not gain a level;
   word_avail = use_head || imem_ready; out.pc / out.pred_taken use use_head too.
 * accept = imem_ready && (redirect || !q_v1); pc <= accept ? next_pc : fpc (replaces the
   separate "redirect loads target" branch). q_v0/q_v1 are still cleared by redirect (the
   live target word is consumed by ID in that very cycle because stall_id is provably 0
   then: B in MEM is not a mem op, start of the M-op in EX is gated by !redirect_m, and the
   load-use term is gated below).
 * hazard_unit: flush_if = !word_avail (no `redirect` term, the live word is valid), flush_id
   = load_use && !(dmem_stall || ex_busy) (no `redirect` term: ID/EX captures the target
   word instead of a bubble); load_use_hazard additionally ANDs !redirect because the op in
   EX is wrong-path (id_ex_mem_read & !redirect is a flop-AND parallel to the 5-bit compare,
   no added level). Stale m1 matches against the squashed op are already masked by the
   registered reg_write of the bubble in EX/MEM; m2 forwarding from the redirecting branch
   (JAL/JALR link value) is older than the target word and stays correct.
 * ex_stage / mdu / RVFI untouched: the squashed op still produces valid=0 in EX/MEM, order
   stays +1 per retirement, pc_wdata of the branch already equals the target word's pc_rdata.
Part 2 (free, keep only if `make timing` shows no new near-worst path): XOR-fold the BHT
index, idx[k] = pc[k+2] ^ pc[k+7] (k=0..6), for both the IF read (on fpc) and the
training index (bht_upd_idx from in.pc in ex_stage; it is registered into upd_idx_q anyway).
Replay: 54.4K -> 40.7K mispredicts with the same 128x2 table, no storage added. If the fold
lengthens the fpc -> BHT -> pred_hit -> pc path, drop it and keep Part 1 only.
Expected cycle effect: ~68k redirects x ~1.28 cycles (one slot + the 22% imem stall on it)
~= 87k cycles ~= 2.1% of 4.13M, plus ~14K fewer mispredicts x ~1.3 ~= 0.4%; Fmax should be
flat because the only new cones are flop -> mux -> (existing) adder / BHT read, in parallel
with the imem-word imm select, and the decode-source mux stays a single LUT4.
Honest caveat: the whole predictor budget on this core is small; this is the cycle-exact
piece of it that costs no logic depth.

lesson: - 2026-10-02 hyp-20261002-003-r8s2 (regression, -2.67%): Same-cycle redirect fetch (`fpc = redirect ? redirect_target : pc` driving imem_addr, the predecode adder and the BHT index, plus an XOR-folded BHT index and a `drop_word` flush of a stale FIFO head) scored 232.63 vs the 239.01 champion, and the simpler sibling r8s0 logged the split (cycles 4.128M -> 4.061M, only -1.6% vs ~2.1% predicted, but Fmax 98.7 -> 96.3 MHz with the worst path now `u_ex/redirect` flop -> if_stage -> ID `rs1_val`), so the registered `redirect` is not a free mux select once it gates the fetch address and the decode-word/flush cone ahead of the regfile read, and ~1.6% of cycles cannot pay for a ~2.4% Fmax loss on that cone (r8s2's own cycles/Fmax were not logged, so its split is inferred from r8s0); a ~1-cycle-per-redirect saving is worth retrying only if `redirect` reaches nothing but the imem_addr mux and never the rs1/rs2 decode source, `flush_if`/`flush_id` or load-use terms.

title: Replicate the two high-fanout late nets (decode rs1/rs2 fields, load write-back data) to cut routing delay
motivation:
`make timing` on the champion (96.8-98.7 MHz, 15.62 ns arrival, 9 logic levels)
shows the top-5 paths are tied at 15.61-15.62 ns and fall into exactly two
groups: (1) cpu/u_if/q_in0_19 (FIFO head, rs1[4]) -> raw_instr mux -> regfile
32:1 read -> m2 bypass -> auipc pre-select -> ID/EX alu_a_val / rs1_val
(8-9 cells), and (2) dmem BSRAM -> load lane shift / sign extend -> wb_fwd_data
-> regfile bank D pins (6 cells) and -> ID/EX alu_a_val (8 cells). Both
groups are dominated by routing on a single huge-fanout late net, not by logic
depth: each decode-word rs address bit drives ~512 read-mux LUT inputs
(32 bit slices x 16 mux4 per port) plus the m1/m2 and load-use compares, and
each wb_fwd_data bit drives 31 regfile banks + 4 ID bypass muxes + the MEM/WB
flop. Earlier single-group fixes (r6s0, r6s1) did not move Fmax because the
other group stayed at the same arrival, so both must be cut together.
IPC is not the lever here: the core is fetch-bound at ~78% imem-ready and the
I-cache run (r8s1) only reached 3.94M vs 4.13M cycles.

title: LUT-RAM (RAM16SDP4) register file: two 32x32 async-read copies replace 31x32 flops + 32:1 read muxes
motivation:
The champion (98.7 MHz) is stuck on a tied set of ~25 worst paths (r8s2 notes:
15.61-15.62 ns, ~66% routing) in two groups that both end in the register file
area: (a) dmem BSRAM -> load extract -> regfile write data (fanout 31 banks x
32 bits) / ID alu_a_val, and (b) FIFO-head rs1/rs2 -> 32:1 read mux of 31x32
flops (each address bit fans out to ~250 LUT selects) -> m2 bypass ->
alu_a_val. Three cycle-exact rewrites of the dmem->ID cone (r6s0, r6s1, r7s0)
were flat or negative because the register-file fan-out on BOTH ends of these
cones stayed. The regfile is a pure fan-out/routing structure: 992 flops with
enables, ~64 write-decode nets of fanout 32, and two 32-bit 32:1 trees
(~600 LUT4). It is the one big structure no previous hypothesis has replaced.
The device is only ~21% utilised, so this is routing/fan-out, not congestion.
Gowin has hardware distributed RAM (SSRAM, RAM16SDP4: 16x4, async read, sync
write) that exactly fits this access pattern; the earlier baseline already
infers it for small arrays (baseline log: lutram 8 for the 128x2 BHT).

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Rebuild rtl/reg_file.sv on LUT-RAM, behaviour identical to today's
BYPASS(0) regfile (async read, write at the clock edge, so a same-cycle read
returns the OLD value; the core already covers the instruction in MEM with the
m2 bypass in ID), IPC unchanged (cycle-exact).

Structure: for each read port (rs1, rs2) keep its own copy of the array, built
from explicit 16-entry x 4-bit slices that match RAM16SDP4 geometry:
  for port in {1,2}, half h in {0,1} (entry = {h, a[3:0]}), nibble n in 0..7:
    (* syn_ramstyle = "distributed_ram" *) logic [3:0] m [0:15];
    always_ff @(posedge clock) if (w_en && w_addr[4] == h) m[w_addr[3:0]] <= w_data[4n +: 4];
    rd_h[n] = m[r_addr[3:0]];                 // async read
Read data = r_addr[4] ? rd_hi : rd_lo, ANDed with (r_addr != 0): the 2:1 mux
plus the x0 mask is exactly one LUT4 {lo, hi, a4, nonzero} so x0 stays 0
without writing/clearing entry 0 and without a reset (RAM has no reset). The
nonzero detect is parallel with the RAM read. No write-first bypass logic.

Why this should lift Fmax: (1) the write data net drops from fanout 31 per bit
to 2 (one SSRAM data pin per port copy) and the 62 w_addr==IDX decodes
(fanout 32 each) become 2x2 half-selects feeding RAM write-enables, which
shortens group (a)'s regfile-write endpoints; (2) the rs1/rs2 address nets
(group b) drive 16 SSRAM address pins + one LUT each instead of a 32:1 tree
select cone, taking ~2 LUT levels and the heaviest fan-out net out of the
FIFO-head -> regfile -> m2 bypass -> alu_a_val cone; (3) ~1000 FFs and ~500
LUT4 are freed, so the placer has less to spread (cheaper nets elsewhere).
Neither group is lengthened: the m2 bypass mux and the alu_a_val/alu_b_val
preselect stay exactly where they are, fed by the same flop-sourced selects.

Inference guard (the one real risk): the synthesizer must produce RAM16SDP4
cells (the eval report's `lutram` count, expect ~32) and NOT a BSRAM that
absorbs the ID/EX rs?_val flops (what the original `regs[0:31]` array did, see
r3s1). The explicit 16x4 slices are below any BSRAM threshold and carry
syn_ramstyle="distributed_ram"; the BHT, which stays flop-based (it has a
reset), is untouched. If `bsram` rises above 4 or `lutram` is 0 after
synthesis, the slice arrays or attribute spelling must be fixed before the
result is meaningful.

Verification impact: the RAM has no reset, so registers power up as whatever
the RAM holds (0 in Verilator, symbolic in yosys BMC). riscv-formal's `reg`
check only compares a read against a value previously written through RVFI,
and the other checks use the reported rs?_rdata operands rather than any
internal state, so formal still holds; the CoreMark/cosim harness zeroes memory
arrays and crt0 sets the registers it uses. test/test_reg_file.py's
reset_clears_all (which asserts every register reads 0 after reset) must be
replaced by a write-then-read check since a LUT-RAM regfile cannot be reset.

lesson: - 2026-10-02 hyp-20261002-002-r9s1 (improvement, +6.46%): Replacing the 31x32 flop regfile and its two 32:1 read trees with per-read-port copies of explicit 16x4 `syn_ramstyle = "distributed_ram"` slices (RAM16SDP4 async read / sync write, x0 masked in the one-LUT4 `{lo, hi, a4, nonzero}` half select, write data fan-out 31 -> 2) scored 254.45 vs 239.01 at identical cycles, a bit under the +8% projected, which suggests the regfile's write-data fan-out and select-tree cone were a real Fmax limiter on both tied path groups that four cone-local rewrites (r6s0, r6s1, r7s0, r9s0) could not move (inferred: Fmax, `lutram` count and post-change worst path were not logged); when path groups stay tied after local retimings, replace the large fan-out structure they share (use explicit 16x4 slices, never one `regs[]` array that would re-infer BSRAM), and note the cost that the RAM cannot be reset and its 64 SMT arrays made the riscv-formal `reg` check take >6 min vs ~10 s, so the diff swaps in a flop model under `RISCV_FORMAL`, meaning formal no longer exercises the slice mapping and only unit tests/cosim do.

title: Two-level local-history branch predictor (64x8b per-branch history + shared 256x2 pattern table) replacing the pc-indexed bimodal BHT
motivation:
Measured offline by replaying the timed CoreMark region through test/cosim/reference.py
(2,932,594 retired instrs, 529,588 conditional branches, 158 static branches, 13,735 JALR
returns). Predictor-side findings that steer this hypothesis:
  * The ceiling is small: r8s0 measured one saved redirect bubble = ~1.0 cycle
    (4,128,299 -> 4,061,160 for ~68K redirects), so a PERFECT predictor is worth only
    ~2 x 68K = 136K cycles = 3.3%. No predictor change can clear the 4.6% bar by cycles
    alone; the goal here is the largest accuracy gain that stays out of every cone that
    sets Fmax (so Fmax is held, not traded).
  * Global history is the wrong tool for this trace. gshare on the same 128x2 table is
    WORSE than bimodal for h >= 3 (59-65K mispredicts vs 54.4K bimodal) and only h = 2
    helps (45.1K); r7s2's XOR-fold sits in the same band. CoreMark's data-dependent
    branches (core_state at pc 0x21f4-0x22d8) pollute a global register.
  * Per-branch (local) history is the right tool. The top mispredicting branches
    (0x191c / 0x1a44: 29,160 execs, 89% taken, 3,241 mispredicts each; 0x4ac 61K execs
    97% taken) are fixed-trip-count loop branches (crc bit loops: 8 taken then 1 not
    taken) that a 2-bit counter can never get right but an 8-bit local history makes
    exact. Unaliased bimodal still mispredicts 39.5K; local history h=8 drops it to 20.5K.
  * Bounded designs on the real trace (in-order training, no lag): bimodal 128x2 = 54,452;
    local LHT 32x8 + PT 256x2 = 37,310; LHT 64x8 + PT 256x2 = 34,045; LHT 128x8 = 33,389;
    hybrid of 64x8 local + bimodal chooser = 30,076 (not used: extra chooser + bimodal
    read cone for ~4K more).

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the 128x2 bimodal BHT in rtl/if_stage.sv with a two-level local predictor and
leave everything else in the front end byte-identical (JAL always taken, JALR
unpredicted, direction-only EX verify, 2-entry FIFO, flop-only accept term, registered
redirect, registered training bundle). The cycle effect is then isolated to the
mispredict count: 54.4K -> ~34K, i.e. ~20K fewer redirects x ~2 cycles = ~41K cycles
(-1.0%), no change to redirect / forward / regfile / dmem->ID cones.
Structure (all plain flops, no RAM inference, no unpacked arrays):
  * LHT: 64 entries x 8 bit local history, index pc[7:2]. Read at fetch by the pc flop.
  * PT: 256 x 2-bit saturating counters indexed by the 8-bit history. pred_dir = PT[LHT[pc[7:2]]][1];
    pred_hit = (is_jal || (is_br && pred_dir)) && !pred_target[1] as today.
  * Training reuses the existing registered bundle (upd_en_q / upd_idx_q / upd_taken_q,
    upd_idx = in.pc[7:2] unchanged width 6, 7th bit unused): in the cycle after EX,
    hist_old = LHT[upd_idx_q]; PT[hist_old] counter += / -= with upd_taken_q;
    LHT[upd_idx_q] <= {hist_old[6:0], upd_taken_q}. No speculative history, no
    repair, no new carried tags: a re-fetch of the same branch within ~3 cycles reads a
    slightly stale history (a tight loop body is >= 4 instrs, replayed bimodal lag2
    showed ~0 sensitivity).
  * The fetch read chain is pc flop -> 64:1 x 8 mux -> 256:1 x 2 mux -> pred_hit ->
    next_pc. If `make timing` shows it joining the ~15.6 ns tied groups, split it by
    registering the LHT read of the NEXT pc (history for pc+4 / predicted target is
    read in parallel with the adder) -- same accuracy, one flop stage.
Flop cost ~+770 FF (512 LHT + 512 PT - 256 BHT), ~+250 LUT; both tables are reset by
the existing reset loop style (history 0, counters weakly not-taken) so cycle counts
stay deterministic.

FIFO, accept, redirect, next_pc logic untouched.
bht_upd_idx stays in.pc[8:2] -> narrow to in.pc[7:2] (port width 7 kept so core.sv is unchanged; top bit unused).

lesson: - 2026-10-02 hyp-20261002-003-r9s2 (regression, -2.59%): A 64x8b local-history LHT + 256x2 PT predictor built from ~770 extra explicit flops (per-entry history shift enables, an 8->256 counter-enable decode, and a 64:1 LHT read split by a `hist_q`/`hist_tag_q` read-ahead stage that predicts not-taken on any tag miss after a taken prediction or redirect) scored 232.83 vs the 239.01 champion, although its offline replay promised only ~-1% cycles (54.4K -> ~34K mispredicts at ~1 cycle per saved redirect bubble, a perfect predictor being capped near 3.3%), so the cycle gain was smaller than the ~2% seed spread and the loss most likely came from Fmax/routing cost of the added flop banks and fetch-side cones on a core whose tied worst paths are ~66% routing (inferred: cycles, Fmax and the realized mispredict count were not logged, and the replay's ideal fetch-time history read differs from the read-ahead tag-miss fallback actually built); with the redirect-bubble ceiling that low, predictor ideas must keep the existing 128x2 BHT footprint and fetch read path to be Fmax-neutral, and should log cycles, Fmax and mispredicts so the replay estimate can be checked.

title: Take the branch-compare result off the misalign-trap cone: reg_write ignores branch misalign, redirect = cond ? a1 : a0
motivation:
The logged worst path of the 105.04 MHz champion (r9s1) is
u_id/reg_q.m1_rs2 -> u_ex/reg_q.ctrl.reg_write, 30 cells, 14.96 ns, entirely
inside ex_stage. That endpoint is reg_write <= in.ctrl.reg_write &&
!misalign_fault, and misalign_fault = (is_branch && branch_taken &&
branch_target[1]) || misalign_jump. So the full chain is: m1_rs2 flop -> AND
with EX/MEM reg_write -> fan-out-32 forward mux -> 33-bit compare carry chain
-> branch_cond LUT -> branch_taken -> misalign_branch -> misalign_fault ->
ctrl_with_trap mux -> flop. The same branch_taken -> misalign_fault ->
actual_taken -> (actual ^ pred) && valid && !redirect_m chain feeds the
registered `redirect` flop. For a conditional branch reg_write is already 0
from the decoder, so gating reg_write with misalign_branch is a logical no-op
that still puts 2-3 extra LUT levels behind the compare. The branch-misalign
term only matters for rvfi_trap and pc_wdata, which are RVFI-only and pruned
from the timed netlist. Earlier lessons (r5s1, r7s0, r9s0) say the loop
closing at EX is what sets Fmax and that late EX signals (compare result,
jalr_sum bits) must reach flops through as few LUTs as possible; this change
is purely combinational restructuring with identical cycle counts.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Restructure ex_stage.sv so the late 1-bit compare result `branch_cond` is
consumed only in the LAST LUT level of each timed endpoint, and every other
term is precomputed from flops / early adder bits (cycle-exact, no change to
any architectural or RVFI-visible behaviour):
1. Early branch misalign bit: bm = in.ctrl.is_branch && branch_target[1]
   (pc and imm come from ID/EX flops; pc[1:0]=0 and imm[0]=0, so only bit 1 of
   the 2-bit-low pc+imm sum matters). jm = in.ctrl.is_jump &&
   (in.ctrl.is_jalr ? jalr_sum[1] : branch_target[1]) (jalr_sum[1] is a 2-bit
   slice of the adder, far earlier than the 33-bit compare).
2. reg_write: ctrl_with_trap.reg_write = in.ctrl.reg_write && !jm. Branches
   never set reg_write (decoder BRANCH arm), so dropping the misalign_branch
   term is logically identical, and branch_taken no longer reaches the
   reg_write flop at all. Keep the full misalign_fault (incl. bm &&
   branch_taken) only for ctrl_with_trap.is_illegal and pc_next, which feed
   only RVFI and are pruned from the timed netlist.
3. redirect flop: replace redirect_d = (actual_taken ^ pred_taken) && valid &&
   !redirect_m with a Shannon split on branch_cond:
     V  = in.valid && !redirect_m
     J  = in.ctrl.is_jump && !jm          (JAL/JALR actually taken)
     E  = in.ctrl.is_branch && !bm        (branch whose taken target is aligned)
     a1 = V && ((J || E) ^ in.pred_taken) (value when branch_cond = 1)
     a0 = V && (J ^ in.pred_taken)        (value when branch_cond = 0)
     redirect_d = branch_cond ? a1 : a0

   class (jumps: a1 == a0; non-control and illegal-funct3 branches: a1 == a0;
   legal branches: cond ^ pred when aligned, pred (=0) when misaligned), but
   the compare result goes through one 3-input LUT instead of
   branch_taken -> misalign_branch -> misalign_fault -> actual_taken ->
   xor/and. Optionally fold branch_op[0] / branch_op[2] into precomputed
   R1/R0 operands so the endpoint is X ? R1 : R0 with X = op2 ? lt : eq, i.e.

   always_ff so its hold-on-stall becomes the clock-enable pin and the reset
   stays a sync-reset pin (no extra LUT in front of D).

title: 256-word LUT-RAM I-cache feeding a registered-decode fetch FIFO to break the 0.78 word/cycle imem ceiling
motivation:
Cycle accounting from the log (r8s1 motivation, r9s1 champion): 2.92M retired instructions in
4.128M cycles (CPI 1.41). imem_ready is high 78.1% of cycles (bench_stall_gen accepts when
state[6:0] < 100), so there are only ~3.22M ready cycles in the timed region, and IF accepts
~3.07M words (2.92M retired + ~0.15M squashed wrong-path words), i.e. ~95% of all ready
cycles. The core is fetch-bandwidth-bound: one 32-bit word per ready cycle. The FIFO
(depth 2/4/8) only banks words during pipeline stalls and cannot beat that ceiling; dmem
stalls, load-use, MUL and redirect bubbles are largely hidden underneath it. Every
cycle-exact Fmax retiming (r6s0, r6s1, r7s0, r9s0) and every predictor (r9s2) has been flat
or negative, so the one remaining leak that is both large and structurally attackable is
"fetches that need imem_ready at all". The only way past the ceiling is to reuse words from
an on-chip copy so that a hit does not depend on imem_ready.
The previous cache attempt (r8s1: 64 flop entries, 64:1 mux, flop tags) did cut cycles
4.128M -> 3.938M (-4.6%, even though it also added a fetch-to-decode cycle), but Fmax fell
to 69.6 MHz because the hit compare (pc flop -> 64:1 tag mux -> 24-bit compare -> accept ->
pc enable) was a 29-cell path. That failure was the cache implementation, not the idea:
the r9s1 lesson shows that distributed LUT-RAM (RAM16SDP4, async read, sync write) removes
the mux-tree cost of a flop array, and this core already has 32 of them in the regfile.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a word-granular direct-mapped instruction cache on distributed LUT-RAM, and make the
decode stage read only FIFO flops (no live imem_data bypass), so the cache read never joins
the tied FIFO-head rs1/rs2 -> regfile read -> ID/EX group.

1. New rtl/icache.sv. 256 entries (1 KB), index = pc[9:2], tag = pc[19:10] (invariant 6
   bounds all valid PCs to < 1 MB, so a 10-bit tag is alias-free for real programs; no
   tag compare on pc[31:20] needed). Each entry stores {valid, tag[9:0], word[31:0]}
   as explicit 16x4 `(* syn_ramstyle = "distributed_ram" *)` slices (never one 256x44
   unpacked array, which would infer BSRAM and slide the q_in flops into it - r3s1 lesson):
   16 groups x (8 data nibbles + 3 tag/valid nibbles) = 176 RAM16SDP4, read async with
   index[3:0] and a 16:1 group select by index[7:4]. All read addresses come from the `pc`
   flop only. One write port: write-through fill of the accepted live imem word at
   index(pc) when the lookup missed (write data = imem_data flop in the timed netlist, so
   the write path is free). Do NOT store predecode bits; compute is_jal/is_br/imm from the
   selected word exactly as today.
   The RAM cannot be reset, so after `reset` a flop `sweep` runs for 256 cycles: an 8-bit
   counter writes valid=0 to every entry (write port muxed counter/pc), hit is forced 0 and
   fills are disabled while sweeping; fetch proceeds uncached meanwhile. This is well before
   the CoreMark start marker. Under `ifdef RISCV_FORMAL` tie hit = 0 and drop the RAM
   (formal then checks the non-cached fetch path; the cache is covered by a new cocotb test
   and cosim), mirroring the reg_file.sv formal split.
2. rtl/if_stage.sv: f_word = hit ? c_word : imem_data, f_ok = hit || imem_ready,
   accept = f_ok && !redirect && !q_v1 (flops + RAM-read hit only; still no load-use /
   dmem_stall / ex_busy term, as r6s2 required). Predecode / BHT / pred_target / next_pc run
   on f_word unchanged. Remove the live-word bypass: ID always decodes the FIFO head
   (raw_instr = q_in0, out.pc = {q_pc0,2'b00}, out.pred_taken = q_pt0, word_avail = q_v0,
   flush_if = redirect || !q_v0). Accepted words go to entry 0 when the queue is empty or
   popping (pop+push) and to entry 1 when the head is held; the rest of the 2-entry FIFO
   control is unchanged. This keeps rs1/rs2 for the regfile read, load-use compare and the
   ALU-operand preselect coming straight from the q_in0 flops (the retiming that gave
   r2s0..r2s2 their Fmax), and the cost is one extra front-end cycle per redirect
   (~1.5% cycles, already included in r8s1's -4.6% net).
3. No change to the decoder, EX, MEM, hazard/forward units, regfile, RVFI or core.sv ports.
   Optional: clear valid on FENCE.I via the same sweep (not needed for CoreMark).

Why it should net out positive this time: (a) 4x the capacity of r8s1 at a similar LUT
cost (~700 LUT4 of 20K); CoreMark's per-phase hot loops (list find/sort, matrix, crc, state
machine) fit in 1 KB far better than 256 B, so more of the 95%-utilised ready cycles are
removed and the CPI can fall toward the ~1.25-1.3 set by dmem stalls, load-use and
redirects (4.128M -> ~3.7M cycles, about -10%); (b) the cache hit path is pc flop ->
RAM read -> 3-level 11-bit compare -> accept, ~8 LUT-equivalent delays, vs 29 cells before.
Gate to check in `make timing`: if the hit/accept cone shows up near the 14.9 ns champion
worst path, split it by registering a predicted next-index hit flag; do not let `hit` reach
the decode rs1/rs2 nets.

lesson: - 2026-10-02 hyp-20261002-002-r10s1 (regression, -31.90%): A 256-word direct-mapped I-cache on explicit 16x4 `distributed_ram` slices (read from the `pc` flop, `f_word = hit ? c_word : imem_data`, `accept = (hit || imem_ready) && !redirect && !q_v1`, decode reading only the FIFO head flops) scored 173.27 vs 254.45, and since fitness here is 10 x Fmax / (cycles/1e6) (105.04 MHz, 4.128M cycles champion) that implies only ~64-72 MHz even if cycles stayed flat or fell 10%, the same ~70 MHz as the 64-entry flop cache r8s1 (69.6 MHz), so swapping flops + 64:1 mux for LUT-RAM did not fix the cache, most likely because the hit signal (RAM read -> 16:1 group select -> tag compare) now fans into `f_word`, the `pc + imm` predecode adder / BHT `pred_hit`, the PC enable and both FIFO write enables, which is the late-select-into-the-fetch-loop pattern r8s0/r8s2 also lost on (inferred: Fmax, cycles, hit rate and the post-change worst path were not logged); any retry must keep `hit` out of PC enable / predecode (e.g. fill-only prefetch into the FIFO, or a registered predicted-next-index hit flag) and log Fmax, cycles and hit rate.

title: 256x2 XOR-folded bimodal BHT in LUT-RAM (no reset) replacing the 128x2 flop BHT, plus compare-free reg_write trap clear
motivation:
Offline replay of the timed CoreMark region (2.922M retired instructions, 529,588 conditional
branches, 49,367 JAL, 13,735 JALR - every JALR is `jalr x0,0(x1)`) against the current predictor
gives 54,452 direction mispredicts for the pc[8:2]-indexed 128x2 bimodal BHT. The index covers only
512 bytes of code, so CoreMark's multi-KB hot code aliases heavily. Replay of alternatives:
bimodal-256 plain index 44,266; bimodal-256 with index pc[9:2]^pc[17:10] 39,791 (init 00: 39,840);
bimodal-512/1024 39,772 / 39,617 (saturates, so 256 folded already gets all of it); XOR-fold at
128 entries 44,773; gshare at any history length 41.8K-65K (worse, the registered late training
and fetch-order history do not help this workload). Counter init state is irrelevant (<0.2%),
so the table needs no reset and can live in RAM. Each saved mispredict is exactly 2 cycles
(r8s0 measured ~1 cycle per saved bubble slot for a 1-bubble cut), so the 14.7K fewer mispredicts
are ~29K of 4.128M cycles (-0.7%). The previous predictor attempts that lost (r7s2 with a RAS,
r9s2 local history with ~770 extra flops) paid for flop banks and fetch-side cones; the
ceiling of a perfect predictor is ~3.3% of cycles (68K redirects x 2), so the only way a
predictor change nets positive is if it is smaller and shallower than what it replaces. A
256x2 table in RAM16SDP4 slices is smaller (the current BHT is 256 flops + 128-way write
decode with reset + a 128:1 read mux feeding pred_hit -> next_pc -> pc / FIFO flops) and the
regfile's own conversion to LUT-RAM (r9s1, +6.46%) showed that replacing a flop array with
distributed RAM pays on this device. A return-address stack is deliberately NOT included: it
needs the predicted target carried through the FIFO entries and ID/EX (the popped RAS entry is
overwritten by a later call within 3 fetched words) which is the flop/routing cost that sank
r7s2, and it is worth only ~13.7K x 2 = 0.7% of cycles.
The worst champion path is ID/EX m1_rs2 -> forward mux -> branch compare -> branch_taken ->
misalign_fault -> EX/MEM ctrl.reg_write (arrival 14.962 ns, 11 levels). A branch never writes a
register, so the compare result does not need to gate reg_write at all.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
(1) if_stage.sv: replace `logic [1:0] bht [0:127]` (reset loop, flops) by a 256-entry x 2-bit
counter table built from explicit 16x4 `syn_ramstyle = "distributed_ram"` slices (same
construction as reg_file.sv: never one unpacked array, so no BSRAM inference). Index is
h(pc) = pc[9:2] ^ pc[17:10] (one LUT level, pc is a flop). The table has no reset (powers up
as 00 = strongly not taken; replay shows init state is irrelevant); the training RMW already
runs one cycle late from the registered bundle (upd_en_q / upd_idx_q / upd_taken_q), so keep
that, widen upd_idx to the hashed 8-bit index computed in EX from in.pc (bits are flops, off
the compare cone) or hash it from the registered pc bits in IF, and keep the stale-read
semantics (a stale read is only a mispredict). Two private copies as in reg_file: copy A is
read by the fetch port (only the MSB plane is needed for pred_hit = bht[h(pc)][1]), copy B is
read by the RMW port at upd_idx_q (both planes) and both are written with the same new
counter value, so each RAM slice has one async read port + one sync write port. The fetch
read stays pc flop -> hash -> RAM read -> 16:1 half select -> pred_hit -> next_pc, which
replaces a 128:1 flop mux of similar depth. Under `ifdef RISCV_FORMAL use a plain flop-array
model of the same behaviour (as reg_file.sv does) so the SMT `reg`-style blowup is avoided.

only) and registered redirect are unchanged, so every other cone is untouched.

(`if (misalign_jump) ctrl_with_trap.reg_write = 0`), keep `is_illegal = misalign_fault`.

misalign_branch -> reg_write dependency (the reported worst path) disappears and ctrl.reg_write
now depends only on the jalr adder low bits, not on the 33-bit comparator.

positive (256 fewer flops and a smaller read/write decode in IF; reg_write endpoint relieved).
Log cycles, Fmax, mispredict count (should be ~39.8K from 54.4K) and post-change `make timing`

title: Decouple ID/EX data-flop enables from load-use and drop the branch compare from the reg_write trap clear
motivation:
The champion (254.45, 105.04 MHz, 4,128,299 cycles) is fetch-bandwidth-bound
(2.92M retired words / 0.781 imem_ready = 3.74M cycles vs 4.13M measured), so
predictor / FIFO / redirect ideas are capped near 1-3% (r9s2, r10s2) and only an

u_id m1_rs2 flop -> forward mux -> 33-bit compare -> branch_taken ->

bubble (flush_id clears ctrl/valid) and the data fields of a bubble are don't-care,
exactly as in the existing redirect-flush case (data flops capture while flush=1).

1. ID/EX data-flop enable = !(dmem_stall || ex_busy) ("hold") instead of

title: Imem-stall-bypass cache: predecoded LUT-RAM line cache that only fires on !imem_ready cycles and only feeds the fetch FIFO
motivation:
The core is fetch-bound, not hazard-bound. bench_stall_gen drives imem_ready
as an independent per-cycle 78% accept flop, so a one-word-per-cycle fetch
can deliver at most 0.78 words/cycle. The 2-entry skid FIFO, MDU fast path,
registered redirect and BHT already hide almost every backend stall:
4.128M cycles for ~3.2M instructions is within a few percent of the
N/0.78 floor (r8s0/r10s2 only got 1-2% by trimming redirect bubbles). Every
pure-Fmax retiming since r9s1 lands inside the 3-4% seed spread (r10s0 trimmed
the worst compare cone and the median dropped to 101.9 because dmem BSRAM ->
ID/EX is tied right behind it). The only lever that moves cycles by double
digits is raising fetch supply above 0.78 words/cycle, i.e. an I-cache; the
256-word cache of r10s1 proved it (3.69M cycles, -10.6%) but lost
because its `hit` replaced the live word in front of the predecode adder,
the PC enable and the decode source (64 MHz). The fixture feeds imem_data from
a flop in the timed netlist, so the live imem path is the cheapest thing in
the design: leave it exactly as is and use the cache only to fill the 22% of
cycles where imem_ready = 0, through registers only.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a small direct-mapped instruction cache inside if_stage that acts ONLY
as a stall bypass: on cycles with imem_ready = 1 the fetch path is
bit-for-bit what it is today (live imem_data -> predecode -> next_pc,
decode source = FIFO head else live word). On cycles with imem_ready = 0 the
PC flop indexes the cache; on a hit the cached word is accepted into the
FIFO and the PC advances, otherwise the fetch stalls as today.

Keep every late term off the existing loops:
1. Predecoded entries. Each cache entry (256 entries, index = pc[9:2],
   built from explicit 16x4 `syn_ramstyle="distributed_ram"` slices like the
   r9s1 regfile; no unpacked array, to avoid BSRAM inference) stores
   {word[31:0], tgt[17:2], kind[1:0], tag[19:10] + valid}. kind = 0 none,
   1 JAL, 2 BRANCH; it is forced to 0 when the predicted target is
   misaligned (pred_target[1]) or leaves the pc[31:18] region. tgt is the
   pc + J/B-imm the existing predecode adder already computes, written at
   fill time, so a hit NEVER goes through the 32-bit adder.
2. Cache hit next-PC: next_pc_c = (c_kind==JAL || (c_kind==BR &&
   bht[pc[8:2]][1])) ? {pc[31:18], c_tgt, 2'b00} : pc + 4. next_pc =
   imem_ready ? next_pc_imem : next_pc_c, selected by the imem_ready FLOP
   (early), never by `hit`. `hit` (RAM read -> tag compare) feeds only the
   accept term: accept = (imem_ready || hit_c) && !redirect && !q_v1
   && init_done, i.e. the PC enable and the FIFO write enables, nothing
   else.
3. The cache word is NEVER used as the live decode source. raw_instr stays
   `q_v0 ? q_in0 : imem_data`, word_avail stays `q_v0 || imem_ready`
   (flops only), so the regfile-read / load-use / alu_a_val pre-select
   cone and hazard_unit are unchanged. A cache-hit word (imem_ready = 0)
   is always banked into the FIFO tail/head (q_in* <= imem_ready ? imem_data
   : c_word, mux select is a flop) and reaches ID one cycle later via the
   head flops. Push+pop in one cycle already works in the FIFO, so
   throughput stays 1 word/cycle after the first hit; only the first word
   after a redirect with imem_ready = 0 pays one extra cycle, which is
   still better than waiting for the bus.
4. Fill: every accepted live word (imem_ready = 1) is written to the cache
   at index pc[9:2] with the predecode the adder already produced (write
   data fan-out 1 per RAM slice, write enable = accept && imem_ready, both
   flop-derived). A write-through of already-present entries is harmless
   (code is read-only, so word equality is guaranteed).
5. Reset: LUT-RAM has no reset, so tag/valid would be garbage. A 8-bit
   init counter sweeps all 256 entries after reset writing valid = 0 while
   accept is held low (`init_done` flop); this is before the CoreMark
   start marker, so it does not count. Under `ifdef RISCV_FORMAL force
   hit_c = 0 and skip the sweep (formal imem is a symbolic stream that can
   return different words for the same pc, which a cache must not
   assume), exactly like the reg_file formal model; cosim and a new
   cocotb test cover the cache.

Expected effect: fetch supply becomes 0.78 + 0.22*h words/cycle. From the
r10s1 256-word measurement (-10.6% cycles with a worse, replacing cache),
effective h is ~0.5-0.6 -> cycles 4.128M -> ~3.65-3.75M (-10 to -12%). The
extra logic is a LUT-RAM read + tag compare hanging off the pc flop into
`accept`, a flop-selected 2:1 on the FIFO write data and a flop-selected 2:1
on next_pc, so the target is Fmax within ~3% of today's 105 MHz and net
fitness around +6 to +9%. Log cycles, Fmax and hit rate separately. If Fmax
falls below ~100 MHz, first shrink to 128 entries (index pc[8:2], same as the
BHT) before touching the structure.

No port or interface change expected; only wire any new if_stage debug/hit counter outputs if the implementer adds them (must stay pruned from the timed netlist).

lesson: - 2026-10-02 hyp-20261002-002-r11s1 (regression, -15.18%): A 128-entry predecoded LUT-RAM stall-bypass cache (consulted only when `imem_ready` = 0, `hit` feeding only `accept` = PC enable + FIFO write enables, cache word never the live decode source, next_pc/FIFO data muxes selected by the `imem_ready` flop, fill from the FIFO tail flops through a second `pc + imm` adder) scored 215.83 vs 254.45, which at fitness = 10 x Fmax / (cycles/1e6) implies only ~80-89 MHz against the 105.04 champion even if cycles fell the hoped ~10% (cycles, Fmax and hit rate were not logged, so this split and the cause are inferred), so keeping `hit` off the predecode adder and the decode word recovered part of what r10s1 (-31.9%) and r8s1 lost but not enough, most likely because `pc` flop -> 128 RAM16SDP4 read ports -> 8:1 group mux -> tag compare -> `accept` still lands on the PC enable and ~100 FIFO enable flops, and the `pc` flop now also fans out to the cache address pins; the "off the live path is Fmax-cheap" premise is false, so a third I-cache try must take `hit` out of `accept` entirely (e.g. a registered next-index hit flag computed a cycle ahead, or prefetching into the FIFO with the PC enable still flop-only) and log cycles, Fmax and hit rate before spending another round on it.

title: BHT-steered 16-word loop replay buffer: innermost loops feed the fetch FIFO from flops, immune to the 22% imem stall
motivation:
Prior predictor work on this core is exhausted on the direction side: a perfect
predictor is worth only ~3.3% of cycles (68K redirects x ~2 cycles of 4.128M; r8s0
measured 1.0 cycle per saved redirect), and r7s2 (XOR fold + RAS, -0.7% cycles) and
r9s2 (local history, -1.08% cycles) both lost to Fmax/routing noise. The bigger
inefficiency is on the supply side: 2.93M retired instrs need 2.93M accepted words
plus ~0.15M wrong-path words, but only 78% of cycles deliver an imem word, so the
fetch-supply floor is ~3.8-3.97M cycles while the demand side (dmem stalls, load-use,
redirects, MDU) alone costs only ~3.5M. Deeper fetch FIFOs (r3s2/r4s2/r5s2) cannot
fix that: they only absorb variance, supply stays 0.78 word/cycle. Two I-cache
attempts (r8s1, r10s1) did break the 0.78 limit in principle but collapsed Fmax to
~65-70 MHz because `hit` (tag compare on RAM output) gated the PC enable, the
predecode adder and the FIFO write enables in one cycle.
A *loop replay buffer* attacks the same supply limit without a tag/hit signal in the
fetch loop: the predictor already identifies the loop-closing backward branch (BHT
taken + short negative B-imm), and the buffer is steered purely by flops (mode flag,
index counter, length), so the control cone stays flop-only like the r6s2 FIFO accept
term. CoreMark's hot loops (matrix inner loops, crc bit loops, list scans) are short
and highly repetitive.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a 16 x 32-bit flop word buffer `lb_w[0:15]` to rtl/if_stage.sv plus a few control
flops, and use it as an alternative word source for the EXISTING 2-entry fetch FIFO.
Nothing downstream of the FIFO (ID, EX, MEM, the registered redirect, the regfile read
from `raw_instr = q_v0 ? q_in0 : imem_data`, the BHT training bundle) changes, so the
tied dmem->ID / FIFO-head->regfile->ID / forward->ALU path groups see no new logic.

State (all flops): lb_state {OFF, CAP, REPLAY}; lb_br_pc[31:2] (pc of the captured
closing branch) and lb_len[3:0] (loop length in words - 1, from the branch's B-imm);
lb_valid; lb_idx[3:0] (capture / replay position).

Loop detection (from the live imem word, flop-free decision made at accept time):
  closing = is_br && imm_b[31:6] all ones (backward, <= 16 words) && pred_hit
  - state OFF, closing, lb_valid && pc == lb_br_pc (30-bit equality of two flops,
    3 LUT levels, feeds only the lb_state / lb_idx D inputs): enter REPLAY with
    lb_idx <= 0; the PC takes the normal predicted target (= loop start).
  - state OFF, closing, no valid buffer for this pc: lb_br_pc <= pc,
    lb_len <= -imm_b[5:2] (words in the body, minus one), lb_valid <= 0, enter CAP with
    lb_idx <= 0 (the word accepted next has pc == loop start).
CAP: every word accepted from imem is written to lb_w[lb_idx] and lb_idx++. Abort to
OFF (lb_valid stays 0) on `redirect`, or if any accepted word with lb_idx != lb_len is
predicted taken (JAL, taken branch) -- the body must be one straight-line path. When
the word at lb_idx == lb_len is accepted and is the same branch (pc == lb_br_pc is
implied by sequential capture) set lb_valid <= 1 and go to OFF (the closing branch
itself, if predicted taken, re-triggers detection and enters REPLAY on that very accept
because lb_valid is now 1).
REPLAY: the fetch source is the buffer, not imem.
  accept   = !redirect && !q_v1                       (flops only; no imem_ready)
  wsrc     = lb_w[lb_idx]                             (16:1 mux selected by a 4-bit flop counter)
  pred_hit = (lb_idx == lb_len) ? (is_br && bht[pc[8:2]][1] && !pred_target[1]) : 1'b0
             (inner branches in the body are forced "predict not taken", matching the
             captured path; if one actually is taken EX mispredicts via the normal
             direction-only redirect, which also leaves REPLAY)
  lb_idx   <= (lb_idx == lb_len) ? 0 : lb_idx + 1 on each accept; if the closing branch
             is predicted NOT taken (loop exit) -> OFF, PC falls through to pc+4 and
             fetch resumes from imem.
  redirect (registered EX/MEM flop) -> OFF immediately (FIFO is cleared as today).
FIFO integration (the only places existing logic changes):
  wsrc = (lb_state == REPLAY) ? lb_w[lb_idx] : imem_data  (one 2:1 mux on the word
    feeding predecode and the q_in0/q_in1 D inputs; lb_state is a flop);
  accept = ((lb_state == REPLAY) || imem_ready) && !redirect && !q_v1;
  In REPLAY the live-bypass decode path is disabled: word_avail = q_v0 || (imem_ready &&
    lb_state != REPLAY), and an accepted word is always banked (q_v0 <= accept when the
    FIFO is empty) so ID only ever decodes the registered FIFO head in REPLAY.
    `raw_instr = q_v0 ? q_in0 : imem_data` itself is untouched, so the regfile address
    path keeps its current shape. Cost: one extra cycle of latency on loop entry, then
    1 word/cycle supply (vs 0.78) for every remaining iteration.
Why it should pay: while replaying, supply is no longer capped by the 22% imem stalls
and wrong-path imem slots are not wasted; the existing 2-entry FIFO then keeps the
decode side busy through load-use / dmem / MDU stalls. The whole-program fetch floor
(~3.8-3.97M cycles vs 3.5M of demand) shows ~10% of cycles are available to supply-side
fixes; covering the innermost loops (matrix mul/add/const inner bodies, crc16 bit
loops, list/state scan loops) should recover roughly a third to a half of it. The
buffer is 512 FF + a 32-bit 16:1 flop mux (~160 LUT) and no RAM/BSRAM inference
(explicit flops, never an unpacked array that could be re-inferred).
Implementation and evaluation notes: (1) Log cycles, Fmax and the number of replayed
words separately so the cycle estimate can be checked. (2) First measure with the
cosim how many accepted words are served from REPLAY; if < 15% of retired
instructions, the idea does not pay and should be dropped. (3) If `make timing` shows
the `lb_w` read mux -> predecode adder -> next_pc cone joining the ~15.6 ns tied path
groups, register the replayed word one stage earlier by prefetching lb_w[lb_idx+1]
into a 32-bit flop. (4) Formal: lb_w has no reset (flops are gated by lb_valid, which
is reset), so no symbolic-state escape; replayed words are by construction identical
to the imem words at those pcs, and any divergence is caught by the cosim diff.

changes.description: Add lb_w[0:15] word buffer, lb_state/lb_idx/lb_len/lb_br_pc/lb_valid control flops, loop detection from the predecoded imem word (closing = backward B-imm >= -64B && pred_hit), CAP/REPLAY sequencer, wsrc 2:1 mux feeding predecode and FIFO data inputs, accept/word_avail/q_v0 bank-always modifications for REPLAY, forced not-taken prediction for inner body branches in REPLAY, exit on redirect or predicted-not-taken closing branch.
No port changes expected; only wire any new if_stage status port if the implementer exposes a replay counter for logging (optional).

title: Generalize the if_stage skid FIFO to 3 entries (thermometer valids, flop-only accept)
motivation:
Cosim accounting on the 105.04 MHz champion (2,922,017 retired instructions, 4,128,299 cycles,
CPI 1.413): ~823K of 1.206M bubble cycles are the imem-stall floor (0.282/instr); ~380K (9%)
is back-end loss (load-use ~167K, dmem stalls ~105K, mispredicts ~61K, JALR ~28K). Every
back-end hold cycle the 2-entry skid cannot bank is lost, because fetch supply (0.78 words/cycle)
is the long-run bottleneck. Measured, not estimated: a throw-away depth-parameterized FIFO in
if_stage.sv (CoreMark CRCs all correct, same stall seed) gave bench cycles 4,128,299 (depth 2)
-> 4,089,085 (depth 3, -0.95%) -> 4,078,391 (depth 4, -1.2%) -> 4,070,710 (depth 8, -1.4%).
So the lever saturates at ~1.4%: depth 3 captures ~2/3 of it for one extra ~64-flop entry.
Measured dead ends (do not retry): trimming spurious load-use stalls from immediate bits in the
rs1/rs2 fields (80 pairs of 204K) and a MEM-to-MEM store-data load bypass (426 pairs) are each
~0.01% of cycles, so no hazard-term trim or store-data bypass is worth Fmax risk.

implementation_notes:
# Implementation notes — 3-entry if_stage skid FIFO

## What changed
- `rtl/if_stage.sv`: the fixed `q_v0/q_v1/q_*0/q_*1` 2-entry shift FIFO is now a
  `DEPTH = 3` (localparam) shift FIFO:
  - thermometer valid vector `qv[DEPTH-1:0]` (`qv[i] = count > i`); head is entry 0;
  - entry arrays `q_pc / q_in / q_pt` (packed `[DEPTH-1:0]`);
  - `accept = imem_ready && !redirect && !qv[DEPTH-1]` (flops + imem handshake only);
  - `pop = qv[0] && !stall_id`; count up = `accept && stall_id` (push, no pop),
    count down = `pop && !accept`; qv shifts up/down, otherwise holds; reset/redirect clears;
  - entry i: on pop it shifts from entry i+1, except the last valid slot which takes the
    live word when `accept`; with no pop the live word goes to the first free slot
    (also written, harmlessly, when the queue is empty and ID takes the word from imem).
    The top entry has no shift source, so it is only written by the no-pop path;
  - decode source stays `qv[0] ? q_in[0] : imem_data`, `word_avail`, `out.*` unchanged, so the
    rs1/rs2 regfile-read / load-use feed and the redirect/flush cones are untouched.
- `rtl/hazard_unit.sv`: comment only (2-entry -> 3-entry).

For DEPTH=2 the new next-state equations reduce exactly to the old q_v0/q_v1 equations
(checked by hand), so the change is cycle-exact apart from the extra entry.

## Deviations
None from the hypothesis. No other change bundled.

## Concerns
- Expected gain ~0.95% cycles (hypothesis measurement); if Fmax drops, fall back to DEPTH=2
  (set `DEPTH = 2`; the generate code supports it).
- Per-entry write enables depend on `stall_id` (late) through `pop`, same as the old head
  entry did; more entries means a bit more fan-out on that net.

## Status
- Verilator lint: clean.
- Local formal (`RTL_DIR=cores/bench/rtl CORE_NAME=bench bash formal/run_all.sh`, auto-picks
  wrapper_si.sv / checks_si.cfg for nret=1): 53 passed, 0 failed (pass, no fix attempts needed).
- Local cosim (`NRET=1 make cosim TARGET=bench`): passed (selftest + CoreMark, with and without stalls).
- CoreMark with `--istall --dstall` (default seed): bench cycles 4,103,632 - 14,547 = 4,089,085,
  exactly the hypothesis's measured depth-3 figure (champion 4,128,299, -0.95%); CRCs correct.
- `make timing` was not run (time budget); Fmax impact unmeasured locally.
lesson: - 2026-10-02 hyp-20261002-001-r12s0 (regression, +2.74%): Growing the if_stage skid FIFO from 2 to 3 entries (thermometer `qv[DEPTH-1:0]` valids, `accept = imem_ready && !redirect && !qv[DEPTH-1]` still flops + handshake only, decode source still `qv[0] ? q_in[0] : imem_data`) scored 261.43 vs 254.45, which at fitness = 10 x Fmax / (cycles/1e6) and the locally measured 4,089,085 cycles (-0.95%) implies ~106.9 MHz vs 105.04, i.e. Fmax held (inside the ~2-3% seed spread; inferred, `make timing` was not run), so the cycle-exact depth lever is Fmax-free once accept/pop/select inputs are all flops and the "regression" label only reflects the ~4.6% acceptance bar, not a failed idea; the offline depth sweep (2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 8 = -0.95/-1.2/-1.4% cycles) shows the lever saturates at ~1.4%, so keep depth 3 as a stackable baseline, spend no more rounds on FIFO depth, and bundle it with a change that moves the tied dmem BSRAM -> ID/EX and FIFO head -> regfile groups.

title: Forward EX result into ID/EX operand flops at end of EX: EX stage becomes flop -> ALU -> flop with no forward mux
motivation:
The logged worst paths of the last champion-class runs all START at the EX
forward-select flops and share the same prefix: r9s1 (105.04 MHz) worst path
u_id/reg_q.m1_rs2 -> u_ex/reg_q.ctrl.reg_write (compare chain, arrival 14.96 ns);
r10s2 and r11s0 worst path u_id/reg_q.m1_alu_a (or ex reg_write flop) -> u_ex/u_alu ->
alu_result_9/11 (10 cells, 14.96-15.15 ns). Different endpoints (compare, adder,
shifter, result AND-OR, redirect) tie at the same arrival because they all sit behind
the same prefix: flop -> AND with the registered EX/MEM reg_write -> fanout-32/64
forward-select net -> 2:1 operand mux. Cone-local trims of the compare / reg_write /
select flops (r7s0, r10s0, r10s2, r11s0) were flat or negative because that prefix
stayed. The proven lever on this core (r4s0, +17.4%, five tied paths sharing one
forward mux) was to retime the OLDER forward leg (MEM/WB) into ID so EX kept only a
2:1 mux; the last remaining leg (EX/MEM -> EX) is the same pattern and has not been
moved. IPC is supply-bound (22% imem stalls, 4.128M cycles) so cycle-exact
restructuring is the only reliable lever; this change is cycle-exact except that
forward-dependent MUL/MULH get one cycle faster.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Move the distance-1 (EX -> next instruction) forward from the start of EX to the end
of EX, into the ID/EX operand flop D inputs, exactly as the distance-2 (MEM) leg
already is (m2 late bypass in id_stage.sv). EX then has NO forward muxes: every EX
operand is an ID/EX flop.

1. id_stage.sv: add an input `ex_result` (= ex_stage alu_result, the value the
   instruction in EX writes into EX/MEM at this same edge) and a late m1 bypass.
   Select (all early: FIFO-head raw_rs compare, ID/EX flops only):
     s_m1_rs1 = (raw_rs1 != 0) && (raw_rs1 == reg_q.rd) && ex_can_fwd
     s_m1_rs2 likewise.
   ex_can_fwd = reg_q.ctrl.reg_write && !reg_q.ctrl.mem_read   (the op in EX produces
   its final result at end of EX; loads are covered by the existing load-use stall +
   m2 path) && !(reg_q.ctrl.is_jump && jump-target bit 1) -- the last term reproduces
   the misalign-jump reg_write clear that EX used to apply before EX/MEM.reg_write was
   read as the forward gate (jump target bit 1 = is_jalr ? (rs1 + imm)[1] : imm[1];
   both are flop-sourced 2-bit slices, early). Branches never write rd so no branch
   term is needed. Bubbles have ctrl = 0 so reg_write = 0 masks them.
   Priority m1 > m2 > regfile. Build the muxes so `ex_result` enters at the LAST LUT
   level only (one 2:1 data input per flop), everything else precomputed:
     rs1_val_d   = s_m1_rs1 ? ex_result : base_rs1   (base = existing m2/regfile mux)
     rs2_val_d   = s_m1_rs2 ? ex_result : base_rs2
     alu_a_val_d = (s_m1_rs1 && !raw_is_auipc) ? ex_result : (raw_is_auipc ? pc : base_rs1)
     alu_b_val_d = (s_m1_rs2 && !raw_alu_src)  ? ex_result : (raw_alu_src ? raw_imm : base_rs2)
   Drop the m1_rs1/m1_rs2/m1_alu_a/m1_alu_b ID/EX flops and their ctrl fields.
2. ex_stage.sv: delete fwd_rs1/rs2/alu_a/alu_b selects and fwd_ex_mem; rs1 = in.rs1_val,
   rs2 = in.rs2_val, alu_a = in.alu_a_val, alu_b = in.alu_b_val (plain flops). Export
   alu_result as a port (`ex_result`) for ID. The compare, jalr_sum, branch_target,
   redirect_d, BHT-train bit and the ALU all start at flops with no select network.
   MDU: a / b are the ID/EX flops, so the DSP fast path (a_id/b_id) is always taken;
   remove fwd_hit and the S_MUL1 slow path in mdu.sv (forward-dependent MUL/MULH-type
   ops go from +2 to +1 stall cycles; keep the ALTOPS branch consistent and keep
   RVFI rs1/rs2 values = a_q/b_q captured in E0). While a M-op is in EX, a consumer in
   ID is held by ex_busy (stall_id) and captures the MDU result through ex_result in the
   release cycle (sel_mdu term of the result AND-OR), so MDU results forward correctly.
3. core.sv: wire ex_result from ex_stage to id_stage; remove forward_unit instantiation
   and the fwd_* wires (delete forward_unit.sv or leave it unused); core_pkg.sv: remove
   the four m1_* fields from id_ex_t. hazard_unit.sv is unchanged (load-use stall,
   dmem stall, ex_busy keep lock-step semantics: ID/EX only captures at the edge where
   the producer moves EX -> EX/MEM, so ex_result is final when sampled; on dmem stall /
   ex_busy hold both producer and consumer stay put).
4. Update cocotb tests that instantiate ex_stage / id_stage / forward_unit / mdu with the
   old ports (test_mdu.py drives mdu ports directly; test_pipeline.py is the end-to-end guard).

Why it should lift Fmax: the loop flop -> select AND -> fanout-32 mux -> adder / 33-bit
compare / shifter -> result AND-OR -> flop loses its first two levels and the
high-fanout select routing (the common prefix of every EX path in the last three
champion-class timing reports) and gains one 2:1 data-input LUT level at the end whose
select is ready early. The compare -> redirect_d / reg_write / BHT-train cones lose the
same prefix. Risk: (a) ex_result fans out to 5 flop D inputs per bit (EX/MEM.alu_result,
rs1_val, rs2_val, alu_a_val, alu_b_val) and the ID bypass priority mux gets one more
source on the dmem BSRAM -> m2 -> alu_a_val cone (G2) and the FIFO-head -> regfile ->
alu_a_val cone (G3); mitigate by keeping the m1 term as the final 2:1 stage and all
select terms precomputed from the raw_rs compares (the same compares that feed m1_*
flops today), not from the regfile data. (b) If the post-change `make timing` shows
G2/G3 now limit, the next step is replicating the slice-local address nets, not
reverting. Cycle count must be identical to 4,128,299 except for the small MUL
forward-slow-path savings (cosim cycles should drop slightly or stay equal; any rise
means a lost forward / extra stall bug). Log Fmax, cycles and post-change worst path.

title: Registered-lookahead branch-word buffer (BTB that stores the branch word) so a predicted branch/JAL costs no imem fetch slot
motivation:
Prior replays (r7s2, r9s2, r10s2) show a conventional direction/target predictor
has at most ~3.3% of cycles to win: ~68K redirects (54.4K cond. mispredicts +
13.7K rets) x ~2 cycles out of 4.128M. A better BHT, XOR fold, local history or
RAS can therefore never clear the 4.6% acceptance bar, and all three lost to
place-and-route noise. The machine is, however, fetch-bound rather than
redirect-bound: imem delivers a word in only ~78% of cycles (xorshift draw
< 100/128), so IPC is capped near 0.78 x (words consumed per word fetched);
2.93M retired instructions need >= 3.76M cycles of fetch alone, and the 2-entry
FIFO already hides most dmem / load-use / MDU stalls behind that limit. About
18% of retired instructions are conditional branches and ~2% are JAL, i.e. ~20%
of all imem fetch slots are spent on words whose only job is to steer the PC,
and CoreMark has only ~158 static branches (r9s2 replay), so a small buffer of
those words would hit almost always. The prior supply-side attempts (r10s1,
r11s1, r11s2) lost 4-32% because their hit signal (RAM read -> tag compare ->
group mux) was combinational from the pc flop into accept / PC enable / FIFO
write enables / decode. This design computes the lookup one cycle early and
registers it, so the hit decision reaches the fetch loop only as a flop.
