hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a branch-word buffer (BWB) to if_stage: a small direct-mapped array
(32-64 entries, explicit 16x4 RAM16SDP4-style slices or flops, no reset) that
stores ONLY conditional-branch and JAL words, as {tag = pc[..:2], 32-bit word}.
The existing 128x2 BHT, pred_hit and the direction-only EX verify stay
byte-identical, so the retirement stream is unchanged.

Lookahead (the Fmax-critical part). Each cycle, index the BWB with the address
the fetch will use NEXT cycle: idx_n = accept ? next_pc : pc (accept is already
flops + imem_ready, lesson r6s2). Register the result: bwb_hit_q,
bwb_word_q (32 flops), bwb_pc_q = idx_n. The tag compare and RAM read end at
flops; nothing downstream of them is combinational into the PC enable.
Redirect (a flop) loads pc <- redirect_target and also looks up redirect_target
the same way, or simply clears bwb_hit_q for one cycle (cheaper; costs nothing
versus today, because the first fetch after a redirect uses imem anyway).

Use. In a cycle where bwb_hit_q is 1 (the word for the current pc is already in
flops), the branch word does not need imem. The pc's own fetch slot is skipped:
  word0      = bwb_word_q (flop-sourced predecode: is_jal / is_br / imm_b /
               pc + imm adder start at a flop instead of the imem BSRAM output,
               so this path is shorter than today's imem_data one),
  pc1        = pred_hit(word0) ? pc + imm : pc + 4  (the same predictor, same
               BHT index from the pc flop),
  imem_addr  = bwb_hit_q ? pc1 : pc,   <- select is a FLOP, so it only adds one
               LUT level on the imem BSRAM address path; pc1 uses the flop
               word0 adder in parallel with nothing late,
  imem word  = the word at pc1, delivered when imem_ready as usual.
Both words (branch word from the BWB + the imem word at pc1) are pushed into
the fetch FIFO in one cycle (BWB word first). The FIFO grows to 3 entries (or
the skipped slot is only taken when q_v1 = 0 and q_v0 = 0 so at most two words
are pushed into an empty FIFO; accept stays flops + imem_ready, and a hit is
simply not taken while the FIFO is non-empty, so no late stall term reaches
the PC enable). When imem is not ready in that cycle only the BWB word is pushed
and pc advances to pc1, so a stall still makes forward progress. Net effect: a
buffered branch/JAL consumes zero imem slots, i.e. ~20% fewer fetch slots and
up to ~10-15% fewer cycles in the fetch-bound regime (hit rate and the
not-empty-FIFO restriction reduce this; the implementer must report both).

Fill. Train from the FIFO tail flops (not from imem_data, lesson r11s2): when a
branch/JAL word is accepted into the FIFO, write {pc tag, word} into the BWB
one cycle later from the registered q_in1 / q_pc1 flops (second write port is
just a registered write enable; RAM16SDP4 sync write). A stale or aliased entry
is harmless because bwb_word_q is only used when the stored tag equals the
lookup address; a tag collision with different code is impossible since the
full pc tag is compared, and self-modifying code does not occur (CoreMark is in
ROM-like imem). pc[31:2] tag width can be shortened to the used program range
(pc < 0x10000, 14 bits) because imem is bounded; keep the compare full-width
inside that range to remain exact.

Correctness / formal. The word supplied from the BWB is by construction the
word previously fetched from the same address; under riscv-formal's symbolic
imem the memory can return a different word the second time, so the BWB must be
disabled under `RISCV_FORMAL` (tie bwb_hit_q = 0 with an `ifdef`) exactly as
reg_file already swaps its model there; cosim and the cocotb unit tests exercise
the buffer on the real, immutable CoreMark image.

Offline replay already done (reference.py ISS on coremark.elf, 2,937,036 retired
instructions, whole run): branch/JAL words are 19.8% of retired instructions, and
a direct-mapped BWB hits 16.0% (16 entries), 17.1% (32), 18.4% (64), 18.7% (128)
of retired instructions, so 32 entries (about 32 x (32 + 12) bits = 6 RAM16SDP4
rows of 11 slices, or ~1.4K flops) already covers 86% of them.

Go / no-go for the implementer (re-check before writing RTL, with the ISS trace
of the timed region via test/cosim/reference.py): replay the dynamic stream
against a direct-mapped 32/64-entry BWB and report (a) the fraction of retired
instructions that are branch/JAL words hitting in the BWB, (b) the fraction of
those that occur with an empty FIFO in the fetch-bound steady state. Proceed
only if (a) >= 12% of retired instructions. Log cycles, Fmax and hit rate
separately in implementation_notes.md. If `make timing` shows the lookahead
RAM read (next_pc -> BWB address -> tag compare -> hit_q) as the worst path,
split it by indexing with `pc` only (lookup the pc-sequential and predicted
target candidates in parallel and register both).

lesson: - 2026-10-02 hyp-20261002-003-r12s2 (regression, -47.87%): A 32-entry branch-word buffer (BWB: LUT-RAM `{valid, tag, word}` read one cycle ahead into `bwb_hit_q`/`bwb_word_q` flops, `use_bwb = bwb_hit_q && !q_v0` skipping the imem slot of a buffered branch/JAL and pushing it plus the word at `pc1` in one cycle) scored 132.64 vs 254.45, which at fitness = 10 x Fmax / (cycles/1e6) and the champion's 4,128,299 cycles implies only ~50-55 MHz vs 105.04 even if cycles fell 10%, so the lookahead did not keep the hit off the fetch loop: the lookup address `pc_n = accept ? next_pc : (use_bwb ? pc1 : pc)` is itself the late cone (imem BSRAM `imem_data` -> predecode -> `pc + imm` adder -> `pred_hit` -> `next_pc` -> RAM read -> tag compare -> `bwb_hit_d`), `pcf = use_bwb ? pc1 : pc` puts a second 32-bit `pc + imm` adder plus an async `bht[a_tgt[8:2]]` read in series ahead of the existing predecode adder, and `imem_addr = use_bwb ? pc1 : pc` now drives the BSRAM address from that adder chain instead of the `pc` flop (inferred: cycles, Fmax, hit rate and the post-change worst path were not logged, and the diff has no implementation notes or go/no-go replay result); a "registered lookahead" only helps if the index it reads is itself a flop (index with `pc` and register both the sequential and predicted-target candidates, as the hypothesis's own fallback said) and the `pc + imm` / BHT-read path stays single-adder, so this is the sixth fetch-supply change (r8s0, r8s2, r10s1, r11s1, r11s2) to lose on the `imem_data`/`next_pc` cone, and with the redirect-bubble ceiling at ~3.3% and fetch-slot savings unproven, stop adding fetch-side lookup structures until one is shown flop -> flop in `make timing`.

title: 4-entry EX-updated return-address stack for `ret` (verified against the ID-stage successor pc) + 3-entry skid FIFO
motivation:
Cycle accounting of the 105.04 MHz champion (r9s1, logged in r12s0's notes): 2,922,017 retired
instructions, 4,128,299 cycles, ~823K of the bubble cycles are the imem-stall floor (0.78 words/cycle,
one word per ready cycle, so fetch supply is the long-run bottleneck), and the rest is back-end loss
dominated by redirects: ~61K BHT mispredicts + ~28K JALRs. JAL and BHT-taken branches are predicted in IF,
but JALR is never predicted, so every `ret` (the bulk of the 28K JALRs) pays the full registered-redirect
penalty: the wrong-path fetch slot at f+1, the blocked slot at f+2 (accept = !redirect) and the refill,
about 2.2 cycles each by the r8s0 / r10s2 accounting (a same-cycle-redirect fetch that saved exactly one
slot per redirect measured -1.6% cycles). Prior fetch-side losers (r8s0, r8s2, r10s1, r11s1, r11s2, r12s2)
all lost on the late imem_data / next_pc / accept cone with RAM or wide-enable structures; a 4-entry flop
shift stack whose update events come from EX flops (not from fetch) adds none of that. The r1s2 RAS was
tried on a core where the critical path was 200 ns, never on this one. Measured elsewhere: FIFO depth 3
= -0.95% cycles with Fmax held (r12s0 261.43), the only measured-positive cycle-exact lever left.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Cycle lever only (IPC), designed to leave every currently tied Fmax group alone (dmem BSRAM -> ID/EX,
FIFO head -> regfile -> ID/EX, EX forward -> compare -> reg_write / redirect).

1. Return-address stack in if_stage.sv: ras_e[0..3] (30-bit, pc[31:2]) + thermometer valids ras_v[3:0],
   a plain shift stack (top = ras_e[0], no read mux). It is updated ONLY from EX events (non-speculative,
   so wrong-path fetch never corrupts it, and no recovery logic is needed):
     push  : op leaving EX is a valid JAL/JALR with rd == x1 (call), !stall && !redirect_m (same
             gating as bht_upd_en); pushed value = pc_plus4[31:2] already computed in ex_stage.
     pop   : op leaving EX is a valid `ret` (in.instr == 32'h00008067, 32-bit compare of ID/EX flops),
             same gating; pop on empty is a no-op.
   Update enables come from ID/EX flops through a few LUTs (flop-only, well under the 14.9 ns tied
   groups); the stack never touches imem_data.
2. IF prediction: ret_word = (imem_data == 32'h00008067) (one 32-bit constant compare, 3 LUT levels,
   parallel to the existing is_jal / is_br + BHT select); ret_hit = ret_word && ras_v[0].
   next_pc = ret_hit ? {ras_e[0], 2'b00} : (existing jal/branch pred_hit ? pred_target : pc + 4).
   pred_hit (-> q_pt, out.pred_taken) = old pred_hit || ret_hit. The ras_e[0] term is a flop, so it
   only adds one data-mux input on the pc D path. Pop lags the fetch by the pipeline depth, so a
   back-to-back `ret; ret` pair can mispredict; that merely costs what a JALR costs today.
3. EX verification without carrying the predicted target through the FIFO / ID/EX: when a ret is in EX,
   the decode source is by construction the NEXT fetched word, and its address is the predicted target.
   if_id_w.pc (= q_v0 ? {q_pc0,2'b00} : pc, already built from flops) is routed to ex_stage as succ_pc.
     tgt_bad      = in.pred_taken && in.ctrl.is_jalr && (rs1[31:2] != succ_pc[31:2])
     redirect_d   = ((actual_taken ^ in.pred_taken) || tgt_bad) && in.valid && !redirect_m
     redirect_target_d = (in.pred_taken && !(in.ctrl.is_jalr && !rs1[1])) ? pc_plus4
                       : in.ctrl.is_jalr ? {jalr_sum[31:1],1'b0} : branch_target
   The rs1[1] term keeps the misaligned-target trap architecturally exact (predicted ret with a
   misaligned rs1: actual_taken = 0 -> redirect to pc+4, PC stays 4-aligned). A predicted ret is only
   produced for imm == 0, so rs1 == target. The 30-bit equality is 3 LUT levels after the forward mux,
   shorter than the existing 33-bit carry-chain compare. rvfi pc_next / trap logic is unchanged.
4. Bundle the measured cycle-exact stack-on: generalize the skid FIFO from 2 to 3 entries (thermometer
   valids, accept = imem_ready && !redirect && !qv[DEPTH-1], decode source `qv[0] ? q_in[0] : imem_data`
   unchanged; -0.95% cycles measured, Fmax held in r12s0).

Go / no-go before spending time: replay the CoreMark retirement trace with the EX-updated 4-entry RAS and
count correctly predicted `ret`s; expected >= ~20K of the 28K JALRs. Expected cycle saving 1.2-1.5% from
the RAS plus 0.95% from the FIFO, i.e. ~2.5-3% fitness if Fmax is flat. That is below the 4.6% bar on
its own; it is the best remaining cycle lever that does not extend the imem_data / late-select cones,
and place-and-route spread (103.4 - 106.9 MHz across recent runs) can add to it. Log cycles and Fmax
separately and run `make timing` once to confirm the pc D cone and the redirect cone are not the new limiter.

lesson: - 2026-10-03 hyp-20261002-001-r13s0 (regression, +1.65%): A 4-entry EX-updated return-address stack (push/pop from ID/EX flops, `ret_hit` = 32-bit `imem_data == 32'h00008067` compare steering `next_pc`, verification by `tgt_bad = pred_taken && is_jalr && rs1[31:2] != succ_pc` with `succ_pc` = `if_id_w.pc`) bundled with the 3-entry skid FIFO scored 258.66 vs 254.45, which is BELOW the FIFO-3-alone result (r12s0, 261.43) and far under the ~+3% expected, so the RAS added nothing net (-1.06% vs r12s0, inside the ~2-3% seed spread) even though its ~28K JALRs x ~2.2 bubbles is only a ~1.2-1.5% cycle ceiling; the likely cost is Fmax from the new late terms it put on the EX forward -> compare -> `redirect_d` / `redirect_target_d` cone (an extra OR term and a `rs1[1]`-selected target mux fed from the forward-mux output) plus the `ret_hit` term and a flop-fed 4th input on the `next_pc` mux behind the late `imem_data` (inferred: cycles, Fmax, correctly predicted `ret` count and `make timing` were not logged, and the hypothesis's own go/no-go ret-prediction replay was never reported); a ~1% cycle lever cannot be resolved against place-and-route noise and must add zero logic to the redirect/`next_pc` cones to survive, so run the offline `ret` replay and log cycles and Fmax separately before building any further JALR/return predictor, and keep the FIFO-3 depth change as the only stacked baseline.

title: Sequential-lookahead I-word cache: registered pc+4 lookup so a hit is a flop and fills imem stall slots
motivation:
Logged cycle accounting: 2.92M retired instructions in 4.128M cycles (CPI 1.41)
against a hard fetch bound of 2.92M / 0.78 = 3.74M, because imem_ready is
address-independent and low 22% of the time. Every back-end / predictor /
FIFO-depth lever is therefore capped at ~9% total (FIFO depth saturates at
-1.4% cycles), and the cycle-exact Fmax retimings are exhausted (dmem BSRAM ->
ID/EX, EX forward -> ALU/compare and FIFO head -> regfile are all tied at
~14.9-15.0 ns). The only lever that moves the fetch bound itself is a second
instruction source that can deliver a word in an imem-stall cycle. Four
attempts (r8s1 64-word flop cache, r10s1 256-word LUT-RAM cache, r11s1 128-word
stall-bypass cache, r12s2 branch-word buffer) cut cycles 5-11% but lost 25-50%
Fmax, always for the same reason: the cache lookup index was a late signal
(next_pc after predecode / pc + imm / pred_hit) or the hit fed accept, PC enable
and FIFO write enables through RAM read -> tag compare in the same cycle.
The LESSONS recipe for a third try is explicit: take `hit` out of `accept` by
computing it a cycle ahead into a flop, index the RAM from flops only, and fill
from flops. This hypothesis is that recipe, with coverage deliberately limited
to the sequential path so the lookup index is early.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a 128-entry direct-mapped word cache (explicit 16x4 `distributed_ram`
slices, same style as reg_file: tag + valid in a small flop/LUT-RAM array, word
in RAM16SDP4 slices) inside if_stage, strictly as a stall-slot filler:

1. Registered lookahead. Every cycle the cache is read with an index built only
   from flops: `idx_n = accept ? (pc + 4) : pc` (accept is already flops +
   handshake: imem_ready && !redirect && !q_v1). The read result is registered
   at the end of the cycle: `cw_q` (32-bit word), and ONE flag flop
   `c_ok_q <= tag_match && !redirect && !(accept && pred_hit)`, i.e. "the word
   in cw_q is the word for the pc that will be in the pc flop next cycle".
   `pred_hit` already feeds the pc D input, so it adds only one more flop D
   cone of the same depth, nothing to a PC enable. After a predicted-taken
   branch / JAL or a redirect c_ok_q is 0 and fetch simply uses imem (no loss
   versus today). Loop bodies and straight-line runs after the first word of a
   block are the covered case.
2. Hit never touches the RAM in the consuming cycle. Next cycle:
   `accept = (imem_ready || c_ok_q) && !redirect && !q_v1` (flop OR flop),
   `fword = c_ok_q ? cw_q : imem_data` with the select a single flop (duplicate
   it with syn_preserve for fan-out), and fword drives the existing predecode,
   FIFO tail/head D inputs and next_pc exactly as imem_data does today. The
   decode source (`q_v0 ? q_in0 : imem_data`) and the raw rs1/rs2 regfile /
   load-use feed are NOT changed: they keep reading the live imem word or the
   FIFO head, never the cache output (lesson r4s2: do not put a queue/bypass mux
   on the regfile-read feed). When c_ok_q is set and the head is empty, the
   cache word is only pushed into the FIFO tail/head (banked) and ID consumes it
   from q_in0 the following cycle if the live-imem word is not the same slot;
   simplest correct form: when c_ok_q && !imem_ready the word goes into the
   FIFO (q_v0 path) and `word_avail` = q_v0 || imem_ready as today.
3. Fill. On every accept the delivered word {tag, fword} is written to the RAM
   at index pc[8:2]; write enable = accept (flops + handshake), write data =
   fword. No second pc + imm adder and no predecoded fields in the cache (r11s1
   paid for that adder). Tag compare uses pc bits [31:9] reduced to the few bits
   the 1 MB address space needs (pc[19:9] -> 11 bits stored in LUT-RAM slices),
   or fewer with aliasing allowed only if the tag array is exact (a false hit
   would break CoreMark CRCs).
4. Correctness. The cache never holds speculative data other than instruction
   words fetched at their own pc, imem is read-only for CoreMark, so a hit is
   always the right word (no invalidation needed; clear valid bits with a reset
   sequence or a valid flop per entry gated by the reset). Redirect clears
   c_ok_q.

Go / no-go before spending synthesis time (the implementer should report these
and stop if they fail): replay the CoreMark pc trace offline and compute (a) the
fraction of fetches whose pc equals the previous accepted pc + 4 (sequential
coverage) and (b) the hit rate of a 128-entry direct-mapped cache on exactly
those fetches. Expected cycle saving ~= 0.22 * coverage * hit_rate of fetch
slots; proceed only if >= ~5% of cycles. Log cycles, Fmax, hit rate and the
post-change worst path in implementation_notes so the cycle / Fmax split is
known (earlier cache attempts never logged it).

Expected effect: cycles -5..-7% (r11s1's full-coverage stall-bypass got -9.5%;
sequential-only coverage keeps roughly 60-70% of that), Fmax roughly flat if
the only new late cone is one 2:1 mux plus one flag-flop D input; a 2:1 mux with
a flop select on fword was the suspected ~8% Fmax cost in r11s2, so the
mux select must be one syn_preserve'd flop and cw_q must be the only second
source. If the post-change `make timing` worst path is lfsr/imem_data -> fword
-> predecode/pc, fall back to feeding cw_q into the FIFO tail only (never into
predecode), which forces a one-slot bubble after each cache-served taken branch
but keeps pc's D cone identical to the champion.

lesson: - 2026-10-03 hyp-20261002-002-r13s1 (regression, -7.08%): The recipe the r11s1/r12s2 lessons asked for (128-word sequential-lookahead `distributed_ram` cache read every cycle at `accept ? pc+4 : pc` and registered into `cw_q`/`c_ok_q`, so a hit is a flop and `use_c = c_ok_q && !imem_ready` only fills stall slots, fill from `fword` at `pc[8:2]`) scored 236.44 vs 254.45, i.e. ~97.6 MHz at the champion's 4,128,299 cycles (fitness = 10 x Fmax / (cycles/1e6)) or ~93 MHz if cycles fell the hoped 5%, so the loss shrank from -15% to -48% on earlier caches to -7% but did not reach break-even, and the residual cost is most likely structural rather than the hit path: a second 32-bit `pc + imm` predecode adder for `cw_q`, `pc` converted from an enable flop to a `pc_d` select chain (`sel_live` over `pc_early`), an `fword` 2:1 mux on the FIFO D / cache-write data, `accept` gaining a `|| c_ok_q` term, and a `pc4` incrementer -> RAM address -> tag compare -> `c_ok_q` D cone that also merges the late `!(accept && pred_hit)` (inferred: cycles, Fmax, hit rate, post-change `make timing` and the offline sequential-coverage go/no-go were not logged and the diff has no implementation notes); this is the seventh fetch-supply change to lose on the `imem_data`/`pc` cone, so stop spending rounds on I-word caches/buffers unless the offline replay and a `make timing` run show the worst path is still the champion's dmem/regfile group, and log cycles, Fmax and hit rate so the cycle gain can be separated from the Fmax cost.

title: Flop-top return stack predicting canonical ret, verified against the next decode-source PC (no pending-target storage), plus XOR-folded BHT index
motivation:
The remaining predictor budget on the 254.45 core is small and well measured. The timed CoreMark
region has ~529.6K conditional branches (128x2 bimodal BHT, index pc[8:2], mispredicts 54.4K),
13,735 JAL calls and 13,735 `ret`s (word 0x00008067; 100% of all JALRs, 0 other JALRs). Every
mispredict and every `ret` pays the registered-redirect penalty (~2 bubbles + the 22% imem stall
on the refetch, ~2.3 cycles), so rets are ~31K cycles (0.75%) and the 14K branch mispredicts that
an XOR-folded index removes (54.4K -> 40.7K at the same 128 entries, r7s2 replay) are another
~32K cycles (0.8%). r7s2 built this exact pair and measured -1.47% cycles (4.363M -> 4.299M),
matching the replay, but landed at 96.7 MHz vs ~99.5 and lost the round on Fmax; r10s2 (fold
only, LUT-RAM) landed inside the seed spread. The Fmax loss in r7s2 is plausibly the extra
state it added to the EX/redirect side: a 2-entry pending-target FIFO (30-bit entries, push at IF,
pop from EX, cleared by redirect), an rs1==pending compare fed by that FIFO head, and a reordered
redirect_target_d mux. This hypothesis keeps the same cycle gain but removes all of that state.
Honest size: ~1.5% fewer cycles; with the 4.6% acceptance bar it only wins if Fmax holds or rises,
so the design rule is: every new input is a flop or the imem word, nothing new on the EX adder
outputs, no new fan-out on pc/accept/imem_data beyond one extra next_pc leg.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Part 1 (zero storage): fold the BHT index, idx[k] = pc[k+2] ^ pc[k+7] (k=0..6), for both the IF
read (bht[idx(pc)]) and the training index (bht_upd_idx = idx(in.pc), registered into upd_idx_q
as today). One 2-input XOR between the pc flops and the 128:1 read mux; counter policy, reset
value 2'b01 and the registered read-modify-write are unchanged.

Part 2 (return-address stack, canonical ret only):
* if_stage predecodes imem_data == 32'h00008067 (ret) and imem_data[6:0]==1101111 &&
  imem_data[11:7]==5'd1 (jal ra, call). Calls push pc+4 (the existing `pc + 4` already computed for
  next_pc) onto a 4-deep SHIFT stack of 30-bit flops: ras0 is the top, a push shifts
  ras0->ras1->ras2->ras3 and loads ras0, a pop shifts back up. The top is therefore a flop
  (no pointer mux), and push/pop fire only when the word is accepted (accept = imem_ready &&
  !redirect && !q_v1, unchanged). Wrong-path pollution is tolerated (accuracy only, no repair),
  and ras reset is not needed (a garbage prediction is only a mispredict).
* A predicted ret is a third next_pc leg: next_pc = pred_hit ? pred_target : ret_pred ?
  {ras0,2'b00} : pc+4, and pred_hit/pred_taken-carried bit for the word is set for ret_pred
  as for JAL/branches (q_pt0/q_pt1 and if_id_t.pred_taken already travel through the FIFO and
  ID/EX, so NO new pipeline or FIFO fields are added).
* Verification in EX without any stored target. A predicted ret is exactly `jalr x0,0(ra)`
  (imm = 0), so its target is the forwarded rs1, and the word that follows a predicted ret in
  the fetch stream is by construction the one fetched at the predicted target. When the ret is in
  EX the decode-source word (if_id_w.pc = q_v0 ? {q_pc0,2'b00} : pc, already a flop-selected
  mux) is therefore the word after the ret, i.e. its pc IS the predicted target (checked for
  live word, FIFO head, dmem-stall hold with the word banked, and squash-by-older-redirect, where
  the ret is dropped and redirect_d is masked by !redirect_m anyway). core.sv passes if_id_w.pc
  into ex_stage as `dec_pc`. In ex_stage:
      ret_pred = in.ctrl.is_jalr && in.pred_taken;
      ret_ok   = (rs1[31:2] == dec_pc[31:2]) && (rs1[1:0] == 2'b00);
      redirect_d = ret_pred ? !ret_ok : (actual_taken ^ in.pred_taken);   (all still && in.valid && !redirect_m)
  The 30-bit equality sits behind the same fwd_rs1_sel/in.rs1_val mux and has the same depth as
  the existing 32-bit cmp_eq (rs1 == rs2), so it is not a new deepest cone and does not touch
  jalr_sum / the adder carry chain.
* redirect_target_d keeps its shape but handles ret_pred: on a mispredicted ret redirect to the
  actual target {jalr_sum[31:1],0} when rs1[1:0]==0, else to pc+4 (misaligned target is
  trapped by the existing misalign_jump logic: rvfi pc_next = pc+4, no redirect to a
  misaligned address, reg_write cleared). Concretely redirect_target_d = (in.pred_taken &&
  !(in.ctrl.is_jalr && !rs1[1])) ? pc_plus4 : in.ctrl.is_jalr ? jalr target : branch_target.
  The select terms are in.pred_taken/is_jalr flops and rs1[1] (forward-mux output), not the
  compare result.
* Everything else (misalign fault, pc_next, rd_wdata = pc+4, EX/MEM bubble on redirect_m,
  BHT training only for branches) is unchanged, so the RVFI stream and riscv-formal pc_fwd /
  liveness / unique checks see the same architectural behavior; the formal run must exercise
  predicted rets with symbolic rs1 (equal to dec_pc, unequal, misaligned).

Go/no-go for the implementer: log cycles, Fmax and mispredict/ret-redirect counts. Expect
~4.06-4.07M cycles vs 4,128,299 (-1.4..-1.6%). If `make timing` shows the new rs1==dec_pc compare,
the ras enable fan-out or the 3-way next_pc mux on the worst path, drop Part 2's EX verify
fan-in first (fall back to Part 1 only), since a 1.5% gain cannot pay for any Fmax loss.
Optionally bundle the already-measured Fmax-free 3-entry fetch FIFO (r12s0: -0.95% cycles at
held Fmax) as the only other change, to bring the total cycle cut to ~2.5%.

lesson: - 2026-10-03 hyp-20261002-003-r13s2 (regression, -4.24%): Re-building the r7s2 return-stack + XOR-folded-BHT pair with every extra EX state removed (4-deep flop-top shift stack, no pending-target FIFO, `ret_ok = rs1[31:2] == dec_pc` against the decode-source `if_id_w.pc`, `redirect_target_d` select `in.pred_taken && !(is_jalr && !rs1[1])`) scored 243.66 vs 254.45, which at fitness = 10 x Fmax / (cycles/1e6) implies ~99-100 MHz vs 105.04 even if the replay's -1.5% cycles were fully realized (r7s2 with the FIFO was 96.7 MHz), so the pending-target FIFO explained only ~3 of the ~5% Fmax loss and the rest is common to all three return-stack builds (r7s2, r13s0 -1.06% vs FIFO-3-alone, r13s2): the 32-bit `imem_data == 32'h00008067` compare as an extra `next_pc` leg behind the late imem word, plus a 30-bit `rs1` (forward-mux output) vs `dec_pc` (a `q_v0 ? q_pc0 : pc` mux, so not a bare flop) compare ending in `redirect_d`, and the `rs1[1]`-gated target select, which together are not 'zero new logic' on the redirect/`next_pc` cones as the hypothesis claimed (inferred: cycles, Fmax, correctly predicted `ret` count and `make timing` were not logged and there are no implementation notes; the XOR fold alone was already noise in r10s2); a ~1.5% ret lever (13.7K rets x ~2.3 cycles) loses to a ~4-5% Fmax cost every time it touches those cones, so stop building return predictors unless the ret decode is a predecoded flop and verification is a registered compare off the critical path (e.g. checked one cycle later in MEM), and always log cycles and Fmax separately so the cycle gain is not inferred from the fitness.

title: Compare-last EX endpoints (redirect / reg_write / BHT as cond ? E1 : E0 with flop-only E0/E1) + 3-entry skid FIFO
motivation:
The champion (105.04 MHz, 4,128,299 cycles) reported its worst path as
u_id/reg_q.m1_rs2 -> u_ex/reg_q.ctrl.reg_write with 30 logic cells / 11 levels
(arrival 14.96 ns): the m1 select flop -> `& ex_mem_w_en` -> fanout-32 forward
mux -> 33-bit compare carry chain -> branch_op[2] eq/lt select -> `^ branch_op[0]`
-> branch_taken -> misalign_branch (`& branch_target[1:0] != 0`) -> misalign_fault
-> actual_taken -> `^ pred_taken` -> `& valid & !redirect_m` -> redirect_d, and the
same compare result feeds ctrl_with_trap.reg_write (plus the `ex_busy || redirect_m`
clear) and bht_upd_taken. So after the carry chain the compare result still passes
through 3-4 LUT levels of purely flop-derived qualification (is_branch, is_jump,
pred_taken, valid, redirect_m, misalign terms, ex_busy) before reaching a flop.
Earlier attempts to shorten this cone (r10s0, r10s2, r11s0) only removed the
compare -> reg_write leg (jump-only clear, which is NOT cycle-exact for a taken
misaligned BRANCH unless the redirect/trap stays correct) and left the
redirect_d / BHT legs, and were judged against ~3% place-and-route noise; none of
them restructured ALL three compare endpoints at once, and none logged a
post-change `make timing`. The only measured-positive, Fmax-free cycle lever on
record is the 3-entry skid FIFO (r12s0: -0.95% cycles, 4,089,085 cycles, Fmax
106.9 MHz, but only +2.74% fitness so under the 4.6% acceptance bar on its own).
Bundling the two gives a cycle gain that is real (~1%) plus an Fmax shot at the
worst measured group instead of repeating either alone.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Two cycle-exact edits.

(1) rtl/ex_stage.sv: make the branch compare result the LAST-arriving input of
every endpoint it feeds, by precomputing, from flops and the 2-bit low parts of
the jump/branch target adders only, the endpoint value for cond = 0 and cond = 1.
  is_br = in.ctrl.is_branch, is_j = in.ctrl.is_jump, pt = in.pred_taken
  mis_b = (branch_target[1:0] != 0)              // pc+imm low bits, no compare
  mis_j = is_j && (jump_target[1:0] != 0)        // 2-bit add after fwd mux, parallel with the carry chain
  A0 = is_j && !mis_j                             // actual_taken if the branch cond is false
  A1 = (is_br || is_j) && !((is_br && mis_b) || mis_j)   // actual_taken if cond true
  ok = in.valid && !redirect_m
  RD0 = (A0 ^ pt) && ok ;  RD1 = (A1 ^ pt) && ok         // redirect_d
  RW0 = in.ctrl.reg_write && !mis_j && !ex_busy && !redirect_m ;
  RW1 = in.ctrl.reg_write && !((is_br && mis_b) || mis_j) && !ex_busy && !redirect_m
  (the existing `ex_busy || redirect_m` clear of reg_q.ctrl / valid stays for the
  other ctrl bits; only reg_write's D is built this way)
Then, with raw = branch_op[2] ? cmp_lt : cmp_eq and inv = branch_op[0], each
endpoint E in {redirect_d, ctrl.reg_write D, bht_upd_taken(=cond)} is
  E = raw ? (inv ? E0 : E1) : (inv ? E1 : E0)
where the two data inputs are flop-only functions: one LUT5 (two LUT4 + the slice
MUX2) after the compare instead of 3-4 chained LUTs. cmp_eq / cmp_lt, the forward
mux, the adders and everything else are untouched; the order of evaluation inside
the endpoint changes, not the function: redirect, reg_write, trap clear, pc_next
(RVFI only), BHT training and MDU start stay bit-identical (cosim cycle count and
riscv-formal `ill` / `pc_fwd` / `liveness` must be unchanged vs the champion).
`ctrl_with_trap.is_illegal` (RVFI only, pruned from the timed netlist) can keep
the existing misalign_fault form.

(2) rtl/if_stage.sv: generalise the q_v0/q_v1 skid FIFO to DEPTH = 3 exactly as
measured in r12s0 (thermometer valids qv[2:0], accept = imem_ready && !redirect &&
!qv[2], head = entry 0, decode source `qv[0] ? q_in[0] : imem_data` unchanged, so
the regfile-read / load-use feed and the redirect / flush cones are untouched).
Expected -0.95% cycles (4,089,085) with Fmax unchanged.

title: Non-stalling pipelined MUL (result taken from the pp flops in MEM, load-use-style interlock) stacked on a 3-entry skid FIFO
motivation:
Logged cycle accounting of the 254.45 champion: 2.92M retired instructions in 4.128M cycles. The imem-stall
fetch floor is 2.92M / 0.78 = 3.74M, so only ~9% of cycles are back-end loss in total. The tied Fmax groups
(dmem BSRAM -> ID alu_a_val, FIFO head -> regfile -> ID/EX, EX forward -> ALU) have resisted ten
cone-local retimings, fetch-supply structures (I-caches, loop buffers, branch-word buffers) lost 4-48% on the
imem_data / next_pc cone seven times in a row, and return predictors lost on the EX redirect cone. What is
left is a back-end structural change that adds no logic to those cones.
The earlier cycle accounting in log.jsonl counted ~94K MULs in the timed region (matrix / CRC kernels).
After r7s1 each costs one stall cycle: the op sits in EX for a second cycle (res_valid raised at the end of
E0, released in E1), EX/MEM gets a bubble and the whole front end holds via stall_id = ... || ex_busy, even
when nothing behind the MUL consumes its result. With 22% imem stalls the fetch is the bottleneck, so the FIFO
cannot hide that bubble: ~94K cycles = ~2.3% of 4.128M. A 3-entry FIFO (r12s0, 261.43, Fmax held at ~106.9,
-0.95% cycles) is the one measured Fmax-neutral cycle lever and was never accepted on its own because
+2.74% is under the 4.6% bar; this bundles it with a second independent cycle lever.

Make MUL (low word) a pipelined op instead of a stalling one, stacked on the 3-entry FIFO.
(1) MUL (not MULH*/DIV*/REM*) no longer raises ex_busy when no EX/MEM forward hits it (fwd_hit = 0). In its
single EX cycle the DSPs already read the ID/EX rs1_val / rs2_val flops (a_id / b_id) and the pp_* flops
capture at the end of EX exactly as today; the op leaves EX normally into EX/MEM with a new flop `mul_low`
set (alu_result don't-care). In MEM the result is mul_low_sum = pp_ll + {pp_lh[15:0] + pp_hl[15:0], 16'b0}
(the existing expression, from the pp flops, which hold for exactly the one cycle the MUL sits in MEM; a dmem

regfile write (MEM stage) and the ID m2 bypass then see the MUL result like any other write-back value.
(2) A MUL's result is not in EX/MEM.alu_result while it is in MEM, so for the hazard unit a pipelined MUL
behaves like a load: the existing 5-bit id_ex_rd vs rs1/rs2 load-use compare is gated by
(id_ex ctrl.mem_read | id_ex mul_low) instead of mem_read alone, giving one bubble for an adjacent consumer and
zero for a consumer two or more slots behind (the m2 bypass in ID covers it). The extra term is one OR of two

unchanged Fmax. That is below the 4.6% bar on its own, so the value of this attempt is the combined measured
cycle count and whether the MEM-stage MUL low-word sum (two chained carry chains, 16-bit + 32-bit) stays under
the BSRAM -> ID/ID-EX group. Fallbacks the implementer should apply if `make timing` shows the sum as the
worst path: keep the FIFO-3 change and the pipelined MUL, but add a registered 16-bit `lh + hl` low sum in
the E1 cycle only for the MUL-with-consumer-in-ID case (consumer adjacency known from the hazard compare), or
drop piece (1) and ship FIFO-3 alone.

title: Flop-indexed taken-branch fold: a 64-entry LUT-RAM branch-word table, read one cycle ahead from the pc flop, lets a predicted-taken branch skip its own imem slot (fill from EX flops, 2-word FIFO push, depth 3)
motivation:
Every cycle-side predictor idea tried so far is capped at ~1-2% of cycles
(bimodal-128 leaves ~54K direction mispredicts, gshare/local-history/XOR-fold/
bigger BHT are within noise, a return stack is worth ~1.4% and lost 4-5% Fmax
three times). The only large predictor-addressable loss left is FETCH SUPPLY:
the offline ISS replay in r6s2 shows the 22% imem stall bounds the run at
2.92M retired / 0.78 words per cycle = 3.74M cycles, and the core takes
4.128M. Taken control transfers (294K taken conditional branches + 49K JAL,
~340K = ~11.6% of all retired instructions) each burn an imem slot to fetch
the branch word itself, even though the BHT/JAL predecode already knows the
branch is taken and where it goes. If the branch WORD is supplied from a small
table instead of the imem port, the imem slot is spent on the TARGET word in
the same cycle (two words per imem slot), which is the only way to push supply
above 0.78 words/cycle. At ~50-60% fold coverage that removes ~170-200K fetch
slots = ~0.22-0.26M cycles = 5-6% of 4.128M (up to ~10% at full coverage).
Past fetch-supply tries (r8s1, r10s1, r11s1, r11s2, r12s2, r13s1) all lost
3-48% Fmax, and their post-mortems agree on WHY: the hit/lookup fed the late
imem_data -> predecode adder -> next_pc cone, the lookup index was a late
computed address (r12s2: `pc_n = accept ? next_pc : ...`), a second
`pc + imm` adder or an imem_data 2:1 data mux was added ahead of the FIFO D
inputs, or the cache fill was taken from imem_data / pred_target. This
hypothesis is built to avoid each of those specific causes.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a fold path to rtl/if_stage.sv with these hard rules (each one answers a
recorded failure):

1. Table: 64 entries, direct-mapped by pc[7:2], on explicit
   `syn_ramstyle="distributed_ram"` 16x4 slices (RAM16SDP4, 4 groups of 16
   entries, same style as reg_file.sv; no reset, so a separate 64-flop `valid`
   vector with sync reset is used). Entry = {tag = pc[15:8] (8b), word (32b),
   target[15:2] (14b)}. Fold is only allowed when pc[31:16]==0 and the target
   [31:16]==0 (text is far below 64KB; this makes the tag exact, program memory
   is not self-modifying, so a tag hit implies the stored word is the word at
   that pc). No `pc + imm` adder is added: the target is taken from the
   existing EX `branch_target` adder at fill time.

2. Fill from EX flops only (never from imem_data / pred_target / FIFO D):
   when an op leaving EX has `in.valid && in.pred_taken && !stall && !redirect_m`
   (it was predicted taken, so it is a JAL or a taken-predicted BRANCH; JALR is
   never predicted), write table[in.pc[7:2]] <= {in.pc[15:8], in.instr,
   branch_target[15:2]} and set valid. Write data are ID/EX flop outputs and
   the existing EX adder output: zero new load on the imem_data / next_pc cone.
   Entry validity at LOOKUP is additionally qualified with the live BHT
   prediction (see 3), so a branch whose counter later drops below 2 is simply
   not folded; a JAL (word[6:0]==1101111) is always folded.

3. Lookahead is registered and flop-indexed: in each cycle compute the lookup
   index for the address that `pc` will hold NEXT from flops and the imem
   handshake only: idx_next = redirect ? redirect_target_m[7:2]
                             : accept ? (pc[7:2] + 6'd1) : pc[7:2]
   (a 6-bit incrementer and flop-selected muxes; `accept` is the existing
   flop + imem_ready term; when the word just accepted is itself predicted
   taken, next pc is the late `next_pc`, so do NOT look up: set hit_q <= 0 for
   that cycle, accepting a small coverage loss instead of building the late
   index chain that killed r12s2). Register `hit_q` (valid && tag match &&
   (is_jal || bht_pred_bit)), `fw_q` (32b word), `ft_q` (14b target) at the end
   of the cycle. The BHT bit for idx_next is read with the same flop-derived
   index (the BHT array itself is unchanged: 128x2 flops, same update path).
   No signal derived from imem_data reaches idx_next, hit_q, fw_q or ft_q.

4. Fold action (cycle where pc == X and `fold = hit_q && !redirect`, both
   flops): imem_addr = fold ? {16'b0, ft_q, 2'b00} : pc  (one 2:1 LUT whose
   select and both data inputs are flops, in front of the imem BSRAM address
   only). The branch word X is NOT fetched; it is pushed into the FIFO from
   fw_q with pc = X and pred_taken = 1. The imem word delivered this cycle
   (the target T, valid iff imem_ready) is pushed right behind it. Predecode,
   BHT index and the `pc + imm` adder use base `fold ? T : pc` where T and the
   select are flops (so the existing single predecode adder is reused, no
   second adder; imem_data stays the only late input exactly as today).
   pc <= imem_ready ? next_pc(T-word) : T  (if the target word is not
   delivered the PC simply becomes T and fetch retries at T; the branch word
   was already banked, so the fold is not repeated).

5. FIFO: depth 3 thermometer-valid FIFO (the cycle-exact depth lever of r12s0:
   -0.95% cycles, Fmax held). A fold needs room for 2 pushes and is only
   allowed when qv[1]==0 (a flop term); the non-fold accept term stays
   `imem_ready && !redirect && !qv[DEPTH-1]` (flops + handshake). The decode
   source stays `qv[0] ? q_in[0] : imem_data` -- it is NOT changed. To keep
   program order in a fold cycle with an empty FIFO the live word (T) must not
   be decoded ahead of the banked branch word, so: in a fold cycle the live
   word is always banked (`word_avail = qv[0] || (imem_ready && !fold)`,
   bank condition `stall_id || fold`), and ID sees a bubble that cycle. This
   costs one decode slot but the machine is fetch-bound (decode idles ~22% of
   cycles anyway), and the extra banked word then hides a later imem stall.
   Only flops (`fold`, `qv[]`) join the existing flush_if / accept / bank terms.

6. Everything downstream is unchanged: the folded word travels with
   pred_taken=1, so EX verifies by the existing direction-only XOR and its own
   `in.pc + imm` target (which equals the table target since tag+word are
   exact). A mispredicted fold redirects exactly like a mispredicted fetch
   (registered redirect clears FIFO, hit_q and the lookahead). No ID/EX/regfile
   / hazard / MDU change, so the tied dmem BSRAM -> ID alu_a_val and
   FIFO head -> regfile -> ID/EX groups are not touched.

Go / no-go (do this before RTL, from the offline ISS replay already used in
r6s2/r10s2 and cosim): replay the timed CoreMark trace with the real
bench_stall_gen sequence and a fetch-slot model (1 word/accept, depth-3 FIFO,
64-entry direct-mapped table, lookahead only when the previous accepted word
was not predicted-taken or after redirect/stall). Report folds/branch coverage,
predicted cycles and mispredicts. If predicted cycle reduction is < 4% (e.g.
conflict misses in the 64-entry table), grow the table to 128 entries (tag
pc[15:9]) before building; if still < 4%, fall back to the smaller deliverable
(depth-3 FIFO only, i.e. r12s0) rather than a fold that cannot pay. Log
cycles, Fmax, fold count and the post-change `make timing` worst path
separately, so the cycle gain can be told apart from any Fmax change.

Expected: cycles -5..-6% (4.128M -> ~3.9M), Fmax roughly flat (all new nets are
flop -> short logic -> flop or RAM -> compare -> flop; the only touches on a
late cone are a flop-selected 2:1 mux in front of the imem address pins and a
flop-selected predecode base mux), net fitness ~+5..+6%. This is the one
predictor-category lever whose ceiling clears the 4.6% acceptance bar; if
place-and-route shows the imem_addr mux or base mux on the worst path, the
fallback is to register the folded target into `pc` one cycle early (pc <= T
at the lookahead cycle) instead of muxing imem_addr.

title: Two-direction shifter (no bit-reverse muxes) on the EX result AND-OR, stacked on a 3-entry skid FIFO
motivation:
The 105.04 MHz champion (r9s1, 4,128,299 cycles) sits on three near-tied path
groups around 15.0 ns arrival: (A) m1_rs2 -> compare -> ctrl.reg_write, (B) dmem
BSRAM -> load extract -> ID rs?_val, (C) m1_alu_a -> forward mux -> adder/shifter ->
alu_result (10 cells in r14s0's `make timing`, through cpu/u_ex/u_alu). Prior rounds
showed that fixing one group in isolation is invisible (r6s0, r10s0, r11s0, r14s0
all inside the 2-3% seed spread), and that cycle-only levers are small: the 3-entry
skid FIFO is a clean, Fmax-flat -0.95% cycles (r12s0 261.43, +2.7%), and the compare-
last rewrite of group A added only +0.9% on top (r14s0 263.77). Group C is the one
group that has not had a standalone cone rewrite: the shared right shifter is wrapped
in `rev32(a)` on the input and `rev32(result)` on the output, so the shift leg of the
EX result is forward-mux -> (sh_left ? rev : a) mux -> 5 shift stages -> (sh_left ?
rev : x) mux merged with the sel_shift AND -> 9-leg AND-OR. The input reversal is a
full extra LUT level (and a doubled fan-in 6-input function with the forward mux) on
the late operand-A net, and a[i]/a[31-i] both load every forward-mux output.
Removing it is IPC-neutral and touches no ID-side cone (B) nor the compare cone (A).
The FIFO-3 half is the only already-measured cycle gain that is Fmax-free; bundled
with a shifter that is one level shallower, the sum has a chance to clear the 4.6%
acceptance bar that neither piece clears alone.

group that has not had a standalone cone rewrite: the shared right shifter is wrapped
in `rev32(a)` on the input and `rev32(result)` on the output, so the shift leg of the
EX result is forward-mux -> (sh_left ? rev : a) mux -> 5 shift stages -> (sh_left ?
rev : x) mux merged with the sel_shift AND -> 9-leg AND-OR. The input reversal is a
full extra LUT level (and a doubled fan-in 6-input function with the forward mux) on
the late operand-A net, and a[i]/a[31-i] both load every forward-mux output.

The FIFO-3 half is the only already-measured cycle gain that is Fmax-free; bundled
with a shifter that is one level shallower, the sum has a chance to clear the 4.6%
acceptance bar that neither piece clears alone.

lesson: - 2026-10-03 hyp-20261003-001-r15s0 (regression, +0.85%): Replacing the `rev32` in/out muxes around the shared EX shifter with two plain shifters (`shr_res` SRL/SRA with `sh_arith` sign fill, `shl_res` SLL, one-hot `sel_shr`/`sel_shl` flops as two AND-OR legs, ~+100-130 LUT4) on top of the 3-entry skid FIFO scored 256.62 vs 261.43 for FIFO-3 alone (r12s0), i.e. ~104.9 MHz if cycles stayed at 4,089,085 (inferred, `make timing` not logged) against ~106.9, so removing a LUT level from group C (m1_alu_a -> forward mux -> shifter -> alu_result) bought no Fmax and the doubled mux tree plus 2x `shamt` fan-out probably cost slightly; with groups A (compare, r14s0), B (dmem -> ID, r6s0/r6s1/r12s1) and now C each having had a standalone cone rewrite that vanished into the ~2-3% seed spread, the three ~15 ns groups are tied closely enough that further single-cone trims in EX/ID are not worth running, and Fmax needs a structural change that moves all three at once (as the r9s1 regfile slicing did) or the lever should be cycles.

title: Shallow EX ALU cone: split left/right shifters (no bit-reversal muxes), carry-select adder, flat adder-last result select, plus 3-entry skid FIFO
motivation:
The champion (105.04 MHz, 4,128,299 cycles, 2.92M retired instr) is bounded by tied ~15 ns
arrival path groups. The latest logged post-fix worst paths repeatedly land in the EX ALU
cone, not in the compare/redirect cone: r14s0 (after the compare-last rewrite) is
u_id/m1_alu_a -> u_ex/u_alu -> reg_q.alu_result_15 (10 cells), r13s0 m1_alu_a ->
alu_result_27 (9 cells), r11s0 / r9s2 / r10s2 the same endpoint family, r14s1
alu_result_0 -> alu_result_10 (10 cells, i.e. the adder carry path). The only ALU
structure nobody has touched in 14 rounds is the shared right shifter: SLL is done by
bit-reversing the operand (`sh_left ? rev32(a) : a`), shifting right, and bit-reversing
the result (`sh_left ? rev32(r) : r`). That puts two full 2:1 mux levels in series with
the barrel (fwd-mux -> rev mux -> 3 LUT levels of barrel -> rev mux -> 2-level result
AND-OR, ~8-9 cells before routing), which is as deep as the whole 33-bit carry chain.
It was a pure area saving (one shifter instead of two) when LUTs mattered; the core now
uses 3.2K of ~20K LUT4 and area is not binding, while ~66% of path delay is routing.
The other limiter on the same cone is the 32-bit carry chain of `a + (b ^ sub) + sub`
feeding straight into the 9-term AND-OR result select. Previous rounds retimed
*around* this cone (forward-select flops, forward-into-ID, compare-last) and each
gained <= 1% because the ALU cone behind it then became the limiter; this hypothesis
shortens the cone itself and is cycle-exact.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make the EX ALU cone shallower with area we do not need to save, keeping every cycle
and every architectural behaviour identical (so riscv-formal, cosim and CRCs are
untouched), and bundle the already-measured FIFO-3 cycle win so the combined result can
clear the 4.6% bar:

1. Dedicated shifters (alu.sv alu_cand / ex_stage.sv): replace the reverse-shift-reverse
   structure with a left shifter `shl = a << shamt` and a right shifter
   `shr = $signed({sh_arith & a[31], a}) >>> shamt` (low 32 bits), both driven straight
   from the forward-mux output with shamt = alu_b[4:0]. No operand/result bit-reversal
   muxes: the barrel is fwd-mux -> 3 mux levels -> result select.
   core_pkg.sv ctrl_t: split `sel_shift` into `sel_shl` (SLL) and `sel_shr`
   (SRL/SRA); id_stage.sv decodes them from alu_op (sh_left / sh_arith flops stay for
   the SRA fill; sh_left is no longer needed by the datapath). ex_stage.sv ANDs the two
   shifter outputs with their own one-hot flops in the existing AND-OR (one OR term more,
   same number of LUT levels as before the shifter, two fewer in the shifter path).
   The `alu` op-encoded wrapper used by test_alu.py keeps its ports and results.
2. Carry-select main adder (alu_cand): split the 32-bit `a + (b ^ {32{sub}}) + sub`
   into a 16-bit low chain (carry-in = sub) and two 16-bit high chains (carry-in 0 and
   1) selected by the low chain's carry-out. The 33rd bit (`ltu` / SLT) is selected the
   same way. Carry chain length halves (the two high chains run in parallel with the
   low one); costs ~16-20 extra LUT/ALU cells and one mux level on bits 16..31 only.
   If `make timing` shows the adder is not the limiter (shifter-only worst path) the
   implementer may drop this item; it is separable and keeps behaviour identical.
3. Flat result select (ex_stage.sv): group the non-adder terms into one
   precombined `other_res` (and/or/xor/lui/pc4/slt/mdu AND-ORed by their flops) so the
   late arriving adder and shifter outputs each see exactly one AND + one OR level:
   `alu_result = (sel_add & add_res) | (sel_shl & shl) | (sel_shr & shr) | other_res`
   with the other_res cone starting at the same forward-mux output and finishing before
   the adder. Select flops stay one-hot flops from ID.
4. FIFO depth 3 (if_stage.sv): generalise the skid FIFO to 3 entries with thermometer
   valids and `accept = imem_ready && !redirect && !qv[2]` (flops + imem handshake
   only, decode source `qv[0] ? q_in[0] : imem_data` unchanged), exactly the build that
   measured 4,089,085 cycles (-0.95%) with Fmax 106.9 MHz (r12s0). Keep rs1/rs2
   for the regfile read and load-use compare on the raw head/live mux output.

Not touched: forward_unit / m1 flops / regfile / MEM stage / hazard unit / redirect
and BHT logic, the MDU, and the dmem -> ID bypass (do not stack changes there; r6s0,
r6s1, r9s0, r12s1, r14s1 all lost on them). Expected: cycles -0.95% from the FIFO
alone (measured); Fmax gain from the shallower EX cone (it is the post-fix worst
group in r9s2/r11s0/r13s0/r14s0), bounded by the tied dmem BSRAM -> ID/EX group at
~14.9 ns in r12s0, hence a modest but real +3..6% over the FIFO-3 baseline.
Implementation notes for the evaluator: after implementing, run `make timing
TARGET=bench` and log the worst-path start/end plus cycles separately; if the worst path
is still u_ex/u_alu, report its cell list (shifter vs adder) for the next round.
cocotb test_alu.py must still pass unchanged (op-encoded `alu` wrapper preserved,
including SLL/SRL/SRA with shamt 0..31 and SRA of negative values).

title: EX/MEM-filled taken-branch fold table (BTB that supplies the branch word) with formal-safe flop model and flop-only lookahead
motivation:
Direction/target predictor ideas are exhausted: bimodal-128 leaves ~54K mispredicts and a return stack
~13.7K rets, so a perfect conventional predictor is worth <=3.3% of cycles (r7s2, r9s2, r10s2, r13s0, r13s2
all landed inside place-and-route noise). The machine is FETCH-bound, not redirect-bound: bench_stall_gen
accepts imem in only 100/128 = 78% of cycles, the core retires ~2.93M instructions in 4.128M cycles
(fetch floor = 2.93M/0.78 = 3.76M), and the FIFO already hides dmem / load-use / MDU stalls behind that floor.
~11.6% of retired instructions (294K taken conditional branches + 49K JAL) spend one imem slot fetching a word
whose only job is to steer the PC to a target the BHT / JAL predecode already knew. A tiny BTB that stores the
branch WORD lets the imem slot fetch the TARGET in the same cycle (two words per slot), the only way to push
supply above 0.78 words/cycle. At 50-60% coverage that is ~170-200K slots x 1.28 cycles = 5-6% of cycles.
This is the same lever as r12s2 (Fmax 52 MHz: late lookup index pc_n = accept ? next_pc, second pc+imm adder,
imem_addr from an adder chain) and r14s2 (never timed: riscv-formal pc_fwd_ch0 hit the 2700 s cap because of the
64-entry async-read RAM array in the fetch path). This version fixes both recorded failure causes, and notes one
fact the earlier post-mortems missed: in the timed wrapper (fpga/core_bench_si.sv) io_imemData is the LFSR FLOP
and io_imemAddr only feeds the LED XOR, so there is no imem BSRAM clock-to-out in the timed fetch cone and no
address-setup endpoint; what costs Fmax is extra LUT levels / fan-out on pc, FIFO enables and the RAM
read -> compare -> hit cone, which is what this design keeps flop -> 1-2 LUTs -> flop.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add to rtl/if_stage.sv (plus a 1-flop pred_taken in EX/MEM and a fill bus in core.sv) a 64-entry direct-mapped
fold table and a fold path. Hard rules, each answering a recorded failure:

1. Table. 64 entries indexed by pc[7:2]; entry = {tag pc[19:8] (12b), word (32b), target[19:2] (18b)}; a separate
   64-flop valid vector (sync reset) because the data RAM has no reset. Data storage = explicit
   syn_ramstyle="distributed_ram" 16x4 slices (RAM16SDP4, same style as reg_file.sv; 4 groups x 15 slices).
   Exactness rule: an entry is written only if pc[31:20]==0 and target[31:20]==0 (checked at fill from flops), and a
   lookup only hits if the lookup address [31:20]==0, so tag compare is exact for the bounded 1 MiB memory map and a
   hit implies the stored word and target are exactly what EX would compute (EX verifies direction only and relies
   on the predicted target equalling its own pc+imm; an aliased wrong target would break pc_fwd, hence exactness).

2. Fill from EX/MEM FLOPS only (never imem_data / pred_target / FIFO D, lesson r11s2/r13s1): add ex_mem.pred_taken
   (one flop, copied from in.pred_taken). When ex_mem.valid && ex_mem.pred_taken (a JAL or a taken-predicted branch;
   JALR is never predicted) write table[ex_mem.pc[7:2]] <= {ex_mem.pc[19:8], ex_mem.instr, ex_mem.branch_target[19:2]}
   and set valid. All write data/enable are flops (branch_target is already an EX/MEM flop), so nothing new loads the
   EX adder / compare / redirect cone. Re-writing the same entry while the op sits in MEM is harmless.

3. Registered lookahead from flops + imem handshake only. Each cycle compute the address pc will hold NEXT cycle:
     base  = fold_eff ? {ft_q, 2'b00}[19:2] : pc[19:2]   (flop-selected mux)
     nidx  = redirect ? <no lookup, hit_d = 0>
           : (accept || fold_eff&&imem_ready) ? base + 1 : base   (one 18-bit incrementer on flops)
   read the RAM at nidx[5:0], compare tag with nidx[17:6], AND valid, AND (is_jal(word) || bht[nidx][1]) with the BHT
   bit read by the same flop-derived index (BHT array / update path unchanged), AND NOT (the word accepted this
   cycle is itself pred_hit, i.e. the next pc is the late next_pc: no lookup, coverage loss accepted, this is what
   killed r12s2). Register hit_q, fw_q (32b word), ft_q (18b target). The only late input into hit_q's D is that
   one AND with pred_hit; fw_q/ft_q come straight from the RAM output. No signal from imem_data reaches nidx.

4. Fold action. fold_eff = hit_q && !redirect && !qv[1] (all flops; fold needs room for 2 pushes in the depth-3 FIFO).
   In a fold cycle (pc == X): imem_addr = {ft_q} target T instead of pc (2:1 mux, flop select, both inputs flops, feeds only
   the output port); the branch word X is NOT fetched, it is pushed into the FIFO from fw_q with pc = X and
   pred_taken = 1; the imem word delivered this cycle is the TARGET word, pushed right behind it when imem_ready.
   Predecode (is_jal/is_br/imm) is unchanged; its base becomes (fold_eff ? T : pc) with T and the select both flops, so
   the single existing pc+imm adder is reused (no second adder). pc <= imem_ready ? next_pc(T word) : T. If the target
   word is not delivered the branch word is already banked and the PC just becomes T (fold is not repeated).
   In a fold cycle the live word is always banked and never decoded ahead of the banked branch word:
   word_avail = qv[0] || (imem_ready && !fold_eff), bank condition = stall_id || fold_eff, so ID sees a bubble when
   the FIFO was empty (decode idles ~22% of cycles anyway; the machine is fetch-bound). Decode source stays
   qv[0] ? q_in[0] : imem_data so the rs1/rs2 regfile read and load-use compare feed (the tied FIFO-head -> regfile ->
   ID/EX group) is untouched.

5. FIFO = depth 3 thermometer-valid FIFO (r12s0, -0.95% cycles, Fmax held); non-fold accept stays
   imem_ready && !redirect && !qv[2]; fold accept uses qv[1] but the select is the flop fold_eff, so accept is still
   flops + handshake. A registered EX/MEM redirect clears the FIFO and hit_q exactly as it clears qv today.

6. Everything downstream is unchanged: the folded word travels with pred_taken=1; EX verifies by the existing
   direction-only XOR and its own pc+imm target; a mispredicted fold redirects like any mispredict. No ID/EX, regfile,
   hazard (stall_id/flush_id logic), MDU, forward or mem change.

7. FORMAL (the r14s2 failure). Under `ifdef RISCV_FORMAL replace the RAM slices by a 4-entry FLOP array (index
   pc[3:2], tags pc[19:4], same ports/semantics, written by the same fill bus) so no memory array enters the SMT
   problem while the fold FIFO / bank / two-push logic is still exercised by the pc_fwd/unique/liveness/ill checks (the

lesson: - 2026-10-03 hyp-20261003-003-r15s2 (regression, -23.98%): The formal-safe rebuild of the r12s2/r14s2 fold table (64-entry `distributed_ram` `{tag, word, target}` filled from EX/MEM flops, lookup index from flops + handshake into `hit_q`/`fw_q`/`ft_q`, `fold_eff = hit_q && !redirect && !qv[1]`, `imem_addr`/predecode base `fold_eff ? T : pc`, two-push depth-3 FIFO, 4-entry flop model under `RISCV_FORMAL`) scored 193.44 vs 254.45, which at fitness = 10 x Fmax / (cycles/1e6) implies only ~75-79 MHz vs ~106.9 for FIFO-3 alone (r12s0, 4,089,085 cycles) even if cycles fell the hoped 5%, so a flop-only lookahead recovered about half of r12s2's loss (-47.87% -> -24%) but the fold datapath itself still costs ~25% Fmax against a lever worth at most ~5-6% of cycles (inferred: cycles, Fmax, fold count, formal result and the `make timing` worst path were not logged and there are no implementation notes; the likely residual is `fold_eff`/`hit_q` fanning into the FIFO push enables and `fw_q`-vs-`imem_data` data muxes, the `base_pc` mux ahead of the single predecode `pc + imm` adder -> `next_pc` -> `pc` loop, and `word_avail` -> `stall_id`); this is the third fold/branch-word-buffer attempt (r12s2, r14s2, r15s2) to fail on the fetch loop, so treat the 78%-imem-accept fetch-supply lever as closed unless a design leaves `imem_addr`, `next_pc`, the FIFO data muxes and `word_avail` structurally untouched and is first shown flop -> flop in `make timing`.
